92859.title: Infanteer (CAF)
92859.employer: The Cameron Highlanders of Ottawa (Duke of Edinburgh's Own)
92859.description: Infantry Soldiers are the Army's primary combat fighters and are responsible for closing with and engaging the enemy. They are the core members of the Combat Arms team, which includes Artillery and Armoured Soldiers. Infantry Soldiers are capable of operating anywhere in the world in any environment and in any combination of arms, including airmobile and amphibious operations. The primary duties of an Infantry Soldier are to: Expertly operate and maintain a wide range of weapons, including rifle, hand-grenades, light, medium and heavy machine-guns, and anti-tank weapons Use sophisticated equipment for field communications, navigation and night-vision surveillance Inspect and maintain weapon systems, vehicles, survival gear and personal defensive equipment Participate in airborne operations Operate with support elements such as fighter aircraft, tactical and artillery Engage in unarmed combat Employ camouflage and concealment, patrol, assault, defence, and escape-and-evasion tactics. Infantry Soldiers normally work outdoors. Both in training and on operations they live and work in conditions that would resemble those in the field. Infantry Soldiers will be posted to a battalion in Canada, but there are employment opportunities across Canada and on deployed operations around the world.
92859.requirements: To start a full or part-time career in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) you must: Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident Be at least 18 years old (17 years old with parental consent), except: For the Paid Education programs - you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) For the Primary Reserves-you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) and must be enrolled as a full-time student Have completed at least Grade 10 or 24 credits of Secondary IV in Quebec (some jobs need higher levels of education) If you have completed your education outside Canada, you must have your Educational Credential Assessments (ECAs) completed for your high school and highest level of education prior to submitting your application. For more information about eligibility requirements or the application process, please visit Joining the Forces . You can submit your application even if you are not sure about the job-specific requirements. Once we get your application, we'll work with you to determine if you qualify. If you have questions at any time throughout the process or you'd like to know which part-time jobs are available in your area, you can visit our Help Centre or Contact Us .

114909.title: VDC Mechanical Coordinator
114909.description: Job purpose The VDC Mechanical Coordinator, reporting to the VDC Manager, supports the preparation and coordination of mechanical design documents and BIM models, with a primary focus on HVAC systems and exposure to plumbing coordination. Working closely with Lar-Mex's project team, the VDC Mechanical Coordinator will assist in developing coordinated mechanical system models and drawings while receiving mentorship and hands-on training from experienced team members. This role offers valuable exposure to real-world project coordination and mechanical construction practices. Duties and responsibilities Job Duties: • Assist in interpreting plans and specifications to support the development of practical and efficient mechanical system designs. • Support the preparation of mechanical system drawings, BIM models, and coordination documents with guidance from the VDC team. • Assist in coordinating drawings and design information with Project Managers to ensure project requirements are met. • Participate in coordination meetings with internal project teams, consultants, and subcontractors. • Help identify and resolve design clashes and coordination issues within BIM models. • Work closely with project teams to support accurate and coordinated design documentation. • Assist in maintaining accurate models that align with project specifications and installation requirements. • Support the preparation of sleeving, layout, and pre-fabrication drawings for construction teams. • Participate in site visits to gain field exposure and assist with drawing verification. • Provide regular progress updates to the VDC Manager and seek guidance when required. • Support the VDC team in maintaining quality and consistency across project models. • Perform other duties as assigned to support project and team objectives. Qualifications Knowledge and Abilities: • Basic understanding of mechanical building systems, including HVAC; exposure to plumbing systems is considered an asset. • Familiarity with BIM software such as Revit and Navisworks through education, co-op placements, or project work. • General understanding of construction drawings and coordination processes. • Willingness to learn mechanical coordination practices and develop technical expertise through mentorship and hands-on experience.
114909.requirements: Required Skills: • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written. • Positive attitude and willingness to learn in a team-based environment. • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines. • Adaptability and willingness to take initiative when solving problems. • Ability to work collaboratively with project and field teams. Considered an Asset: • Co-op, internship, or project experience related to BIM, drafting, or mechanical systems. • Exposure to construction or mechanical contracting environments. • Understanding of mechanical assembly or installation methods. • Bilingual written and oral proficiency in English and French.

115470.title: Early Childhood Educator (ECE) - Montessori Classroom Assistant & Elementary Support
115470.description: Description Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is seeking an Early Childhood Educator to join our teaching team. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working with children across multiple age groups and appreciates the variety that comes with being part of a growing school. Working alongside experienced Montessori educators, the successful candidate will primarily support our Montessori Casa classrooms (ages 2.5 to 6 years), with opportunities to contribute to our lower elementary program and before and after school care, depending on qualifications, experience, and the needs of the school. Qualifications and experience in the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition (ISKCON) is an asset. The ideal candidate is charismatic, builds respectful relationships with children, has a natural ability to understand others' needs, is flexible and able to adapt to the needs of the program that come with working in a close-knit school community rather than that within a traditional school model. Responsibilities Responsibilities will vary based on qualifications and experience and may include: Support, create or implement a curriculum that promotes children's physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and practical life development. Lead or assist with the daily operation of a Montessori Casa classroom. Prepare and maintain a safe, organized, and engaging learning environment using Montessori principles and incorporating values of the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition. Observe children's interests, behaviour, and developmental progress, maintaining accurate records and documentation. Assess children's abilities and discuss observations and progress with families and colleagues. Support children's independence, concentration, confidence, and positive social interactions through respectful guidance. Guide children in developing practical life skills, self-care routines, conflict resolution, and self-regulation. Lead or participate in activities including storytelling, music, art, outdoor learning, movement Support lower elementary students with classroom routines and learning activities, where appropriate. Plan and organize activities for school-age children attending our before and after school program. Assist children with eating, dressing, toileting, diapering, handwashing, rest periods, and other daily care routines as needed. Prepare snacks and assist with meal routines. Maintain classroom materials, equipment, and learning resources. Ensure the health, safety, and well-being of all children while following licensing requirements and school policies. Communicate professionally with parents regarding children's daily experiences and developmental progress. Participate in staff meetings, collaborative planning, and ongoing professional development. About Our School Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is an independent multi-age Montessori school located in Russell, Ontario. We currently operate three licensed Montessori Casa classrooms for children aged 2.5-6 years, offer before and after school care for neighbouring schools, and provide a multi-age elementary program. We have been operating for 10 years and continue to place an emphasis and value on genuine relationships. We believe in a holistic education model, nurturing mind, body and soul. The outstanding characters of the educators will be what shapes the character development of the children in their classrooms, and therefore we are looking for a unique individual to imbibe the teachings of bhakti and the qualities of a vaishnava. Educators have opportunities to contribute beyond a single classroom, share their individual strengths, and continue developing professionally as our programs evolve. Why Join Us? We're looking for someone who is seeking more than simply a job. We encourage initiative, offer regular professional development opportunities through our educational network, and provide the chance to take on increased responsibilities as our school continues to develop. If you're looking for a unique work environment, where relationships matter, and every day brings something a little different, we warmly invite your application.
115470.requirements: Qualifications Early Childhood Education Diploma (ECE) and registration (or eligibility for registration) with the College of Early Childhood Educators, or Montessori Certification, Teacher's Diploma, or Bachelor's Degree in Education with relevant experience Experience working within a school aligned with the bhakti tradition, including the ability to lead and teach daily mantra meditation and the study of vedic texts such as the Srimad Bhagavatam and Bhagavad-Gita Experience working with children Assets Experience working in a Montessori classroom Knowledge of Montessori pedagogy Knowledge of Vedic philosophy Experience volunteering/working in an ISKCON environment. Knowledge of Vaisnava culture; familiarity of its activities and operations Experience working with children across multiple age groups Ability to storytell, play and teach musical instruments, drama and visual arts Requirements CPR & First Aid (Level C) Vulnerable Sector Police Record Check Up-to-date immunizations (or valid exemption) Reliable transportation (public transportation to our location is limited) Job Type : Full-time Benefits Dental care Extended health care Paid time off Discounted or free meals Ability to Commute/Relocate Russell, ON K4R 1B8: Reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (required) Work Location : In person

115496.title: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME)
115496.division: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC)
115496.description: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME) Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC)/ Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) Student Procurement Officer Finance and Awards Administration Division National Capital Region NSERC and SSHRC are looking for a part-time student (15 to 22.5 hours per week) to support our Procurement and Contracting team. We are seeking a motivated, action-oriented team player who is interested in supporting a dynamic procurement environment and eager to develop new skills. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience while contributing to a collaborative and fast-paced team. Who we Are The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) funds visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will benefit our country. We are Canada's largest supporter of discovery and innovation. We work with universities, colleges, businesses and not-for-profits to remove barriers, develop opportunities and attract new expertise to make Canada's research community thrive. We give Canadian scientists and engineers the means to go further because we believe in research without borders and beyond frontiers. The Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) is the federal research funding agency that promotes and supports research and research training in the humanities and social sciences. Through its Talent, Insight and Connection programs, and through partnerships and collaborations, SSHRC strategically supports world-leading initiatives that reflect a commitment to ensuring a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC also oversees the delivery of a number of tri-agency programs, including the Canada Research Chairs and other research chairs programs, and the New Frontiers in Research Fund , which supports international, interdisciplinary, fast-breaking and high-risk research. Description of Duties Reporting to a Senior Procurement Advisor for the Procurement and Contracting group, the position provides contracting and procurement advice and services to Cost Centre (CC) Managers and Project Authorities (PAs) by planning and delivering the procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 for goods and below $40,000 for services) for low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services. This includes requirements such as call-ups against standing offers, low dollar value purchase orders; and requirements which fall under Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Shared Services Canada (SSC) for mandatory procurement instruments, including IT requirements. Responsibilities: Analyze client requirements, specification and requisition documents, review the adequacy of statements of work/ statements of requirements in order to plan and deliver procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 goods, $40,000 services) and low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services.
115496.requirements: Essential Qualifications Requirement: - must be returning to school in Winter term Official Language English essential Education Enrollment in a Supply Chain and Operations Management program (or equivalent) Experience Experience in a client service environment; Experience using Microsoft Office; Experience reviewing documentation; and Experience providing administrative support services Abilities Ability to plan/organize and address priorities Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing Ability to evaluate problems and suggest effective solutions Ability to analyze proposals and contractual documents Ability to work under pressure and with conflicting demands Ability to provide advice and guidance to clients Personal Suitabilities Strong interpersonal skills Client service orientation Results orientation Team-oriented Adaptable to ongoing change Autonomy, flexibility, accuracy, initiative and judgment Asset Qualifications Experience working in a procurement/financial system (such as SAP) Bilingual - Proficiency in both official languages Conditions of Employment • Adherence to the NSERC Code of Conduct; • Adherence to the NSERC Conflict of Interest and Post-Employment Policy; • Compliance with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector; • Legal status to accept employment for the entire period of employment; and • Reliability security clearance Work Location Hybrid between telework and Zibi Building (125 Zaida Eddy Private, 5th floor, Ottawa ON) Should you be interested in this opportunity, please apply and submit your resume and cover letter through the Algonquin College HireAC portal. Your covering letter should clearly state why you would like this opportunity and how you meet the qualifications. We recommend using each of the experience factors as headers and provide clear and concrete examples and details of where, when and how you obtained the experience. For example, for each essential experience requirement, you should list where you gained the experience, your title at the time, a description of the tasks you performed relevant to the experience factor, and your accomplishments. We thank all those who apply. Only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. Security Clearance: Reliability status

115549.title: Respiratory Therapist, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) - BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre
115549.description: Respiratory Therapist, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre Vancouver, BC Advance Your Career in Neonatal Intensive Care at BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre **Relocation expenses up to $5,000 available for qualified candidates! Are you passionate about making a profound difference in the lives of newborns and their families? Join the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre - a world leader in specialized neonatal care and the sole provincial quaternary referral centre serving British Columbia and the Yukon. Here, you'll develop a specialized expertise in neonatal care and transport, caring for both fragile newborns and their mothers. Our unique family-centered design features 70 single-family rooms that keep mothers, newborns, and families together-because healing happens best when families are united. As a key member of our multidisciplinary team, you'll collaborate closely with nurses and physicians to deliver exceptional care. You'll be part of a dedicated resuscitation team for high-risk deliveries and urgent neonatal care scenarios, making life-saving impacts every day. Our NICU Respiratory Therapists also lead the way in neonatal transport, working alongside BC Emergency Health Services and BC Ambulance Services to provide critical respiratory support during transfers - a unique and highly valued role. At BCW NICU, education is embedded into your daily schedule, with integrated multidisciplinary learning opportunities designed to advance your skills and professional growth. You'll also have the rewarding opportunity to teach families how to care for their newborns confidently at home, making a difference that extends beyond the hospital walls. If you're ready to join a cutting-edge, supportive environment where innovation, compassion, and family-centered care come first, the NICU at BC Women's Hospital is the perfect place to grow your career. Watch this video to better envision your dream career in the NICU at BC Women's Hospital What you'll do Review patient's medical history, conduct assessments of the patient's pathophysical condition, recommend appropriate care and document patient response and outcomes. Set up, checks, perform specified quality control procedures and operate respiratory equipment, making adjustments as appropriate. Initiate, monitor and assess ventilator dependent patients as per care protocols and daily care. Recommend and administer individualized medical gas therapies. Provide invasive and non-invasive cardio-pulmonary monitoring. Evaluate patient's responses during testing, therapies and related treatments; make changes as appropriate; observe and record data on patient chart. Respond to cardiac arrests and other emergency calls. Prepare reports, statistical information and summaries of research activities as required. Attend departmental and program meetings to provide or exchange information. Participate in departmental, program and health centre committees. Participate in the education and mentoring of students, staff members, physicians and other health care professionals. Perform other related duties as assigned. What you bring Qualifications Graduate of an accredited school of Respiratory Therapy and successful completion of the Canadian Board of Respiratory Care examination. Current and continuing registration with British Society of Respiratory Therapists (BCSRT) and the Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapists (CSRT). Current Basic Life Support certification. Current Neonatal Resuscitation Program certification. 115551.description: Anesthesia Assistant, Anaesthesia Tech Services BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre Vancouver, BC What you'll do Sets up, tests, calibrates, operates and monitors equipment for regular use including anesthetic machines, breathing circuits, ventilators, scavenging devices, intubation equipment, fiberoptic bronchoscopes, monitoring equipment, infusion devices and blood gas machines. As a rapidly expanding business, we want you to join our team and grow with us, and we can build you up from store manager to regional manager and beyond! 115784.description: Description: Respiratory therapists evaluate, treat and manage patients of all ages with respiratory illnesses and other cardiopulmonary disorders in a wide variety of clinical settings. Respiratory therapists must demonstrate behavior and ethics that are consistent with the standards and ethics of all health care professionals. In addition to performing respiratory therapy procedures, Respiratory Therapists are involved in clinical decision making (such as patient evaluation, treatment selection and assessment of treatment efficacy) and patient education. Respiratory Therapists report directly to the Director of Respiratory Services. RRTs, as part of the Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA), work in hospital, clinical care and community care settings as part of a multidisciplinary health-care team in order to provide the best patient care. Hospital settings include Intensive Care Units (ICU), Neonatal ICU, Pediatric ICU, Emergency Departments, Critical Care Units, and other hospital wards. Community Care Settings include Home Oxygen Suppliers. RRTs work in shifts in order to provide health-care coverage based on the needs of the facility or clinic and this may include days, nights, and weekends. Opportunities to grow as a RRT include taking advanced courses to work in specialized areas and pursuing management and leadership positions. Pay, Incentives and Benefits: Wages: $38.64 - $47.14 /hr May be eligible for Recruitment Incentive up to $30,000 and Relocation up to $3,000 In addition to the above pay bands, the SHA provides a comprehensive benefits package including: Extended Health and Dental benefits Defined-Benefit Pension Plan Life and Disability Insurance Employee and Family Assistance Program Annual Vacation The Saskatchewan Health Authority is currently offering hiring incentives up to $30,000 plus relocation assistance of $3,000 may be available.

115927.title: Veterinary Technician
115927.description: Join Our Team at Brockville Animal Hospital! Are you seeking a place that truly respects your professional journey, champions your growth, and values the balance between work and life? Brockville Animal Hospital, a thriving small-animal practice located in the heart of Ontario's stunning Thousand Islands region. We are looking for Veterinary Technicians to join our team and make a meaningful impact on pet healthcare while enjoying a long-term, fulfilling career with us. We are seeking a Veterinary Technician to join our professional veterinary team for an open current position within our privately owned and locally operated veterinary hospital in Brockville, Ontario. As the longest established and one of the only independent practices in the area, we are committed to providing high standards of medical care, fostering strong client relationships, and maintaining a collaborative clinical environment. The successful candidate will demonstrate professionalism, technical competence, and a strong commitment to patient care. This role requires the ability to work effectively within a team, support veterinarians in clinical procedures, and contribute to efficient daily operations while upholding regulatory and ethical standards of the profession. Why Choose Brockville Animal Hospital? Located along the beautiful St. Lawrence River, our practice is surrounded by the natural beauty and recreational opportunities of the Thousand Islands. This picturesque setting offers a perfect backdrop for maintaining that ideal work-life balance. Brockville's welcoming, friendly community is known for its relaxed pace, with no rush-hour traffic and easy access to outdoor activities such as camping, boating, river cruises, scuba diving, sports teams, and scenic parks. What Sets Us Apart? Not Corporate: We are a veterinarian-owned, community-centered practice that thrives on collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. Supportive Leadership: Our dedicated veterinarians work side-by-side with our team, offering hands-on leadership and mentorship that fosters personal and professional growth. Advanced Care: Our hospital offers a broad range of intensive diagnostics and procedures, including dentistry, surgeries, and treatments. Efficient Workflow: We've mobilized our Registered Veterinary Technicians to elevate patient care and efficiency. With VetWise, our after-hour emergency system, you can count on excellent client support while protecting your downtime and work-life balance. Cutting-Edge Technology: Our Co.Vet system streamlines medical records, saving you time so you can focus on providing quality care and getting home on time. Team-Centric Mentorship and Growth At Brockville Animal Hospital, we foster a close-knit, supportive environment. Weekly staff meetings and dedicated mentorship for new graduates ensure every team member feels empowered, supported, and engaged in their career development. Position: Veterinary Technician Hospital: Brockville Animal Hospital Location: Brockville, Ontario Job Type: Full-time Employment 35-40 hours/week What We Offer Wage rate commensurate with skillset & experience: $23.00/hr - $35.00/hr On-call shift premiums We offer a comprehensive health benefits package, including 50% of Medical, Dental, and Vision premiums covered by BAH. Employer contributions increase by 5% annually, ultimately reaching 100% coverage. Opportunities for professional development and continuing education (CE) Generous discounts on veterinary services and products Annual uniform allowance plus 6 scrub tops supplied at the start of your employment Supportive, respectful, and team-oriented workplace culture We prioritize work-life balance and are committed to equitable scheduling. Our rotation includes shared evenings and weekends, with a day off provided in lieu for every other Saturday worked.
115927.requirements: Key Responsibilities Provide high-quality care to hospitalized and surgical patients Assist veterinarians during examinations, procedures, and surgeries Perform anesthesia induction, monitoring, and recovery Accurately prepare, and administer medications and vaccines Collect and process laboratory samples (blood, urine, feces, cytology) Take and process diagnostic imaging (radiographs) Maintain detailed and accurate medical records Educate clients on preventive care, treatment plans, and post-operative instructions Maintain a clean, safe, and organized clinical environment Follow all clinic protocols, health & safety standards, confidentiality, and regulatory requirements Qualifications & Requirements Ability to work collaboratively in a team-based environment Strong communication and client service skills Excellent organizational and multitasking abilities Compassionate, calm, and professional demeanor Ability to lift and restrain animals safely Experience in general practice / surgery / dentistry / anesthesia considered an asset Completion of the OAVT Professionalism & Ethics Workshop and planning to write the Veterinary Technician National Examination (VTNE) is an asset

115937.title: Personal Support Worker
115937.description: The Personal Support Worker provides direct support to individuals with developmental disabilities, dual diagnoses, autism spectrum disorder, acquired brain injuries, or mental health challenges who require specialized behavioural supports. The Support Worker promotes independence, dignity, safety, and quality of life by implementing Behaviour Support Plans (BSPs), teaching positive coping strategies, and supporting individuals in achieving their personal goals. Key Responsibilities Behavioural Support Implement individualized Behaviour Support Plans (BSPs) as developed by the clinical team. Utilize evidence-based positive behaviour support strategies. Monitor, document, and report behavioural observations, incidents, and progress. Recognize triggers and early warning signs and implement proactive intervention strategies. Use approved de-escalation techniques while maintaining the safety of residents and staff. Participate in behavioural data collection and tracking. Support crisis interventions in accordance with organizational policies. Direct Resident Support Assist individuals with activities of daily living (ADLs) including personal hygiene, dressing, toileting, and meal preparation as required. Promote independence and skill development. Support community participation, recreation, employment, and volunteer activities. Foster meaningful relationships while maintaining professional boundaries. Encourage choice, inclusion, and person-centred planning. Health & Safety Administer medications as delegated and trained. Follow all medication administration policies and documentation requirements. Respond appropriately to medical emergencies and behavioural crises. Follow infection prevention and control procedures. Complete incident reports and serious occurrence documentation when required. Ensure a safe and clean living environment. Documentation Complete shift notes and communication logs accurately. Record behavioural data and complete ABC charts as required. Document interventions and outcomes objectively. Communicate significant changes to supervisors and the interdisciplinary team. Team Collaboration Participate in team meetings, case conferences, and training. Collaborate with Behaviour Therapists, Social Workers, families, healthcare professionals, and community partners. Provide mentorship and guidance to new staff regarding Behaviour Support Plans. Maintain confidentiality in accordance with organizational policies and legislation. Knowledge & Skills Strong understanding of Positive Behaviour Support principles. Experience implementing Behaviour Support Plans. Knowledge of Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA) principles is considered an asset. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Strong conflict resolution and crisis intervention abilities. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Excellent organizational and time management skills. Ability to maintain professionalism in high-stress situations. Physical Requirements Ability to safely assist with transfers and mobility. Ability to stand, walk, bend, lift, and provide physical support throughout the shift. Ability to respond quickly during behavioural or medical emergencies. Working Conditions Days, evenings, weekends, holidays, and overnight shifts as required. Work in residential homes and community settings. Exposure to challenging behaviours, medical needs, and crisis situations. May be required to work independently or as part of a team. Core Competencies Person-Centred Support Positive Behaviour Support Professionalism Compassion and Empathy Crisis Prevention and Intervention Teamwork Communication Accountability Problem Solving Adaptability Respect and Inclusion Expectations Employees are expected to: Treat all individuals with dignity, respect, and compassion. Follow all organizational policies, Behaviour Support Plans, and health and safety procedures. Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Attend mandatory training and maintain required certifications. Contribute to a positive, respectful, and collaborative workplace culture. Hours of Work: Thurs 2pm-9pm Fri 2pm-9pm Saturday 7am-2pm Some Sundays to meet staffing requirements. This job description is intended to outline the general duties and responsibilities of the Personal Support Worker position and may be amended as operational requirements evolve.
115937.requirements: Qualifications Required Minimum one year experience supporting individuals with complex behavioural needs (preferred). Valid Standard First Aid and CPR-C. Current Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening. Valid Class G Driver's Licence with a clean driver's abstract. Reliable transportation.

115942.description: Join a chef-led artisan bakery focused on craftmanship, fermentation, and great taste. Typically a four on then five off schedule Shift times/Hours of work: 06:50 to 19:17 and 19:17 to 06:50 What we offer: We are a B.C. top employer and offer welcoming workplaces with a range of benefits and policies to support you at every stage of your career. • Competitive pay with recognition of previous experience • Employer-paid benefits, including extended health, dental, and a municipal pension plan • Relocation assistance for eligible positions • Four weeks vacation with one year of continuous service • Education and career development opportunities • Mentorship programs for new graduates and internationally educated professionals • Employee and family assistance program, plus exclusive employee discounts About the role: In this role, you will provide respiratory care in alignment with Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapists (CSRT) standards and a client- and family-centered care model. You will work both independently and collaboratively to support clients with a range of acute and chronic cardio-respiratory conditions. This position involves consulting with other healthcare professionals, contributing to quality improvement, and applying best practices in respiratory therapy. You will also maintain and advance your clinical skills and may participate in committees, team initiatives, and approved research projects. About us: We are committed to achieving a culturally diverse and inclusive workforce that is representative of the communities we serve, and where you are encouraged to bring your whole self to work. Well-being and work-life balance are promoted within the team, and our commitment to environmental sustainability supports our primary goal of increasing the health and well-being of everybody in our region. 115944.title: Cardiology Technologist
115944.description: We are seeking a Permanent Part Time Cardiology Technologist at Vernon Jubilee Hospital in Vernon, BC. Days of work: Rotating, Days Shift times: 08:00 to 16:30 What we offer: • Employee & Family Assistance Program • Employer paid training/education opportunities • Employer paid vacation • Extended health & dental coverage • May be eligible for Municipal Pension Plan • Work-life balance A Relocation Allowance package may be offered with the position. Applicable positions may qualify for up to $15,000 as a recruitment incentive. What will you work on? The Cardiology Technologist performs techniques relating to Electro Cardiogram (ECG) testing, stress testing, Holter and event Recorders and pacemaker monitoring and other types of diagnostic cardiac equipment. • Explains procedures to prepare patients for testing such as ECG, stress testing, Holter monitoring, pacemaker monitoring, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and related tests and answers related questions. • Performs a variety of non-invasive examinations such as ECG, stress testing and Holter and event monitoring and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring by attaching electrodes to the patient, operating equipment, analyzing and recording relevant data for interpretation by cardiologist and/or internist. • Explains cardiac pacemaker screen system to patients, monitors cardiac pacemakers and notifies cardiologist and/or internist of abnormalities; contacts patients by telephone for repeat recordings as required. • Monitors patients and scans test strips during cardiograms and stress tests and takes appropriate action upon recognition of cardiac arrhythmias or other abnormalities in accordance with established policies and procedures. • Scans and analyzes ECG, stress, Holter and event monitor, and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring test strips. Selects and assesses appropriate portions of test strips and summarizes for interpretation by medical staff in accordance with established policies and procedures. • Transfers and assigns ECGs in ECG Cardiology Management systems (i.e. Tracemaster) for interpretation by medical staff. • Demonstrates ECG testing procedures and operation of related equipment as required. • Monitors ongoing departmental activity levels and assists fellow staff to meet requests for service. • Maintains statistics and files completed reports. • Maintains equipment by cleaning, lubricating and replacing items such as paper rolls, electrodes, and leads. • Participates in Quality Management and/or Quality Assurance programs (including LEAN projects/initiatives) by providing information and input to Manager (or designate) • Participates in the instruction/orientation of staff and/or students by assisting with departmental orientations, in-service presentations, demonstrating procedures and answering questions, as required. • Maintains and updates own clinical knowledge within area of practice. • Performs other related duties as assigned. Where are we located? Vernon is where lakeside charm, local legends, and adventure collide. With 301 days of sunshine, pristine lakes, endless forests, and a trail system that's earned us the title of Trails Capital of BC, it's an outdoor lover's paradise. But that's not all-Vernon is a place of vibrant community, fertile vineyards, and fascinating people, always ready for fun, inspiration, or a good story. Whether you're hiking, biking, or simply soaking in the beauty, there's no shortage of unforgettable moments here. 115949.title: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSOCIATE, NATIONAL CREATION FUND AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
115949.description: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSOCIATE, NATIONAL CREATION FUND AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT Competition number: J0826-0306 Department: National Creation Fund and Professional Development Status: Full-Time Term (end date: August 31, 2028) Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (35 hours per week) Annual/hourly salary: $65,000 - $81,200 (position with benefits and pension plan) Closing date: September 20th, 2026 Anticipated start date: as soon as possible Introducing the National Arts Centre The National Arts Centre (NAC) is Canada's bilingual, multi-disciplinary home for the performing arts. The NAC presents, creates, produces, and co-produces performing arts programming in various streams - the NAC Orchestra, Dance, English Theatre, French Theatre, Indigenous Theatre, and Popular Music and Variety - and nurtures the next generation of audiences and artists from across Canada. The NAC is located in the National Capital Region on the unceded territory of the Anishinabe Algonquin Nation. At the National Arts Centre, we believe the performing arts are vital to the human experience. A house of dreams for the Canadian performing arts, we work with artists and arts organizations from across this land to revitalize our sector. Curious to learn more? Read our 2023-2026 Strategic Plan, The Journey Ahead . Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Anti-Racism and Accessibility We are on a journey, committed to ensuring that equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, anti-racism and reconciliation with Indigenous peoples will guide our actions. The NAC welcomes applications from?candidates who can help us meet our vision, and contribute to the diversity of?lived experiences, perspectives, and approaches.?When you join the NAC, you will be part of an inclusive?community working hard to dismantle barriers to employees'?well-being, access, potential, and success. The NAC actively seeks candidates who identify as women, Indigenous, Black, Persons of Colour (IBPoC), members of 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, and people?with disabilities. We encourage you to self-identify in the recruitment process. About the National Creation Fund and Professional Development The National Arts Centre's National Creation Fund is dedicated to the alchemy of artistic creation and driven by a conviction in the power of creation as a means of evolving culture, sparking innovation, and shaping our world. The Fund champions creation through transformative investments in the development of bold new music, dance, theatre and interdisciplinary performances, and through our work as a home for research and experimentation on the conditions required to create ambitious work. The NAC Professional Development team produces high-impact programs for artists and arts professionals, including apprenticeships, mentorships, and intensives. Designed for early- and mid-career artists, producers, designers, technicians and administrators from across Canada, participants have the opportunity to expand their networks, increase access to projects and roles of greater scope and scale, and expand, deepen and refine their arts and leadership practice. Key activities: Under the direction of the Artistic Producer, National Creation Fund, the Administrative Associate is the administrative backbone of the National Creation Fund and Professional Development teams, providing administrative, operational, and logistical support to both teams. This role provides high-level administrative and operational support across both departments, playing a pivotal role in the National Creation Fund's submission and investment processes and the planning and execution of Professional Development's suite of residencies, gatherings, and apprenticeships. Working closely with members of the Creation Fund and Professional Development teams, the Administrative Associate helps ensure both departments run smoothly and effectively, offering our communities and partners a meaningful experience. The incumbent is a key administrative resource, supporting multiple areas while maintaining strong attention to detail, positive relationships, and organizational effectiveness. Working closely with department leadership and team members, the Administrative Associate serves as a trusted partner in planning, problem-solving, and implementing priorities while ensuring operational excellence. Department Operations and Administration Respond to inquiries from artists, participants, partners, and arts organizations; Maintain the flow of the Fund's submission process by coordinating with our curatorial teams, booking meetings, circulating prep material, identifying and securing access support and interpretation, to ensure curatorial decisions are made and shared in a timely manner; Establish and maintain digital document management systems, electronic filing systems, databases, templates, and administrative records; Track, organize, and maintain department files, applications, submissions, agreements, reports, and supporting documentation; Assist with the administration and drafting of agreements and reporting; Prepare correspondence, meeting materials, agendas, presentations, reports, and briefing documents; Coordinate translation requests and assist with the preparation of bilingual materials; Identify and book access support measures as needed; Support the management of the Fund's National Advisory Committee, including booking meetings, organizing and executing meeting logistics, preparing and circulating advance materials, and onboarding new members; Schedule departmental meetings, maintain weekly meeting records and departmental Outlook Calendar; Recommend and implement administrative improvements that may enhance efficiency, organization, or experience; Support departmental financial administration, including expense claims, procurement forms, purchase requests, credit card reports, recurring payments, and payment documentation; Manage invoices and process payments, and ensure timely payments due under various contracts; Act as principal departmental liaison with NAC Finance Department for administration matters; Maintain and update the contact list and manage invite and RSVP lists for performances, as well as ticket allocation and distribution. 115951.title: Firearms Officer B/L
115951.description: The Ministry of the Solicitor General, Ontario Provincial Police, and the Chief Firearms Office are seeking a qualified individual to join our Licensing Unit. In this exciting, rewarding and challenging opportunity, you will be responsible for processing firearms license applications and to providing firearms licensing support and related services to the public and to Municipal, Provincial and Federal Agencies. Please note: The successful candidate will be expected to work out of the Ottawa or Sudbury work location, five (5) days a week. About Us: The Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) is one of North America's largest deployed police services with more than 6,400 uniformed officers, 2,900 civilian employees and 530 Auxiliary officers. We provide essential services that ensure the safety and security of the people of the Province of Ontario. The OPP is a division of the Ministry of the Solicitor General, the largest operational ministry in the province with a presence in every community across Ontario. We are the largest police service in Ontario and the second largest in Canada. The mandate of the Chief Firearms Office (CFO) is to protect public safety through the administration of the licensing provisions of the Firearms Act and Regulations. The Chief Firearms Officer for the Province of Ontario is delegated authority under the Act by the Minister of the Solicitor General, and is responsible for the administration and delivery of these key components of the Firearms Act. The OPP Values promote always doing the right things for the right reasons, by: Serving with PRIDE, PROFESSIONALISM and HONOUR. Interacting with RESPECT, COMPASSION and FAIRNESS. Leading with INTEGRITY, HONESTY and COURAGE. About the job Do you have the ability to deliver high?volume operational and administrative support in a dynamic environment, managing confidential information across multiple systems, responding to inquiries, and promoting firearms licensing through public outreach and education? In this exciting position you will process and assess firearms licence applications, transfers, and authorizations, by conducting detailed screenings, database reviews, and eligibility decisions to protect public safety. Additionally, you will act as a critical point of contact for the public, law enforcement, and justice partners, conducting interviews, responding to safety concerns, providing expert guidance on the Firearms Act, and supporting investigations and court processes.
115951.requirements: What you bring to the team Mandatory: Ability to pass an OPP background/ security investigation. Oral and written French Language skills at the advanced level Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Working knowledge of federal and provincial FOI requirements to ensure appropriate information sharing, along with strong understanding of the firearms licensing program to clearly explain eligibility and accurately direct inquiries. Proficiency with office and operational systems (e.g., Word, Excel, Outlook, CFIS, RMS, CPIC, Cognos) to accurately process applications, manage data entry, track application status, generate reports, and maintain organized records, along with effective use of standard office equipment. Interpersonal and Communication Skills You possess strong written, oral, listening, and interpersonal communication skills to prepare correspondence, respond to inquiries, provide clear and accurate information on the firearms licensing program, and collaborate effectively with internal teams and external partners. You are experienced in demonstrating tact, sensitivity, and professionalism when dealing with distressed, emotional, or irate individuals, and when communicating with ex?spouses, police services, and courts regarding licence?related matters. Problem Solving Skills You possess strong analytical and problem?solving skills to assess applicant eligibility, identify appropriate information sources and systems, conduct searches, verify documentation accuracy, and compile information for operational and court purposes. You possess effective decision?making and troubleshooting abilities to manage inquiries, resolve application or report discrepancies, address routine equipment or system issues, and determine when matters require escalation to supervisors or external agencies. Judgement and Discretion You have the ability to apply established firearms?licensing procedures and FOI guidelines to evaluate applications, make approval/refusal/referral decisions within authority, exercise discretion in information sharing, and escalate non?standard matters appropriately. You are able to manage and prioritize a high?volume, fast?paced workload by planning daily tasks, responding to changing demands, resolving client issues, and maintaining accuracy under frequent interruptions and competing priorities. You are proficient at communicating professionally and effectively in all interactions, preparing and editing documents and presentations, and exercising tact, diplomacy, and sound judgment when dealing with applicants, ex?spouses, law enforcement, and courts. How to Apply You can submit your application by visiting the OPS Careers Website and enter job ID 248755 Don't meet every qualification? If you are excited about this position and meet most, but not all, of the listed qualifications, please still consider applying. We recognize that no one person might have every qualification in this job ad, and you just might be the right candidate!

116034.title: Supervisor, Operations
116034.description: Reporting to the Manager, Shift Operations, Custodial Support Services (Manager), the Supervisor, Operations (Supervisor) is a member of the Custodial Support Services (CSS) leadership team. The Supervisor works closely and collaboratively with the Manager to direct custodial activities in order to implement the published Service Level Standards (SLS) as it pertains to the respective shift. The client-centric Supervisor engages with frontline custodial staff through formal and informal discussions relating to scope of work execution and performance. Accountable to validate the SLS by completing quality assurance (QA) audits, the Supervisor is responsible for engaging with frontline custodial staff to remove roadblocks preventing them from executing their work. The Supervisor works collaboratively with the Manager, to initiate the performance improvement process to correct behaviour and address audit issues as required. The Supervisor also participates in the recruitment process and in collaboration with the Manager, is responsible for the hands-on orientation of new staff ensuring that custodial staff are trained and comply with all university, Facilities, and CSS' health and safety policies and procedures and ensures staff competency in the safe use and maintenance of equipment. The Supervisor is expected to be knowledgeable of a variety of cleaning products, chemicals, tools and equipment, to stay current with industry trends, and to make suggestions for increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of custodial support services. The Supervisor works an assigned shift; however, must also be available to work flexible hours as required, including weekends. In addition, the Supervisor is on a rotating call-in list for emergency calls from the Emergency Response Centre. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Plan, execute and manage frequency based quality control audits each shift to ensure SLS targets are achieved, with the intention of getting through all spaces on campus on a determined frequency. • Collaborate with the Managers to provide consistent, decisive leadership for all custodial staff. • Manage, train, coach, and mentor custodial staff to ensure assigned facilities are cleaned in compliance with the SLS. • Connect with custodial staff in the field on a routine basis to, among other reasons, engage in conversations regarding work requirements, health and safety related issues impacting their scope of work, performance management, and to reinforce the importance of the work performed. • Escalate issues of poor performance or poor audit outcomes, building users concerns, staffing challenges and training requirements to the Manager for support as needed, if no support is required, provide a debrief to the Manager. • Working with the Manager, train and monitor custodial staff on the safe and proper operation of all cleaning products and equipment ensuring that items requiring repair or maintenance, are addressed in a timely manner. • Ensure that custodial staff properly clean equipment each shift and that equipment, supplies and tools are properly replaced, re-stocked, and secured at the end of the shift. • Complete requests for supplies and equipment, in order to have adequate inventory levels in compliance with the CSS Procurement Policy. • Communicate and work collaboratively with the Manager to ensure alignment relating to operational conditions that arise. • Ensure that university supplied workwear and staff identification is prominently worn by all custodial staff while on shift; ensure that all custodial staff wear safety footwear. • Working in alignment with the Manager, manage the client service relationships within assigned facilities as required. • Assist in the development, coordination and delivery of training programs. • Participate in mandatory engagement town hall meetings and ensure that all custodial staff are in attendance. • Remain current with industry standards and systems related to custodial services. • Deliver messaging and paperwork to key press locations in order to keep custodial staff informed of operational updates, processes, policies, etc. • Support or assist with leading other CSS initiatives as assigned. • Plan, prioritize and manage the work of employees, providing strategic and tactical advice, guidance and coaching. Identify the need for staff resources, participate on staffing committees, and make effective recommendations regarding employee selection. • Manage performance by establishing performance standards, reviewing and evaluating performance and conducting formal performance reviews on an ongoing basis. • Assess staff training and development needs, and ensure that employees receive training required to improve and sustain successful performance. • Investigate, address and resolve employee/labour relations issues, including disciplinary matters. Make decisions or effective recommendations on matters involving possible discipline, discharge and probationary termination. • Foster a productive and harmonious workplace through the promotion of a positive, inclusive teamwork environment, which recognizes the value of all CSS employees. SPECIAL SKILLS: • Proficiency with computers, Internet, and Microsoft Office Applications software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), databases, and custodial services related software applications such as client maintenance management systems (CMMS), OrangeQC, cleaning software, key systems, etc.; ability to adapt to new technologies. • Capacity to embrace change and act as a change champion for others. • Analytical, organizational, planning and problem-solving skills, in order to coordinate and direct the work of custodial staff and to examine alternate possibilities and arrive at the best solution. • Client service aptitude with the ability to consistently deliver excellent client service with an ability to interact professionally and effectively with staff at all levels of the university, faculty, students and members of the public, and to provide clear and accurate information to clients and contacts. • Capable of maintaining strict confidentiality with an ability to recognize and handle confidential information in an appropriate manner. • Receptive to diverse thoughts and alternative perspectives and incorporate them into the work where appropriate. • Ability to work independently and as part of a team, mindful of the interests of other stakeholders. • Ability to maintain composure in a stressful environment. • Ability to remain adaptable in an environment constantly subjected to interruption and change. • Ability to provide consistent, timely and appropriate staff intervention. • Ability to motivate and to create a positive work environment; sensitivity to issues affecting staff. • Ability to write clear, concise and reports. DECISION MAKING: • Collaborate with Manager to decide on content of messaging that is distributed to key press locations. • Assesses the suitability of job candidates and recommends the most appropriate person for hire. • Determines priorities and makes decisions about staff utilization and assignment of work to achieve optimum efficiencies and productivity. • Assesses employees' training needs and makes recommendations for internal or external training to attain proficiency. • Monitors and assess output and the quality or employees' work, and recommends need for formal training or development plans to management and identifies possible performance and/or disciplinary issues. • Problem solving related to custodial procedures. • Allocates and monitors the work of custodial staff. • Determines appropriate actions to handle emergencies in accordance with CSS, Facilities and university procedures, escalating where appropriate. • Assesses and identifies potential inefficiencies with current programs, escalating where appropriate.
116034.requirements: QUALIFICATIONS: • Post-secondary education in Facilities Management, Business Administration, or a related field combined with relevant experience in supervising/managing unionized custodial staff in an educational or large commercial/industrial setting. • Knowledge of inventory control, custodial procedures, tools and equipment, and practices that operate 24/7. • Competent supervisor as defined under the Occupational Health and Safety Act with practical knowledge of the Occupational Health & Safety Act and how it applies to custodial work. • Satisfactory Criminal Records Check (CRC) and Vulnerable Sector Screening (VSC). • Valid Province of Ontario Class Full G driver's licence and insurable under the university's insurance plan. • Knowledge of the International Sanitary Supply Association (ISSA) and Association of Physical Plant Administrators (APPA) training considered an asset. • Knowledge of programming autonomous equipment considered an asset. • Consideration may be given to an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

116107.description: Position: Multicultural Liaison Officer (MLO) Term: 17.5 hours per week - September 2026 - June 25, 2027 Reports to: Manager of the Multicultural Liaison Officer Program Location: Various locations across the Ottawa region About OCISO OCISO supports immigrants through the journey of making Canada their home by providing creative and responsive programs that are culturally and linguistically appropriate, by building community through mutual respect and partnerships, and by fostering healthy and inclusive spaces for open dialogue and healing. As a Human Remains Transport Specialist with EORS, you will. You'll work in a two-person team responding to calls from hospitals, retirement homes, and private residences across Ottawa - treating every decedent, and every family, with the dignity they deserve. About EORS Since 2003, Eastern Ontario Removal Services has been the National Capital Region's leading removal service for the funeral industry - the largest and longest-running provider in Ottawa. Our unmarked, professionally equipped fleet and trusted relationships with funeral homes, hospitals, and police services are built on one thing: staff who show up with compassion, integrity, and respect every time. Why Join Our Team Paid, hands-on training - no prior experience required Security clearance fully paid for by the company Full-time or part-time schedule Health benefits: dental, vision, and life insurance (for eligible employees working 20hrs a week) Work as part of a supportive two-person team, never alone on a call A genuinely meaningful role - you make a difficult moment easier for grieving families A Day in the Life You'll work 12-hour on-call shifts in pairs. When a call comes in, the dispatcher sends you the details and your team heads to the scene - a hospital, home, or care facility. You'll carry out the removal with care and professionalism, then transport the decedent to different locations for after care. What You'll Do Complete removals of decedents from hospitals, private residences, and retirement/nursing homes Safely operate company vehicles to transport human remains Offer calm, compassionate support to grieving families at the scene Complete funeral home intake paperwork accurately Coordinate with funeral home staff, police, and dispatchers throughout your shift

For example, in 2024, TELUS planted 8 million trees to help mitigate climate change and build a better and more sustainable future. You will join a three-year rotational program designed to meet all of your CPA practical experience requirements while working through your CPA professional education program. 116289.title: Immigration Law Clerk/Paralegal
116289.description: At Green and Spiegel, the title of the role is Immigration Case Analyst. Green and Spiegel, Canada's preeminent immigration law firm, sets the gold standard in the highly specialized area of immigration law. With a team of 120 talented individuals, the firm guarantees that each and every client receives top notch service. Given the breadth and depth of expertise at Green and Spiegel, there is no case too complicated or too large for the firm to handle. The firm reflects the diversity of the clients they serve and can provide services in approximately 30 languages. Knowing that you have a significant role in helping people at a critical point in their lives, makes working at Green and Spiegel a very exciting and rewarding place to work. Come join the team! The Immigration Case Analyst plays a key role in the intake, processing and follow up of client files. Immigration Case Analysts operate at various levels of autonomy and on various types of immigration files depending on their level of experience and tenure with the Firm. If you are someone who is eager to learn, values teamwork and strives for excellence in all that you do, then Green and Spiegel will be a great place for you. We are seeking a legal professional with any level of previous experience at an immigration law firm and someone who thrives working on challenging and rewarding work in a fast-paced environment. Experience with the following immigration application types would be an asset: LMIAs Work Permits Sponsorships Express Entry Investor Programs Immigration Case Analysts may report into a Team Lead, Associate Lawyer or Partner depending on the level and team. Key Duties and Responsibilities: Acting as the key point of contact for client inquiries at all stages; sending out initiation for files and providing clients with status updates throughout the life-cycle of their file Completing government forms required for various applications, drafting submission letters, mining the client's file for information and following up on outstanding information in a timely manner Conducting research and leveraging government resources to ensure processes are current and appropriate documents are being used Full accountability of assigned files or applications including checking client ledgers and billing processes, reviewing invoices for approval Scheduling appointments and meetings with clients Ensuring that timelines and deadlines are diarized and met including expiry dates and other key dates
116289.requirements: Skills and Qualifications: Bachelor's degree OR a Diploma or Certificate is required Any legal administrative or immigration experience including LMIA, Express Entry, PNP, Sponsorship and Work Permit Applications is an asset Excellent customer service skills Strong attention to detail and organizational abilities Excellent writing abilities is a requirement Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-volume environment

CC-351719.title: Assistant Store Manager
CC-351719.description: Position Overview The Assistant Manager is generally responsible for assisting with the day-to-day operations of the store as assigned by the Dealer-Owner or Store Manager. These duties commonly include supervision of personnel, serving as manager in the manager's absence, helping to meet sales and financial objectives, advertising and promotional planning, working on special projects, supervising inventory, merchandising, pricing, and facilitating communications between management and employees. The Assistant Manager performs all assigned tasks with sufficient speed and accuracy to support store efficiency and a high level of customer service. Key Responsibilities Provide guidance and supervision for staff members as directed by the Store Manager or Dealer-Owner(s). Assist the Store Manager with staff meetings and training. Serve as manager in the manager's absence. Hire or suggest the hiring of new full or part-time sales personnel within assigned departments. Advise the Store Manager well in advance of the need for increased or reduced sales personnel. Establish work schedules for full and part-time sales personnel. Ensure that store fixtures, trucks, the POS system, and other equipment are in proper condition to meet the store's operational needs. Make suggestions to the Store Manager when equipment should be replaced. Identify current or foreseen operating situations and inform the Store Manager in a timely manner to facilitate a solution. Suggest rule or policy changes to the Store Manager when such changes would improve efficiency, morale, operations, profits, sales, etc. Be a positive role model by following company procedures. Attend trade shows and Homecoming as directed by the Store Manager. Develop promotions to build store traffic. Ensure that the sales floor and sales staff are ready for all promotions. Understand and use merchandising techniques that produce the highest possible level of sales. Ensure that endcaps and feature displays are properly merchandised, maintained, and changed on a timely basis. Facilitate and maintain communication between employees, the Store Manager, and Dealer-Owner(s). Be responsive to employees who have questions and/or comments about their job responsibilities. Encourage employees to share their ideas and suggestions. Resolve employee complaints and problems. Take appropriate disciplinary action when employees violate company rules and/or policies. Act in a timely manner when taking disciplinary action or acknowledging positive behaviour by employees. Maintain records of such actions. Greet and assist customers on the sales floor. Be aware of shoplifting and take action consistent with company policy to discourage it. Maintain good customer service through your presence on the sales floor by making effective use of your knowledge of products, projects, and services. Set a good example for other employees through your ability and desire to assist customers and to maximize sales. Resolve customer claims and/or complaints in a manner that is timely, courteous, and discreet. Authorize credit limits, acceptance of cheques, etc. in a manner consistent with company policy. In the absence of the Store Manager, exercise sound judgment in the event that a departure from store policy may be required. Understand the POS system and procedures related to purchases and payments. Work on additional duties and assignments as assigned by management. Work in a safe manner in accordance with provincial and federal safety legislation. Report any potential hazards and unsafe behaviour to management in order to have the situation corrected. Qualifications High School graduation or equivalent. 2 - 3 years of retail experience is an asset. Ability to work a flexible schedule including weekends, evenings, and holidays. Ability to lead. Ability to work co-operatively in a team environment. Excellent communication skills. Excellent mathematical skills. Good understanding of Home Hardware's policies and procedures. Willingness to continually develop professional skills and knowledge base. Working Relationships Reports directly to the Business Owner.
CC-351719.requirements: Education Requirement 1 Education Requirement High School Diploma Requirement Are Working Towards or Have Earned Any of the Following: Diploma or equivalent Degree Preferred year of study: Graduate

CC-351725.title: Sales Associate
CC-351725.description: Position Overview The Sales Associate is responsible for providing prompt, courteous and efficient service to customers. The role includes advising customers on appropriate merchandise and related items, processing transactions (cash, credit card, debit card) using retail software, ticketing and replenishing merchandise, cycle counting, and general housekeeping of shelves. Key Responsibilities Assist customers in locating merchandising in store, on homehardware.com, as well as processing special orders. Ensure customers are greeted within 30 seconds of entering the store or your department. Determine customer's needs by asking open-ended questions. Communicate product knowledge to the customer as appropriate. Assist customers in locating and comparing merchandise. Assist customers with finding all items needed to complete their project. Process special orders for non-stock or out of stock items. Record repeat customer requests for product and follow-up when product arrives at the store. Assist customers with carrying out of large or heavy items. Relieve as cashier when necessary. Follow procedures and maintain standards according to store policy in the following areas: Loss prevention Receiving and pricing goods Merchandise handling and presentation Housekeeping Reordering merchandise Restocking shelves Handling cash Advise the designated manager of shortages, damaged goods, back-orders etc. Change prices on merchandise, bins, displays, etc. as necessary. Build special displays and signage for sales, promotions and other special events. Remove sales and promotional displays, prices etc. and rearrange stock following promotional events. Always take appropriate safety precautions when cutting pipe, glass, wire mesh, making keys etc., and make an effort to minimize waste. Help unload incoming trucks. Check incoming merchandise against invoices to spot shortages, damaged goods, back-orders, etc. Keep stock in storage area neat, clean, and orderly. Participate in regular cycle counting, and assist in taking annual inventory counts. Reorder merchandise according to stores buying procedures. Attend store meetings, training sessions, etc. as required. Work on special projects as assigned by department manager. Work on additional duties and assignments as assigned by management. Work in a safe manner in accordance to provincial and federal safety legislation, as well as use of good common sense. Report any potential hazards and unsafe behavior to management in order to have the situation corrected. Qualifications Ability to work a flexible schedule including weekends, evenings and holidays. Friendly and helpful attitude toward customers. Excellent communication skills. High School graduation or equivalent. Willingness to learn. Good mathematical skills. Prior retail experience beneficial. Creative abilities for making attractive in-store displays. Willingness to continually develop professional skills and knowledge base. Ability to work co-operatively in a team atmosphere. Working Relationships Reports directly to the Department Manager, or Store Manager.

CC-351726.title: Drafting Technologist
CC-351726.employer: All Railings Division of DFL Fabrication Ltd.
CC-351726.description: Position Overview The Drafting Technologist supports the production of accurate, fabrication-ready shop drawings for miscellaneous metals and structural steel projects, including railings, guardrails, stairs, canopies, airshaft frames and gratings, etc. This entry-level role, well suited to a co-op student or recent graduate, uses AutoCAD to translate architectural and structural drawings into detailed fabrication drawings, and Bluebeam to manage markups, redlines, and drawing approvals, under the guidance of senior drafting and engineering staff. The Drafting Technologist works closely with estimating, project management, and fabrication shop personnel, gaining hands-on experience while helping to ensure drawings are accurate, code-compliant, and support efficient production and installation. Reporting Relationship Reports to the Project Manager, with day-to-day guidance and mentorship provided by a Senior Drafting Technologist. Major Functions Shop & Fabrication Drawing Production Assist in preparing shop and fabrication drawings for miscellaneous metals and structural steel components, including railings, guardrails, stairs, and structural connections, using AutoCAD, under the guidance of senior drafting staff. Support the translation of architectural and structural drawings, specifications, and field measurements into accurate, fabrication-ready drawings. Learn to develop connection details, material call-outs, and dimensions in accordance with project specifications and engineering requirements. Assist in producing general arrangement drawings, elevations, sections, and details to support fabrication and installation. Help maintain drawing templates, standard details, and title blocks to ensure consistency across projects. Drawing Coordination & Markup Management Assist in reviewing architectural, structural, and engineering drawings for accuracy, completeness, and constructability. Begin using Bluebeam to manage drawing markups, redlines, and revisions throughout the design and approval process, with support from senior staff. Help track and incorporate comments from engineers, project managers, and clients into revised drawings. Support the preparation and maintenance of shop drawing submittal packages and drawing logs for client and engineer approval. Assist in coordinating design changes and revisions with project management and fabrication teams to maintain schedule. Field Documentation & As-Built Drawings Assist in incorporating field measurements, RFIs, and site conditions into drawing revisions. Support the preparation of as-built and conformed-to-construction drawings following installation. Coordinate with field personnel, under supervision, to confirm dimensions and help resolve discrepancies between drawings and actual site conditions. Quality Control & Drawing Standards Assist with quality checks on drawings to confirm dimensional accuracy, code compliance, and adherence to company drafting standards. Learn and apply applicable codes and standards, including AISC, AWS welding symbols, and the Ontario Building Code, with guidance from senior technologists. Help maintain organized, up-to-date drawing files and revision histories for audit and reference purposes. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work with estimating, project management, and fabrication shop personnel to support accurate pricing and efficient production. Participate in project kick-off and design review meetings to build understanding of project scope and technical requirements. Provide drawing support and clarification to shop and field personnel during fabrication and installation, as directed. Contribute ideas to the continuous improvement of drafting processes, templates, and standards. Key Competencies Currently enrolled in, or a recent graduate of, a Drafting, CAD Design, Architectural/Structural Technology diploma or certificate program (or equivalent); co-op students and new graduates are encouraged to apply. Working knowledge of AutoCAD is required, with a strong willingness to build advanced proficiency on the job. Exposure to Bluebeam Revu (or similar markup software) is an asset; training will be provided. Some prior drafting experience through school projects, co-op terms, or part-time work is an asset. Basic understanding of structural steel and miscellaneous metals fabrication methods, connections, and welding symbols is an asset. Developing ability to read and interpret architectural and structural drawings, specifications, and shop drawings, with a strong aptitude to learn. Familiarity with applicable building codes and industry standards (e.g., AISC, AWS, Ontario Building Code) is an asset. Exposure to Tekla Structures or similar 3D modelling software is considered an asset. Performance Metrics Drawing accuracy: frequency of drawing errors or field-driven revisions after drawings are issued for fabrication. Minimize rework required after drawings are issued for fabrication. Reduce recurring errors identified through quality checks. Drawing turnaround: timeliness of shop drawing production and submittal packages against project schedules. 100% of drawing packages delivered on or before internal deadlines. Standards compliance: adherence to company drafting standards, templates, and applicable codes. 100% compliance with drafting standards on internal quality reviews. Key Competencies: Foundational technical drafting skills (AutoCAD); Bluebeam is an asset. Attention to detail and dimensional accuracy. Blueprint and specification interpretation. Organization and drawing document control. Communication and cross-functional collaboration. Problem solving and adaptability. Time management and ability to meet deadlines. Initiative, self-management, and eagerness to learn.
CC-351726.requirements: Education Requirement 1 Education Requirement Education in One of 2 Subjects Requirement Are Working Towards or Have Earned Any of the Following: Certificate Diploma Undergraduate Degree Studied at least one of the following subject areas: Architecture Engineering Preferred year of study: Graduate 3rd Year Student 4th or Subsequent Year Student
