CC-351728.description: Join Our Team at Canada Post Experience the dynamic mail operations and retail environment only Canada Post can offer. As a self-starter with a flexible schedule, you will have the opportunity to work a variety of shifts including, days, evenings, overnights and weekends. This temporary on-call position is a great opportunity to learn about the business of mail operations, as well as the great jobs available at Canada Post. Please note that some offices rotate their staff and a temporary Postal Clerk might be called to work in positions to serve the public at a counter, conduct financial transactions and perform other related duties as required. Key Responsibilities: Perform a variety of sales/customer service activities to ensure complete customer satisfaction Operate a computer point of sale system Maintain floor displays Conduct merchandizing and inventory control Maintain a high level of postal products, services and delivery knowledge Process financial transactions (cash, cheques, debit & credit card payments) Receive, sort, sequence and batch mail items Additional Job Responsibilities: Operate mail processing equipment (clearing jams, remove mail from sorting machines, etc.) where applicable Transport mail between floors/sections using rolling or motorized equipment, where applicable Operate a computer to key in data, when applicable Review mail items for address accuracy, proper postage, etc. Be required to stand in one place for up to 3.5 hours at a time Exercise physical effort in the handling of mail items weighing up to 22.7 kilograms (50 lbs) and carrying mail items weighing up to 15.9 kilograms (35 lbs) and bending, reaching, lifting, carrying, etc. Our Values: Trust, Respect, and Deliver represent our fundamental promise to ourselves, our expectations of one another, and our shared duty to our country. Our behaviours - Make the call, Know the destination, Deliver for others, Ignite our pride - embody our values, bringing them to life and guiding our actions. Qualifications: Experience in customer service in a retail environment Sales experience is an asset Experience working in a production environment is an asset

CC-352344.description: Position Overview The District of Rainy River Services Board (DRRSB) is seeking a passionate and motivated individual to fill an existing Permanent Full-Time Early Childhood Educator vacancy, welcoming both qualified educators and those interested in obtaining their Early Childhood Education qualifications to join the Early Years team. Key Duties Provide continuous supervision of children to ensure their safety and well-being. Ensure compliance with policies and procedures set out under the Child Care and Early Years Act, 2014, District of Rainy River Services Board policies and procedures and the College of ECE's Standards of Practice and Code of Ethics. Actively participate in daily programming, supporting children's learning, development, and well-being while meeting the diverse needs of all children. Engage in child-initiated, teacher-supported play-based learning that follow the "How Does Learning Happen" document. Provide a daily balance of indoor and outdoor exploration time that invites children to investigate, imagine, think, create, solve problems, and have meaningful experiences. Work within a team to build and maintain healthy relationships and communicate effectively and respectfully with children, families, and colleagues. Respond to parent questions and concerns about their child's day, using care and compassion. Ensure consistency with respect to setting of limits for children. Maintaining positive discipline as set out in the Child Care and Early Years Act, 2014. Participate in maintaining the Atelier's environments, equipment, toys, and storage areas to meet health and safety standards. Qualifications Two-year College diploma in Early Childhood Education, approved equivalency, or willingness to obtain (qualifications can be obtained while working full-time; grants may be available to help support costs). Candidates with an equivalent combination of education and childcare experience will be considered. Registered with the college of Early Childhood Educators, or ability to register upon completion of Early Childhood Educator Program from a recognized institute. Ability to work with minimal supervision, exercise a high level of integrity, professionalism, exercise sound judgment in decision making and maintain confidentiality at all times. Current first aid, including infant and child CPR. Ability to complete the Ontario Food Handler Certification and ongoing renewals. Up to date immunization record. Provide a satisfactory outcome of a CPIC Vulnerable Sector Screen. Legally eligible to work in Canada. We offer a competitive salary, an excellent benefit package and participation in the OMERS Pension Plan. Candidates who meet or exceed the requirements for this rewarding position are invited to submit a complete application for employment (Application form, cover letter and resume, including 3 work-related references) to: Joanne Spence, B.HRLR, CHRL, Human Resources Manager

CC-353489.title: Community and Fund Development Lead
CC-353489.description: Position Summary The Community & Fund Development Lead is responsible for coordinating and implementing fund development and community engagement strategies that generate sustainable revenue, foster meaningful community relationships, and increase awareness of the North Okanagan Hospice Society (NOHS). This position supports the organization's mission by delivering high-quality fundraising initiatives, donor stewardship programs, grant activities, community partnerships, events, and communications that align with the Society's strategic priorities. The position builds and maintains strong relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, and supporters while ensuring an exceptional donor and community experience. Working collaboratively across the organization, the position contributes to a culture of teamwork, innovation, and service excellence. As a member of a small non-profit organization, the position provides support to organizational initiatives as required, with all responsibilities contributing to revenue generation, donor stewardship, community engagement, or increased awareness of Hospice services. Key Responsibilities Fund Development & Donor Relations Coordinate the implementation of the Society's annual fund development strategy in alignment with organizational goals and fundraising targets. Build, cultivate, solicit, and steward meaningful relationships with individual donors, sponsors, foundations, service clubs, businesses, and community partners. Identify, develop, and secure new funding opportunities, including major gifts, grants, sponsorships, and community partnerships. Coordinate annual giving initiatives including direct mail campaigns, online fundraising, monthly giving, memorial giving, and other donor engagement campaigns. Develop and implement donor stewardship initiatives that foster long-term relationships, meaningful recognition, and donor retention. Maintain accurate donor records and fundraising data within the donor management system while monitoring fundraising performance and preparing reports as required. Monitor fundraising budgets and campaign performance to maximize revenue generation and return on investment. Strategic Fund Development, Planning & Evaluation Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Society's annual fund development plan in alignment with strategic priorities and revenue goals. Monitor and evaluate fundraising campaigns, donor engagement activities, and community initiatives using key performance indicators and fundraising metrics. Analyze fundraising data, donor trends, and campaign outcomes to identify opportunities for growth, innovation, and continuous improvement. Prepare reports, summaries, and recommendations to support informed decision-making by the Executive Director and Board of Directors. Identify emerging fundraising trends, community needs, and best practices to strengthen the Society's fund development strategies and long-term sustainability. Support the development of annual fundraising goals, campaign calendars, and project timelines to ensure coordinated implementation of fund development activities. Foster a culture of continuous improvement by evaluating the effectiveness of fundraising initiatives and recommending enhancements to maximize community engagement and revenue generation. Grants & Sponsorship Development Research, identify, and pursue government, corporate, foundation, and community grant opportunities that align with organizational priorities. Prepare compelling grant proposals, applications, supporting documentation, and required reporting to funding agencies. Maintain an annual grants calendar to ensure timely submission, reporting, and stewardship of grant-funded initiatives. Develop sponsorship opportunities and customized sponsorship packages that create value for community partners while supporting organizational fundraising objectives. Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with current and prospective sponsors to encourage long-term investment in the Society's mission. Fundraising Events & Community Engagement Coordinate the planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the Society's fundraising events and community engagement initiatives. Lead the coordination of signature fundraising events including Dancing with the Vernon Stars, Hike for Hospice, the Butterfly Release, Kentucky Derby Gala, and other fundraising initiatives as assigned. Support third-party fundraising events and community-led initiatives that benefit the Society. Recruit, orient, coordinate, and recognize volunteers supporting fundraising events in collaboration with the appropriate organizational lead. Represent the Society at community events, networking opportunities, presentations, and stakeholder meetings, promoting the mission and values of Hospice. Foster positive relationships within the community that strengthen awareness, engagement, and support for Hospice services. Marketing, Communications & Public Awareness Coordinate fund development marketing and communication initiatives that increase community awareness, donor engagement, and support for the Society. Develop and maintain engaging content across the Society's social media platforms, ensuring consistent branding, messaging, and storytelling. Collaborate on fundraising campaigns, promotional materials, newsletters, donor communications, and digital marketing initiatives. Support media relations by preparing media releases, public announcements, promotional content, and community communications as required. Monitor communication and social media performance using analytics and engagement metrics to evaluate effectiveness and inform future strategies. Ensure all marketing and communications reflect the values, mission, and visual identity of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Collaboration & Organizational Support Work collaboratively with the Executive Director, program leaders, administrative staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to advance the Society's mission. Participate actively in staff meetings, strategic planning, training, and organizational initiatives. Support an integrated approach to fundraising, communications, volunteer engagement, programs, and community outreach. Foster a respectful, compassionate, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace. Maintain confidentiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards in all interactions. Exercise sound judgment and responsibly manage organizational resources within approved budgets. Provide support during periods of increased organizational activity while maintaining focus on the primary responsibilities of the role. Perform other duties consistent with the purpose, scope, and evolving needs of the position. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Education, Training and Experience Required Qualifications: Diploma or bachelor's degree in Fund Development, Business Administration, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Non-Profit Management, or a related discipline is preferred. An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered. Minimum of three (3) years' experience in fund development, donor relations, community engagement, marketing, communications, event management, or a related field, preferably within the non-profit sector. Demonstrated experience coordinating fundraising campaigns, donor stewardship initiatives, sponsorship development, and community events. Experience researching, writing, and managing grant applications and funding reports. Experience developing marketing and communication materials, including digital and social media content. Experience using donor management (CRM) databases to maintain records, generate reports, and support fundraising activities. Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and competing priorities. Experience working collaboratively with volunteers, community partners, sponsors, and diverse stakeholder groups. Experience working in a hospice, healthcare, or not-for-profit environment is preferred Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and relevant administrative systems Intermediate knowledge of computer hardware and software functions Attention to detail and accuracy required Clear Criminal Record Skills and Attributes: Cultural Competency: Demonstrates respect, sensitivity, and understanding of diverse cultural perspectives and practices. Builds inclusive relationships with donors, volunteers, community partners, and stakeholders while promoting equitable access and participation in Hospice programs and services. Relationship Building : Establishes, cultivates, and sustains positive relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, staff, and Board members. Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, and exceptional donor stewardship while fostering long-term community support for the Society. Communication: Communicates effectively with clarity, professionalism, empathy, and authenticity across diverse audiences. Demonstrates exceptional written communication skills, including grant writing, donor communications, marketing materials, and social media content. Confidently represents the Society through presentations, networking opportunities, and community engagement activities. Collaboration & Teamwork: Works collaboratively with staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to achieve shared organizational goals. Fosters a respectful, inclusive, and supportive team environment while contributing positively to organizational culture. Initiative & Innovation: Demonstrates creativity, resourcefulness, and a proactive approach to identifying new fundraising opportunities, community partnerships, and donor engagement strategies. Applies sound problem-solving, decision-making, and critical thinking skills to improve programs and achieve organizational objectives. Planning & Organization: Demonstrates exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple fundraising campaigns, grants, events, and competing priorities while consistently meeting deadlines and maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Analytical Thinking & Results Orientation : Uses fundraising data, donor insights, and performance metrics to evaluate outcomes, identify trends, and recommend continuous improvements. Demonstrates accountability for achieving fundraising goals while supporting the Society's long-term sustainability. Self-Management: Demonstrates resilience, adaptability, accountability, and sound judgment while managing competing priorities in a dynamic non-profit environment. Maintains confidentiality, professional boundaries, and a commitment to continuous learning and professional growth. Attitude: Models a positive, enthusiastic, and professional attitude that reflects the mission, vision, and values of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Demonstrates compassion, integrity, and a genuine commitment to building meaningful relationships and strengthening community support for Hospice services.

CC-353492.title: Vice-President, Revenue and Strategic Partnerships
CC-353492.description: Title Vice-President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships Type Permanent, Full-time, 35 hours per week Location Ontario (Toronto, Ottawa) Reports to President & CEO Salary $150,000-185,000 About Us Kinvia, previously known as Canadian Feed the Children, envisions a world in which children, youth, and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Kinvia works in partnership with local NGO?s and communities in Uganda, Ethiopia, Ghana, Bolivia, and with Indigenous Peoples in Canada. Kinvia is here with communities who are building local, self-reliant, sustainable systems to provide food for their children, youth, and families across generations. It works in solidarity with communities to impact all areas of nourishment at all stages of their lives, including income generation, education, gender equality, racial justice, and climate impacts. About this opportunity Reporting to the President & Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships (?VP?) is accountable for advancing its long-term financial sustainability through an integrated, diversified, and partnership-driven revenue strategy aligned with Kinvia?s 10-year strategic directions. As a key member of Kinvia?s Senior Leadership Team, the VP is accountable for the day-to-day operation of the Philanthropy Team and the organization?s annual revenue targets. The VP also advises and supports the President & CEO and the Board to advance Kinvia?s mission and financial sustainability. Mentoring, supporting, and collaborating with a dedicated team, as well as collaborating across teams, the VP ensures donor and constituent relationships are built and stewarded, while providing strategic leadership to the team in executing key initiatives, ensuring vision, growth, and relationship-building are fully realized in practice. Key aspects of this role include revenue generation and diversification, resource mobilization, as well as integrated communications, storytelling, stewardship activities, and brand enablement to ensure that all fundraising communications and engagement strategies effectively support Kinvia?s brand and revenue generation and diversification objectives. Vision A world in which children, youth and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Mission Kinvia accompanies children, youth, and their communities as they work to overcome systemic barriers to ensuring their rights to nutritious and culturally appropriate food, fostering wholistic well-being. Kinvia?s Approach Kinvia?s approach is grounded in a community led approach. Kinvia works alongside local partners and communities to support them to achieve self-determined, equitable and sustainable food systems. Our approach also recognizes the importance of working directly or indirectly with the economic, social, environmental and political systems that underpin and influence food systems. Kinvia?s Values Kinvia?s values are how it governs the organization, makes decisions and acts as it undertakes its work together. They also serve as the foundation of its culture, behaviors and core beliefs. Accountability ? Kinvia demonstrates its commitment to trust through responsible actions, a focus on meaningful impact, transparency, and reciprocal accountability. Partnership ? It nurtures collaborative relationships and engages communities in shaping decisions that affect their lives. Inclusiveness ? It diligently works to create safe spaces where diverse perspectives and experiences can inform and direct change. Solidarity ? It uplifts one another and accompany those affected by systems of oppression and marginalization. Respect ? Kinvia values the dignity of people and uphold human rights. Humility ? Kinvia is on a continuous journey of healing, growth and discovery, and are committed to creating spaces where they can listen to and learn from each other. Impact Report To read Kinvia?s 2024-2025 Impact Report, please visit: https://kinvia.ca/who/impact-financials/ Where Kinvia Works Kinvia works with local community-based partners in Bolivia, Ethiopia, Ghana, Uganda and with 24 Indigenous partners in Canada. Our work is centred in supporting self-determined, equitable and sustainable food systems by working with communities, particularly women and youth on: Food production, harvesting and processing through sustainable agricultural practices and the use of indigenous seeds Livelihood and job creation Financial inclusion Social inclusion and equity in food systems, including gender transformative change in food systems Tradition and culture in food systems Nutrition Education Community governance structures and leadership Tackling the root causes of poverty and homelessness among Bolivian children and youth. To learn more, please visit: https://kinvia.ca/where/ Responsibilities Revenue Diversification & Growth, Strategic Partnerships & External Influence Provide executive leadership for Kinvia?s integrated revenue diversification, growth, and strategic partnerships strategy, aligned to the organization?s 10-year strategic vision and annual operating priorities. Lead the evolution from reliance on traditional fundraising channels toward a balanced, resilient revenue mix that includes major gifts, philanthropy, partnerships, institutional funding, and innovative revenue models. Ensure clear revenue growth pathways, multi-year forecasting, and financial sustainability in collaboration with the senior leadership team. Serve as organizational lead for monitoring external trends in philanthropy, development, and social impact financing to ensure Kinvia remains adaptive, competitive, and future-ready. Champion an integrated resource mobilization model that aligns fundraising, strategic partnerships, communications, brand, and impact storytelling in service of revenue growth, influence, and long-term engagement. Embed an equity-informed and community-centered approach to resource mobilization, evolving traditional fundraising models to prioritize dignity, reciprocity, and community agency, while addressing systemic power imbalances in how resources are generated and shared. Philanthropy, Donor Stewardship, Strategic Partnerships & Resource Mobilization Serve as the senior organizational steward of Kinvia?s long-standing donor and partner relationships, ensuring trust, reciprocity, and shared purpose remain central to all revenue-generating activities. Provide strategic oversight and co-leadership to the Director, Philanthropy & Resource Mobilization in advancing major gifts, foundations, corporate partnerships, institutional funding, and other priority revenue streams. Work in close collaboration with the President and CEO and personally cultivate and maintain select high-value relationships with donors, partners, and funders, acting as a senior representative and relationship-builder for Kinvia. Ensure strong donor and partner stewardship, prospect development, and relationship management systems that prioritize retention, growth, and long-term commitment. Work in close partnership with the VP, Programs & Partnerships to co-design funding and partnership strategies that are aligned with program priorities, country strategies, in-country funding opportunities, impact objectives, and community accountability. Support and activate Board members, committees, and volunteer leaders to extend Kinvia?s relationship capital, networks, and revenue-generating capacity in ways that are strategic, values-aligned, and appropriate to governance roles Integrated Fundraising, Communications & Brand Enablement Provide executive oversight to the Director, Integrated Fundraising & Communications, ensuring that fundraising communications, brand, and engagement strategies effectively support revenue diversification objectives. Ensure Kinvia?s brand and communications strengthen revenue, influence, and trust, while deepening brand equity, amplifying impact, and reflecting the values, voices, and leadership of the communities we work alongside. Offer strategic counsel to the President & CEO and Board on reputation, positioning, and communications risks, including issues and crisis communications as required. Ensure consistent, values-aligned messaging across donor, partner, sector, and public audiences that reflect Kinvia?s identity, commitments, and impact. Oversee high-level performance and integration across annual giving, digital engagement, storytelling, and stewardship channels without direct operational management. Leadership Governance & Organizational Impact Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the President & CEO and an active contributor to Senior Leadership Team decision-making. Support the Board of Directors through clear reporting, insight, and strategic framing related to revenue, risk, and opportunity. Foster strong cross-functional collaboration across Programs & Partnerships, Finance & Operations, and Resource Mobilization to ensure alignment between strategy, resources, and impact. Help position Kinvia as a sector leader in sustainable, ethical, and impact-driven resource mobilization. People and Culture & Values Provide strong, empowering leadership to a high-performing advancement and partnerships team through the leadership of two Directors, fostering shared accountability across revenue, partnerships, and programs. Model and reinforce a culture of trust, accountability, learning, and innovation. Support talent development, succession planning, and organizational resilience within the advancement function. Uphold and advance Kinvia?s commitments to equity, anti-racism, anti-oppression decolonization, and community accountability in all revenue-related practices. Operations, Oversight and Accountability Oversees development and communications departments? budgets and maintains executive accountability for advancement-related revenue targets, budgets, forecasting, and performance reporting. Ensure strong systems, controls, and ethical standards for donor stewardship, data management, and compliance. Oversee effective use of fundraising and CRM systems (e.g., Blackbaud NXT) in collaboration with Directors. Prepare high-level reports and recommendations for the President & CEO and Board of Directors. The Candidate: The ideal candidate?s career demonstrates progressive advancement into senior fundraising and leadership roles, including overseeing staff and ideally reporting to a board on fundraising matters. Candidates should have a breadth of experience across the areas in the portfolio, including storytelling, digital engagement and leveraging an organization?s brand to support donor engagement and revenue generation, and with relationship-based fundraising across multiple revenue streams including annual giving, mass market, major gifts and with individuals, foundations, and corporations. As a strategic, systems-thinking leader, candidates have strong financial and budgetary acumen, including managing budgets and with multi-year planning and forecasting, relevant charity regulations, and of CRA guidelines. As a senior executive, you also have experience leading through complexity, change and constraint while maintaining focus on long-term sustainability. Your engaging, honest, and transparent communications style is evident by how you cultivate and maintain strong and trusting relationships with donors and partners, and with your colleagues, direct reports, and Board members. Candidates must demonstrate strong alignment with Kinvia?s mission and values, including a commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression, demonstrated cultural knowledge, humility, and sensitivity, and the ability to engage respectfully and collaboratively with diverse communities, including Indigenous partners in Canada and global partners across Kinvia?s programs. While the Search Committee recognizes that it is unlikely that any one individual will possess all the desired qualifications in equal measure, in addition to the above, the ideal candidate should have the following: Progressive senior leadership experience in fundraising, advancement, or revenue development, with demonstrated success growing and diversifying revenue. Proven ability to lead through complexity, change, and constraint while maintaining focus on long-term sustainability. Deep expertise in major gifts and relationship-based fundraising; experience across multiple revenue streams required. Strong strategic, financial, and systems-thinking capabilities, including experience with forecasting and multi-year planning. Exceptional relationship-building skills with donors, partners, executives, and Boards. Demonstrated ability to lead and empower senior leaders and build high-performing, collaborative teams. Excellent communication, influence, and executive presence. Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression. Experience working closely with a non-profit Board of Directors. CFRE designation is considered an asset. French or Spanish language skills considered an asset. Willingness to travel occasionally and work flexible hours as required. A strong alignment with Kinvia?s values and a desire to make a meaningful difference. Location/Work Hours: While Kinvia is remote first work environment it requires the successful candidate to be based in Toronto or Ottawa and be available to work occasional evenings or weekends to accommodate fundraising events, donor meetings across time zones, and urgent deadlines. The role also requires candidates to be able and willing to travel domestically and internationally. Candidates must be legally eligible to work in Canada. What we offer: Join our team and enjoy a range of benefits designed to support your professional growth and personal well-being: Flexible Work Environment: Embrace a work-life balance with our remote work options. Health & Dental Benefits : Comprehensive coverage to ensure your health and wellness. Mental Health Day : Two employer-supported mental health days per year to help you rest, recharge, and care for your wellbeing. Pension Program: Secure your future with our employer-matched pension plan. Summer Hours & Holiday Program: Enjoy flexible summer schedules and extended holiday periods. Generous Time Off: Benefit from personal days, vacation, and sick leave to recharge and refresh. Volunteer Opportunities: Make a difference with paid volunteer days. Parental Leave Top-Up: Additional support during your parental leave. Learning and Development Support: Invest in your career with our continuous learning and professional development opportunities. Inclusive Culture: Be part of a workplace that is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, decolonization, anti-racism, and anti-oppression. How to Apply: To learn more about this impactful leadership opportunity with Kinvia, please submit your application: https://kinvia.bamboohr.com/careers/72 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, please apply as soon as possible. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those under consideration will be contacted. The position will remain open until the successful candidate has been selected. __________________________________________________________________ ??Kinvia is committed to inclusive, accessible and barrier-free employment practices and to creating a workplace that reflects and supports the diversity of our community. We encourage and welcome applications from qualified applicants including members of racialized groups, Indigenous Peoples, women, persons with disabilities, and persons of any sexual orientation or gender identity. Please let us know if you require an accommodation and we will work with you to ensure a barrier-free hiring process. For further information about Accessibility or Accommodation process at Kinvia, please contact our People and Culture Department. ?

CC-353506.title: Independent Living Assistant - Relief
CC-353506.description: Under the supervision of the Site Manager and under the direction of clients, the Independent Living Assistant (ILA) assist adults who have physical disabilities with activities of daily living by performing personal support services. This includes tasks involved with personal care and hygiene, general housekeeping, and meal preparation to support independent living, dignity and choice of lifestyle. Summary of Duties Under the direction of the client, provide personal care assistance including: Transfers and lifts Morning and nighttime routines Dressing[MH1.1]/undressing, including medical aids (i.e. braces etc.) Light housekeeping duties Meal preparation including serving, feeding as required and clean-up Peri-care, bowel and bladder care, catheterization, condom application and emergency procedures Attend shifts and bookings punctually and unscheduled booking requests as promptly as possible. CC-354122.title: Marketing Lead
CC-354122.description: Salary Range $100,000 - $150,000 This posting is for an existing vacancy. We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants. The Short Version You'd be our marketing function. Not a marketing team member - the function. One person, senior, with the mandate and the budget to decide what we say, how it looks, and where it runs. That's either the most appealing thing you've read this month or a red flag. We'd rather you know now. Why This Isn't an Agency Job At an agency you'd touch twelve brands and own none of them. Here you own one, end to end: the strategy, the words, the visuals, the campaign, and the number it moved. You'll see a piece of work from a half-idea in a Tuesday meeting through to the metric it changed a quarter later. Very few marketers get that loop, and it's the fastest way we know to get good. You'll report to our Founder, sit close to our Executive Management team, and have real authority over the brand. When you say we're not doing something, we're not doing it. What You'd Actually Do Own the marketing strategy and the budget behind it Write - properly. Editorial, campaign, product, the occasional thing under someone else's name Design and ship the assets. You'll art-direct yourself most of the time Run our content engine end to end: what we publish, why, and whether it works Use AI tooling the way a craftsperson uses a jig - to move faster on the parts that don't need you, so you can spend your judgment where it counts Bring in freelancers and contractors when the work outgrows one pair of hands, and manage them well Tell us honestly what's working and what isn't Who We Think This Is We're looking for an unusual combination, and we know it. You've probably got two of these deeply and can hold your own in the others: Journalism or editorial. You can find the story, ask the uncomfortable question, and structure an argument. You've worked to a deadline that didn't move. Design and graphics. You can build the asset, not just brief it. Figma or Adobe, and taste that shows in the work. AI fluency. You've integrated generative tools into a real workflow and formed opinions about where they help and where they quietly make things worse. Marketing outcomes. You've owned a number, not just a deliverable. Senior-level judgment matters more to us than years. If you've spent three years running a small brand well, that may beat eight years in a large one.

From helping get the boldest research ideas off the ground to supporting the most advanced equipment, together we are pushing the boundaries of what?s possible in children?s health care. What you?ll do We're looking for an Event Experience Coordinator to help plan and deliver impactful and exceptional events that build connection, demonstrate impact, and support fundraising efforts. Reporting to the Senior Event Manager, you'll work closely with internal teams, participants, donors, and volunteers to create meaningful experiences that advance the Foundation's fundraising and stewardship goals. And that permeates every action we take. Support communications related to activism opportunities, events, and calls to action. Assist with maintaining accurate contact lists and engagement records. Help identify and share stories, successes, and examples of activist participation. 3. Campaign and Communications Support Assist with drafting and preparing campaign communications, including emails, newsletters, and social media content. Support the development and organization of campaign resources and toolkits. Assist with internal coordination between Activism, Campaigns, Communications, and other relevant teams. Support research and information gathering related to campaign issues and audiences. Assist with monitoring campaign engagement and identifying emerging trends. 4. Assist with onboarding and engaging participants in relevant digital community spaces and platforms. Help organize resources and information for activists and community members. CC-354633.title: Child and Youth Counsellor (School support)
CC-354633.description: About the Organization At the Child and Parent Resource Institute (CPRI) we provide highly specialized trauma-informed mental health and developmental services. These services include Assessment, Consultation, Treatment, Research and Education. We work with local community services, building on what they have already done and use evidence based practices to adapt our approach to the unique needs of each child. Position Overview CPRI is looking for Child and Youth Counsellors to provide care and treatment in accordance with the residents' individual treatment program and in liaison with their families and community agencies. These positions will provide school support to the clients. Key Responsibilities Provide care, assessment and treatment in the provision of highly specialized residential treatment services for children and youth with complex mental health issues and/or developmental challenges. Work as part of a multidisciplinary team, involving clinicians, guardians and community resources, to utilize best practices, trauma-informed approaches and using a bio-psycho-social model of care in the treatment of children. Work during any assigned shift, during a 24 hour period to assist clients with normal activities of daily living, recognize and report any physical signs and symptoms of health conditions and provide assessment of clients in accordance to the Plan of Care goals. Following completion of training, administer medications and treatments in accordance with CPRI Medication Procedure. Provide individual care, counselling and group therapy for clients. Identify stages of behavioural escalation and respond in a clinically appropriate manner to deescalate the behaviour and develop strategies to reduce the clients concerning behaviours. Maintain clinical records and documents, actively participate in communication processes with partners and participate in plan of care meetings, etc. Attend regular training and development opportunities to maintain an up-to-date knowledge of safeguarding, health and safety and well-being of children and youth being served. Enhance the social, behavioural and emotional functioning of children and youth within the classroom. Plan, collaborate and implement Individual Crisis Management Plan (ICMP) and individual programs. Utilize and review ICMP strategies and individual programs. Provide feedback to the clinical team and primary counsellors regarding client strengths and barriers regarding implementation of ICMP and individual plans within the school setting. Provide educational staff with information and updates on ICMP and individual programs. Encourage a positive school culture and enhance learning with the teacher and client. Assist in the integration of the child and youth's treatment goals with the classroom program, to further the child and youth's overall treatment progress. Daily documentation on clients in the classroom including data collection as requested by clinical team. Transitioning clients to and from school. Planning and provision of summer programming. Qualifications You have successfully completed the: Child and Youth Worker program, or Developmental Service Worker program, or Equivalent with a minimum of one year's experience in a related field following graduation. Knowledge and Experience You have demonstrated experience providing care and treatment to children with physical, developmental and/or behaviour needs on-site and in the community. You have knowledge of evidence based practices for children and adolescents with developmental delay and/or mental health problems, including behavioural modification strategies, learning theories, counselling skills and clinical practices. You are able to develop and implement individual client treatment plan reviews, program evaluation, and educational programs and knowledge of professional, community and facility resources available to assist the child/family. You are able to safely and effectively manage behavioural crisis situations and respond in a trauma-informed approach. Communication Skills You have effective oral and written communication skills to liaise and consult with relevant team members, and provide counsel to residents, their families and community agencies. Analytical, Assessment, and Problem-Solving Skills You can gather and compile data from multiple sources to identify client needs. You can develop/modify client plans of care. Organizational Skills You can manage conflicting priorities, make appropriate care decisions, and maintain adequate records. Salary: $1,184.70 - $1,336.66 Per week Note: If you have not completed the Medication Training Program, administering medications and treatments as prescribed by a physician and in accordance with the CPRI Medication Procedure, you will be hired in the Child and Youth Assistant (CCW1) salary range ($1,082.59 - $1,195.32 Per Week) until this is successfully completed. CC-354636.title: Design Build - Project Manager
CC-354636.description: Position Overview Avia NG is seeking a detail-oriented and hands-on Design-Build Project Manager to support the planning, design, and construction of a major airport capital project for a client. Role Responsibilities This role works collaboratively across multiple offices and disciplines, balancing in-person design and construction assignments with virtual coordination and project management activities. You will be involved throughout the full project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction and closeout. This role will be critical in ensuring seamless technical coordination and design interfacing across various engineering projects. The ideal candidate will work alongside engineers, designers, and project managers to manage project timelines, deliverables, and communication between design and construction teams, ensuring that project milestones are met efficiently and within scope. Your role will be to support the Project Lead in the delivery of an aviation - coastal engineering project, working within an active airport environment. Key Duties As a Project Manager you will work alongside Project Leads and other project managers, architects, engineers, and aviation specialists to support the design and coordination of airport building and aviation related facilities. You will manage the development and coordination and review of design submissions, drawings, specifications, calculations, cost estimates, quantity takeoffs, technical reports, and presentations, with a strong emphasis on maintaining design intent and constructability within an airport environment, aligned with the project scope. This includes coordination of multidisciplinary design teams and ensuring alignment between architectural, engineering, operational, and regulatory requirements. You will help with document control requirements, track decisions, prepare meeting materials, and support the resolution of design and coordination issues that arise from working in live construction and aviation environments. As project moves into implementation, you will also support construction phase services, including assistance with RFIs responses, document control, Change Orders management, payment certifications, and site reviews, helping ensure construction aligns with approved designs and aviation operational requirements. Technical Coordination Serve as a liaison between Client, design teams, contractors, and technical stakeholders to ensure the successful delivery of engineering projects. Assist in the preparation, review, and monitoring of project plans, schedules, specifications and budgets. Coordinate site investigations, technical assessments, and other engineering-related activities. Ensure technical specifications, requirements, and construction plans align with project objectives. Address any technical issues that arise during the project lifecycle by working closely with engineers and contractors. Design Interface Management Facilitate the exchange of information between owners, stakeholders, the design teams, engineers, and contractors. Ensure design deliverables meet project requirements and are in compliance with regulations and standards. Monitor the progress of design work, ensuring that milestones and deadlines are met. Assist in the coordination of design modifications or changes throughout the project, ensuring timely updates to all stakeholders. Project Support Provide administrative and logistical support for the project team, including preparing documentation, reports, and meeting minutes and summaries. Maintain a comprehensive project schedule and provide regular updates on project progress. Track and manage project documentation, ensuring compliance with company procedures and regulatory requirements. Organize project meetings, workshops, and coordination sessions, ensuring timely follow-up on action items. Be onsite during construction to ensure that the construction is progressing as per the schedule and monitor any design and construction issues. Collaboration and Communication Work closely with the Project Lead and other Project Managers and senior technical staff to ensure the project remains on schedule and within budget. Ensure clear communication between all internal and external stakeholders, providing updates on design, scheduling, and technical issues. Manage and resolve any coordination challenges between design, engineering, and construction teams. Qualifications Motivated Project Manager with 7 to 10 years of progressive experience delivering Design-build (DB), alternative Delivery, P3 or major infrastructure projects, with direct involvement in both design coordination and construction execution. Demonstrated experience administering Design-build contracts, including management of RFIs, submittals, shop Drawings reviews, Change orders, progress payment Certification, Contract Correspondence, Notices, Claims and claims management, Delay Events and Schedule reviews. Demonstrated experience in civil engineering, project engineering, project management, design coordination, or contract administration on active construction projects, including construction documentation, contractor coordination, site meetings, and multidisciplinary stakeholder engagement. Strong communication, negotiation and report writing skills and ability to prioritize/manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced project environment. Experience working for a contractor, construction manager, or as a Contract Administrator (CA) on complex infrastructure projects is preferred. Strong understanding of construction claims, dispute avoidance/resolution processes, schedule impacts, change management, entitlement assessments and contract interpretation. Proficient with MS Office suite of programs (MS Word, Excel, Outlook) and AutoCAD 2D; experience with AutoCAD, Civil3D, construction software (e.g. Procore, Primavera, MS Project) is considered to be an asset. Ability to act as the day-to-day Contract Administrator for assigned projects, coordinating communications between the owner, contractor, design team, and stakeholders while ensuring contractual compliance and timely resolution of project issues. Ability to read and interpret engineering and construction drawings, specifications, schedules and contract documents. Valid Driver's license. Topographic survey experience, geotechnical/pavement design knowledge are considered assets. Benefits RRSP - Company matching contribution. 100% Company paid benefits. Opportunities for growth and development. Hybrid work policy and flexible hours. Why are we hiring? We are growing and growing fast! We are adding to our ranks to create a great work life balance for all. This role is a permanent full-time position in our Toronto office.

You will drive employer outreach, recruitment activities, workforce planning support, hiring incentives, placement monitoring, and employer-focused retention strategies. Working closely with participant-facing staff, you will help create strong employment matches and achieve GROW?s employer engagement, placement, and retention targets. What You?ll Be Responsible For Employer Engagement and Job Development: Recruit and engage landscape and horticulture employers across Ontario. Build and maintain an active portfolio of employer relationships and employment opportunities. Conduct employer outreach through calls, meetings, site visits, industry events, chapter and sector activities, and referrals. Assess employers? workforce needs, hiring requirements, workplace environments, and available positions. Promote the benefits of hiring GROW participants, engage and support employers with apprenticeship registration, sponsorship and workforce development, and encourage inclusive, barrier-free recruitment practices. Position Landscape Ontario and GROW as trusted workforce-development partners for the industry. Maintain regular contact with employers to identify current and future workforce needs. Employment and Placement Matching: Match GROW participants with suitable registered employers based on participant qualifications, employment goals, employer needs, and workplace fit. Develop paid employment, work-experience, and Training Placement Agreement opportunities for GROW participants. Gather accurate information about job duties, qualifications, schedules, compensation, workplace expectations, and advancement opportunities. Work with the Employment & Career Development Coordinator and other program staff to identify suitable candidates. Coordinate employer introductions, interviews, hiring activities, and placement documentation. Support employers in understanding applicable hiring incentives, wage subsidies, and program requirements. Ensure placement opportunities meet GROW and Ministry requirements. Deliver or support employer-focused training related to recruitment, onboarding, retention, and workforce planning. Represent GROW and Landscape Ontario at chapter meetings, sector meetings, trade events, career fairs, and networking activities. Develop relationships with industry associations, community partners, Employment Ontario providers, and other workforce-development organizations. Share employer and labour-market insights with the GROW team to support recruitment, training, and service planning. Performance, Records and Reporting: Deliver shared employer engagement, placement, employment, and retention targets. Maintain accurate employer profiles, job opportunities, site visits, participant matches, placements, and follow-up records. Ensure Training Placement Agreements and related documentation are complete, accurate, and submitted on time. Monitor progress and provide updates on employer pipelines, participant matches, employment outcomes, risks, and required follow-up. You will play a key role in connecting day-to-day operations with broader program priorities and ensuring the team has the clarity, information, and support needed to succeed. The Role The Program Specialist provides scheduling, logistics and coordination support across CanREA's Programs Team portfolio, which spans operational best practices, site health and safety, workforce development, insurance best practices, advocacy for behind-the-meter solar and energy storage, statistics and data analysis. Primary Responsibilities Calendar and Meeting Scheduling Coordinate and maintain calendars for Programs Team meetings, committees, working groups and task forces, confirming availability across internal and external participants and time zones. Prepare and circulate meeting agendas and pre-read materials in advance of scheduled sessions. Record decisions, action items and next steps during meetings, and distribute minutes promptly after each session. Stakeholder Outreach and Follow-Up Conduct outreach by phone and email to member companies, training institutions, government contacts and other external stakeholders to confirm meeting attendance and gather scheduling availability. Follow up with assigned owners on outstanding action items to confirm completion by agreed deadlines, escalating to the Manager or Senior Director where needed. Maintain up-to-date contact lists and distribution groups for member committees, working groups, training partners and other Programs Team stakeholders. Respond promptly and professionally to stakeholder inquiries, directing more complex questions to the appropriate Programs Team lead. Program and Project Coordination Support the Programs Team in tracking workplans, timelines and deliverables across the portfolio, including wind, solar and energy storage operational best practices, site health and safety, workforce development, insurance best practices, and behind-themeter solar and energy storage advocacy. Maintain organized project files, shared drives and tracking documents so that program status is current and easy for the team to access. Coordinate the logistics of producing and circulating technical guidance, best-practice documents and position papers, including formatting, proofreading support and version control. Support the coordination of external consultants, contractors and vendors, including scheduling check-ins and tracking deliverable due dates. Provide administrative and scheduling support for research projects and data-collection initiatives, including coordinating interviews or surveys with stakeholders. Support the planning and logistics of CanREA's participation in external workforce tables, advisory committees, and industry and education-sector events. What Success Looks Like Meetings, committees, and working groups are scheduled accurately, efficiently and with minimal conflicts. Stakeholders receive timely, professional outreach and consistent, reliable follow-up. Action items are tracked diligently and closed out on schedule. Program files and records are well organized, current and easy for the team to find. Scheduling conflicts, stakeholder concerns and other potential issues are identified swiftly and communicated proactively. Support to the Programs Team, CanREA members and external stakeholders is dependable, detail-oriented and consistent. Qualifications Functional Competencies Scheduling and calendar management ? demonstrated ability to coordinate calendars across multiple stakeholders and time zones, and to manage competing scheduling priorities. Stakeholder outreach and communication ? comfortable initiating outreach by phone and email, following up persistently and professionally, and maintaining positive working relationships with members and partners. Organization and attention to detail ? ability to track multiple project files, action items and deadlines simultaneously, with strong follow-through. Writing and communication skills ? clear, professional writing for meeting agendas, minutes, correspondence and stakeholder communications. Self-starter ? comfortable working with a good degree of autonomy, prioritizing tasks and recognizing when to escalate to the Manager or Senior Director. Team player ? open to supporting CanREA-wide priorities and pitching in across the Programs Team as needed. Remote work ? able to work effectively, reliably and independently from home. Administration Knowledge of MS Office Suite, including Outlook calendar management. Familiarity with scheduling and project management/collaboration tools (e.g., MS Planner, Monday.com, SharePoint, or equivalent). Familiarity with AI tools such as Claude and Chat GPT. Ability to travel occasionally to attend CanREA events and meetings. Approximately 510% of the time. Education Post-secondary diploma or degree in a relevant field such as business administration, communications, public policy, environmental studies or a related discipline, or a comparable combination of education and experience. Experience 1 to 3 years of experience in a coordination, scheduling, administrative or program/project support role. Experience scheduling and coordinating meetings, committees or events involving multiple external stakeholders is an asset. Experience using scheduling, calendar or project management/collaboration tools. Fluency in English (written and spoken) is required; French (written and spoken) is an asset. Non-profit or association experience is an asset. Knowledge of or interest in the renewable energy sector and energy storage and environment policy is considered an asset. To Apply You can apply for CanREA?s Program Specialist position by filling in this form, being sure to include both your resume and cover letter in PDF format by Monday, September 28 . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so early submission is encouraged. We thank all applicants for their interest in CanREA, however only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. AI at CanREA At CanREA, we embrace AI as a tool to support smarter, more efficient ways of working, when used thoughtfully and responsibly. That said, people matter most. While AI may assist in drafting materials like this posting, we do not use AI to evaluate applicants. Every application is reviewed by members of our team to ensure a fair and human-centered hiring process. CC-327434.title: Retail Store Manager
CC-327434.description: Retail Store Manager at Neepawa Freshmart Neepawa Freshmart is seeking an experienced, results-driven Retail Store Manager to take full operational and financial ownership of our grocery location. As the Store Manager, you will plan, direct, and evaluate the daily operations of the entire store. You will lead the supervisory team, manage profit and loss (P&L) statements, drive sales growth, manage vendor and supply chain distributions, and maintain strict brand and regulatory compliance to ensure an exceptional community shopping experience. Key Responsibilities and Duties Strategic Operations & Financial Management Plan, direct, and evaluate the daily operations of all store departments (Front-End, Grocery, Produce, Deli/Bakery). Manage corporate and store-level budgets, analyze financial statements, track profit margins, and implement cost-control strategies to maximize profitability. Establish strategic sales goals and develop localized marketing, promotional, and merchandising campaigns to drive foot traffic. Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) such as labor efficiency, shrinkage/wastage control, and sales per labor hour. Supply Chain & Inventory Control Oversee procurement strategies and coordinate directly with Loblaw distribution networks and local vendors to secure inventory. Analyze local consumer trends to optimize product assortment, ensuring steady availability of President's Choice, no name, and fresh inventory. Implement strict inventory management protocols to minimize stockouts, control waste in fresh departments, and handle complex supply chain disruptions. Human Resources & Team Leadership Direct, mentor, and evaluate the store's supervisory team, department heads, and general staff (approximately 15-30 employees). Authorize personnel actions including hiring top-tier talent, conducting performance evaluations, overseeing promotions, and managing progressive discipline or terminations. Define and implement robust staff training programs focused on customer service excellence, product knowledge, and operational efficiency. Co-ordinate labor allocation and authorize master employee schedules to ensure optimal floor coverage while remaining within labor budgets. Compliance, Safety, & Community Relations Ensure absolute compliance with federal, provincial, and municipal regulations, including Manitoba labor laws, occupational health and safety standards, and food safety regulations. Address and professionally resolve escalated consumer complaints, ensuring the store maintains an outstanding reputation within the Neepawa community. Secure store assets by managing security protocols, internal audit controls, and facility maintenance. Employment Requirements Education: A university degree or college diploma in business administration, retail management, or a related discipline is highly preferred. (Extensive experience at a senior retail level may be accepted in lieu of formal education). Experience: Minimum 3 years of progressive retail management experience is required, with a strong preference for individuals with a background in high-volume grocery operations or supermarket management. Financial Literacy: Proven capability in managing store budgets, P&L statements, inventory valuation, and labor metrics. Languages: Good verbal and written communication skills in English. Technical Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of retail point-of-sale (POS) systems, digital back-office accounting systems, and inventory management software. Work Conditions & Physical Capabilities Fast-paced, high-pressure environment requiring rapid problem-solving and decisive leadership. Walking, standing for extended periods, and routine desk-based administrative work. Flexibility to work varied shifts to support store needs, including opening/closing rotations, holidays, and peak weekend cycles.

CC-327435.title: Food Processing Machine Operator
CC-327435.description: Company Overview Freshmart is a proudly Canadian grocery and fresh-food retailer committed to serving families across rural and urban Manitoba with fresh produce, quality meats, dairy, and everyday household essentials. Our Neepawa location is a cornerstone of the local community, dedicated to delivering an outstanding shopping experience in a clean, safe, and well-maintained store environment. Position Summary Freshmart Neepawa is seeking a skilled and dependable Food Processing Machine Operator to join our production team. Under the supervision of the Production Supervisor or Department Manager, the incumbent will operate, monitor, and maintain food processing machinery used in the preparation and packaging of fresh meats, deli products, and other food items sold in-store. This is a hands-on, physically active role requiring strong attention to detail, knowledge of food safety standards, and the ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced, temperature-controlled production environment. Key Responsibilities Machine Operation & Production Set up, operate, and monitor food processing machines including slicers, grinders, mixers, vacuum sealers, and packaging equipment as per production schedules. Adjust machine settings such as speed, temperature, and portion weights to meet production specifications and quality targets. Operate conveyor systems, labelling machines, and wrapping/sealing equipment as required by departmental needs. Monitor machine output continuously to ensure consistent product quantity, weight, and appearance throughout the shift. Quality Control & Food Safety Inspect raw materials and finished products for compliance with Freshmart's quality, safety, and presentation standards. Maintain accurate production logs, batch records, and quality control checklists as required by management. Adhere strictly to Freshmart's HACCP, SOP, and Food Safety Management System requirements at all times. Report any product defects, spoilage, foreign matter, or deviations from quality standards immediately to the supervisor. Sanitation & Hygiene Clean and sanitize all machinery, equipment, work surfaces, and processing areas at the start and end of each shift and as required throughout the day. Follow strict personal hygiene and PPE protocols including hairnets, gloves, aprons, and safety footwear at all times in the production area. Comply with all food-handling regulations under Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) guidelines and applicable provincial standards. Machine Maintenance & Troubleshooting Perform routine operator-level maintenance checks including lubrication, blade/belt replacement, and calibration adjustments. Identify and promptly report equipment malfunctions, abnormal noises, or mechanical failures to the maintenance team and supervisor. Assist maintenance personnel during scheduled preventive maintenance activities and equipment inspections. Inventory & Material Handling Receive, inspect, and store raw food materials, packaging supplies, and ingredients in designated refrigerated or dry storage areas. Monitor inventory levels of packaging materials, labels, and processing supplies and notify supervisors of low-stock situations. Accurately weigh, measure, and portion food products in accordance with production orders and retail display requirements. Safety & Compliance Follow all Freshmart safety policies and Manitoba Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) regulations at all times. Use all required personal protective equipment (PPE) correctly, including cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, and safety footwear. Participate in all mandatory safety training, emergency drills, and workplace health inspections as required by the company. Administrative & Other Duties Complete daily production records, downtime logs, and required departmental paperwork accurately and on time. Communicate proactively with supervisors and team members regarding production targets, material shortages, or equipment concerns. Perform other duties as assigned by the Production Supervisor or Department Manager. Qualifications Minimum High School Diploma or GED preferred or equivalent experience. Previous experience operating food processing machinery in a commercial, retail, or industrial setting is a strong asset. Knowledge of food safety standards, HACCP principles, and food handling best practices is an advantage. Ability to read, understand, and follow operating procedures, machine manuals, and safety instructions. Ability to communicate effectively in English. Must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Food Handler Certification (or willingness to obtain upon hire) is an asset. Skills & Competencies Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to identify and troubleshoot basic machine malfunctions and operational issues. Physical fitness - ability to stand for extended periods, lift up to 50 lbs, perform repetitive hand and arm movements, and work in cold/refrigerated environments. Reliable, punctual, and detail-oriented with a high standard for product quality, cleanliness, and food safety. Team-oriented with a positive, cooperative attitude and the ability to work effectively in a shared production environment. Ability to work efficiently under pressure, meet production targets, and adapt quickly to changing priorities. Ability to strictly follow sanitation, personal hygiene, and contamination-prevention protocols. Work Environment Food processing and production area; refrigerated and temperature-controlled zones Physical Demands Prolonged standing, repetitive hand/arm movements, lifting up to 50 lbs, and working in cold conditions Schedule Monday to Sunday (rotating); may include early mornings, evenings & holidays PPE Required Safety footwear, cut-resistant gloves, hairnet, apron, hearing protection (where applicable) Travel Local only; no out-of-town travel required

CC-331228.description: Role Overview The Lead Hand role is an opportunity for employees who demonstrate strong leadership qualities to further their supervisory experience. ON Mine supervisor surface certification or the ability to complete this. Minimum of a proficient Mill Operator 3 in the Rainy River Progression System (Development Opportunities will be considered if the operator has required hours, and is planned for testing). Demonstrates eagerness and commitment to learn and develop through the mill operator progression system. Demonstrates the necessary leadership potential, in addition to the ability to work in a teamwork-oriented environment under minimal supervision or an equivalent combination of experience. To be considered for one of the permanent roles: previous lead hand or supervisory experience is required. Good knowledge of DCS control systems. Positive attitude, team player that demonstrates and encourages New Gold's values. CC-331237.title: Project Geologists
CC-331237.description: Position Overview We are seeking 3 Project Geologists to support an active diamond drilling and field exploration programs at the Moss Gold Project. The role centres on detailed core logging, sample selection, and ongoing QA-QC, alongside daily verification of geological, geophysical, and geochemical data, drillsite supervision, and close coordination with drilling contractors, keeping the program advancing to high technical and safety standards while supporting the geological development of the property. Core Logging & Sampling Logging of diamond drill core, select sample sites, and implement and maintain the QA-QC programs in accordance with site procedures. Data Management & QA-QC Monitor and verify daily data collection and data compilation / data entry for geological, geophysical, and geochemical datasets. Integrate geological information to track and inform program execution, compliance, and optimization. Drill Program Execution Track drilling progress on a daily basis. Visit drill sites to spot holes and assess safety and technical requirements. Contractor Liaison Liaise with drill contractors to optimize drill pad locations in accordance with field conditions. Field Exploration Activities Ensure field teams follow all required safety procedures. Lead a group of field technicians and geology students conducting field activities including prospecting, mapping, soil sampling, and surface stripping. Technical Support & Other Duties Assist the Senior Geologists in technical studies as they arise. Carry out any additional tasks associated with the development of the property, as directed by the Exploration Manager or designate. Qualifications Bachelor's degree (B.Sc.) in Geology, Earth Sciences, or a related field. 3-8 years of exploration / core logging experience, ideally in gold or an Archean greenstone environment. Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices and environmental stewardship. Previous field experience would be considered an asset. Capable of lifting to 50 lbs. Familiarity with Leapfrog, Micromine or QGIS would be considered an asset. Willing and able to work camp-based rotation at site. Compensation Gold X2 offers competitive remuneration commensurate with qualifications and experience, together with travel to and from site and meals and accommodation while on camp rotation. A comprehensive benefits package is also provided.

CC-331239.title: Early Childhood Educator graduate
CC-331239.description: About the Position The District of Rainy River Services Board (DRRSB) is seeking passionate and motivated individuals to fill existing Early Childhood Educator vacancies on a casual or call-in basis, welcoming both qualified educators and those interested in obtaining their Early Childhood Education qualifications to join the Early Years team. Key Duties Provide continuous supervision of children to ensure their safety and well-being. Ensure compliance with policies and procedures set out under the Child Care and Early Years Act, 2014, District of Rainy River Services Board policies and procedures and the College of ECE's Standards of Practice and Code of Ethics. Actively participate in daily programming, supporting children's learning, development, and well-being while meeting the diverse needs of all children. Engage in child-initiated, teacher-supported play-based learning that follow the "How Does Learning Happen" document. Provide a daily balance of indoor and outdoor exploration time that invites children to investigate, imagine, think, create, solve problems, and have meaningful experiences. Work within a team to build and maintain healthy relationships and communicate effectively and respectfully with children, families, and colleagues. Respond to parent questions and concerns about their child's play, using care and compassion. Ensure consistency with respect to setting of limits for children. Maintaining positive discipline as set out in the Child Care and Early Years Act, 2014. Participate in maintaining the Atelier's environments, equipment, toys, and storage areas to meet health and safety standards. Qualifications Two-year College diploma in Early Childhood Education, approved equivalency, or willingness to obtain (qualifications can be obtained while working full-time; grants may be available to help support costs). Candidates with an equivalent combination of education and childcare experience will be considered. Registered with the college of Early Childhood Educators, or ability to register upon completion of Early Childhood Educator Program from a recognized institute. Ability to work with minimal supervision, exercise a high level of integrity, professionalism, exercise sound judgement in decision making and maintain confidentiality at all times. Current first aid, including infant and child CPR. Ability to complete the Ontario Food Handler Certifications and ongoing renewals. Up to date immunization record. Provide a satisfactory outcome of a CPIC Vulnerable Sector Screen. Legally eligible to work in Canada. Compensation and Application Process We offer a competitive salary, plus 6% vacation pay and 10% in lieu of benefits. Candidates who meet or exceed the requirements for this rewarding position are invited to submit a complete application for employment (Application form, cover letter, and resume, including 3 work-related references). CC-331408.title: Recruiter
CC-331408.description: Position Overview Reporting to senior leadership, you'll own the full recruiting lifecycle for skilled trades roles across Canada. This is a high-impact role with the autonomy to build sourcing pipelines, refine recruiting processes, and shape how Tramin attracts talent. Key Responsibilities Source, screen, and recruit skilled tradespeople across Canada: welders, heavy-duty mechanics, millwrights, electricians, labourers, and related roles. Build and maintain a steady pipeline of qualified candidates ahead of project demand. Develop sourcing strategies across job boards, social media, trade schools, unions, industry networks, and referral channels. Conduct phone screens, and trade qualifications (Red Seal, CWB, provincial tickets) as required by client and jurisdiction. Partner with operations and projects managers to forecast hiring needs and prioritize roles. Track recruiting metrics (time-to-fill, source effectiveness, pipeline health) and report regularly to leadership. Represent Tramin at trade shows, job fairs, and community and Indigenous engagement events as needed. What You Bring 3+ years of recruiting experience, ideally for skilled trades, industrial services, mining, construction, or oilfield roles. Strong working knowledge of Canadian skilled trades certifications and labour markets. A network of contacts in the trades, or a proven track record of building one quickly. Comfortable with high-volume, fast-paced hiring across multiple regions and time zones. Self-starter who operates independently and owns outcomes end-to-end. Strong communication skills and the ability to build trust with both candidates and operations. Experience working with Indigenous communities, employment partners, or local hiring programs is a plus. Compensation and Benefits Competitive compensation aligned with qualifications and experience. Stable, established company (1988) with a growing project pipeline across Canada. Real ownership of the recruiting function. You build it, you run it. Long-term position with room to grow as the company scales. If you are a driven, resourceful recruiter who enjoys the pace of industrial hiring and wants to own a function rather than fit into one, we'd like to hear from you. CC-331411.title: Experienced Mill Operator
CC-331411.description: Position Overview We are currently seeking a dedicated and hard-working individual to join our team as an experienced Mill Operator. In this role, you will be responsible for the safe and efficient operation of mill processing circuits. Your primary duties will include ensuring that all operational activities are carried out safely and effectively, while consistently meeting production targets. Your commitment to safety and efficiency will be critical in maintaining a productive work environment. Camp and travel accommodations will be provided. Key Responsibilities Operating and monitoring various circuits in the processing plant as required by the supervisor. Circuits include: Crushing, Grinding, Leaching/Elution, Reagents, Detox and Tailings. Inspect the circuits regularly to detect any trouble spots and have them corrected as quickly as possible. Ensure the safe & efficient operation of all areas in the mill and report any unsafe conditions to mill supervisor immediately. Develop an understanding of all the mill circuits through training, reading, and hands-on experience. Always maintain a clean work area. Qualifications Applicants who reside in Northwestern Ontario and have experience working in a cross-cultural environment, coupled with knowledge of the unique challenges and opportunities presented to those living in the Northwest Ontario, are assets. Hiring priority will be given to qualified applicants who are beneficiaries of the Impact Benefits Agreement (IBA) and to qualified applicants residing in the Northwest Ontario communities. (Indigenous) Members must clearly identify their status on the online job application and resume if they wish to receive priority consideration. 5+ plus years in milling environment Experience in operational circuits (Grinding, leaching, reagents, CND, tailings, crushing, elution & control room). ABOUT US Strides Toronto Support Services (?Strides Toronto?) Strides Toronto is a multi-service agency supporting infants, children, youth and young adults from birth to age 29, and their families, primarily across east Toronto. Assist in maintaining a clean, organized office environment that is welcoming and safe for guests. Receive and sign for program deliveries and inform appropriate Manager or staff. THE ?MUST HAVES?
