Intermediate level computer and database skills, specifically MS Office ? Word, Excel Awareness of the role of inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility (IDEA) in the workplace and within the community being served by the position. An understanding of anti-black racism, anti-oppressive/anti-racism perspective in the context of the social determinants of health. The Opportunity: We are seeking a Major Gifts Administrator who supports our dynamic, deadline-driven Major Gifts team. Responsibilities: Support the Major Giving team members to successfully cultivate, solicit and steward donors and prospects to meet the fundraising goals Ensure smooth day-to-day implementation of stewardship initiatives through close collaboration and coordination with others in the Philanthropy department, as well as colleagues across the organization Assist in preparing and distributing proposals, reports and presentation materials using various software tools including, but not limited to, Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point, Raiser?s Edge, Canva, and Salesforce Prepare professional, timely correspondence, gift agreements and acknowledgements, receipts, thank you letters, Welcome Packs, reports, pledge reminders, invitations, newsletters and other communications Regularly update and maintain donor records and prospect lists in our database, Raiser?s Edge (RE), and prepare weekly pipeline and activity reports Support donor and prospect research activities Collate and extract donor record information from RE upon request Collaborate on Special Purpose funds and funded programs, ensuring regular communications with project teams, timely collection of statistical data and needed information for reports and financial accountability Manage the Application Bank and Library of Resources for the Major Gifts team Ensure annual (or as needed) updating of Major Donor materials Steward a small portfolio of major donors (up to 50) Organize and coordinate activities such as meetings, tours, webinars, lunches and other events pertaining to major donors, and their associated stewardship plans Qualifications: Post-secondary education in a related field ? We listen and adapt our support to the needs of each community, working together with those affected by disaster, alongside our supporters and partners. ShelterBox is committed to working towards a future where no one goes without shelter after disaster. As conflict, climate change and rapid onset disasters are displacing more than ever before, we have our work cut out for us. ShelterBox is headquartered in the UK. ShelterBox Canada is one of 13 affiliates around the world focused on raising awareness and funds for our vital aid. Role Objectives: Working closely with the Executive Director and our small staff team, you will help to deliver ShelterBox?s Annual Giving strategy, recruiting new supporters as well as developing long-term meaningful relationships with existing supporters. This will involve managing a busy and varied workload of national campaigns, with specific responsibility for donor recruitment, retention and development across a variety of traditional and digital channels. The Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate will have at least three years of fundraising experience in individual giving, and experience fundraising for an international charity is considered a strong asset. They will bring a wealth of experience creating and executing direct mail campaigns, multi- channel fundraising campaigns and have strong knowledge of digital fundraising. They will also have experience monitoring the effectiveness of campaigns and reporting against project plans and budgets. They will have strong knowledge of best practice around donor stewardship, and donor centric communications, and have experience implementing segmented donor journeys and communications. They will have exceptional communication and interpersonal skills and be highly organized with strong attention to detail. They will work well in a remote team environment and be able to work towards multiple deadlines and goals. Knowledge of the humanitarian sector, and experience using WordPress, Adobe Creative Cloud, and/or Keela CRM are considered an asset. Responsibilities: Fundraising Campaigns Produce and manage multichannel direct marketing campaigns, email appeals and other donor communications for ShelterBox?s individual annual gifts, monthly gifts, and mid/major level donors within agreed timescales and budgets. Develop effective campaign structure, including data tracking and segmentation to personalize campaigns and improve donor retention. Create and update campaign pages on the website, and other external channels. Manage the day-to-day relationships with external agencies to ensure the timely delivery of mailed and telemarketing campaigns. Work with the Executive Director to design and test new creative approaches to maximize campaign results. Produce and proof copy, artwork, and data, ensuring that creative is delivered to highest standard of quality. Monitor and analyze data reports to adapt and improve strategies or future campaigns. Ongoing fundraising activities Manage online and offline multi-channel fundraising activities including individual giving, monthly gifts, mid/major level donors and legacy giving. Who We Are Parkdale Community Food Bank (PCFB) is a non-profit, registered charity in the heart of Toronto?s Parkdale neighbourhood. Every month, our programs support more than 17,000 individuals with access to nutritious food and community support. We believe joy is fundamental to nourishment, and our mission is to create a hunger-free community where everyone has a place at our table, with barrier-free access to food they actually want to eat. About the Delivery Program PCFB founded one of the first completely free grocery delivery programs in Toronto back in 2020, to reach community members who couldn?t leave their homes during the pandemic. The program has kept going since, now serving people who face mobility or health barriers to visiting the food bank in person. Clients place weekly orders based on what?s available, and this role is what makes sure those orders actually reach their door. Mission of This Role For a lot of our Delivery Program clients, the Delivery Program Assistant is the only person from PCFB they?ll see face to face. The Delivery Program Assistant brings more than groceries. They carry our mission of dignity and joy in nourishment straight to someone?s door, often noticing the small things, a favourite snack, a treat someone mentioned once, that turns a simple delivery into a moment of real care. When a client isn?t able to come to the food bank, you make sure the food bank still comes to them. This role reports to the Delivery Program Manager for daily operations. They split their time between the road (pickups and deliveries) and the warehouse (prepping, sorting, and organizing donations for the team), with the exact mix shifting depending on the season and what the program needs that week. Responsibilities Operations Pick up donations around the Toronto area, coordinated by the Delivery Program Manager. Deliver groceries to community members enrolled in the Delivery Program, including covering driver routes over the summer when the team needs extra hands. Adjust pace and planning around seasonal volume shifts. Winter is the busiest stretch for deliveries (50%+ above baseline), and pickups spike heavily over the holidays. Resource and Donation Management Prepare incoming resource donations for the packing team, sorting through boxes and flagging what goes to Delivery versus Drop-In. Set aside high-value or requested items like coffee, condiments, and treats, for the clients who?d appreciate them most, drawing on knowledge built through packing and client audits. Receive and organize food donations, including sorting Daily Bread Food Bank deliveries and setting aside specialty items for volunteers to pack. Keep the warehouse shelves organized and restocked throughout each shift so packing volunteers can find what they need quickly. Track incoming donations in the team?s Discord channel. Volunteer and Community Support Support volunteers who need a hand across the warehouse, kitchen, drop-in, or delivery team. Answer phones and greet visitors, directing them to the right person or resource. Build relationships with clients through the client audit process, one of the more regular points of direct client contact in this role. Qualifications Must-Haves A valid G driver?s licence and comfort navigating Toronto for pickups and deliveries. Experience in a customer-facing role; regularly interacting with clients and volunteers The ability to juggle multiple moving pieces at once and stay highly organized. Comfort being the visible face of PCFB in the community, including appearing in photos donors sometimes take during pickups Nice-to-Haves Familiarity with Toronto?s food donation and supplier landscape Experience or training related to workplace health and safety Comfort using Discord or similar team communication tools AI is not used at any stage of our hiring process. The Parkdale Community Food Bank is committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible environment where employees feel valued and respected, and where every employee has the opportunity to realize their potential. As such, we welcome and encourage applicants who identify as racialized persons, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons across the spectrum of sexual orientation and gender identities and have lived-experience. If you are a person with a disability and require accommodation and/or assistance during the application process, please contact us in advance. We strive to provide reasonable accommodations whenever requested. Information received relating to accommodation requests will be treated with confidentiality. To apply, please email your resume and cover letter in one pdf document to info@pcfb.ca with the subject line ?(Your Name) - Delivery Program Assistant?. Please note the application deadline of August 3rd 2026. Early applications are encouraged.

CC-337827.description: Schedule and Reporting Schedule: 14 Days On / 14 Days Off, Day Shift Only Reporting to: Construction Technical Supervisor Position Overview The Construction Coordinator position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to mining infrastructure construction projects through the coordination of contractors, consultants, in-house construction resources, and other departments across varied disciplines. The Construction Coordinator is a highly visible and collaborative role responsible for driving results within planning and executing a variety of earthworks and equipment support projects at Rainy River Mine, including the construction of large-scale tailings dam raises. The position is highly focused on achieving results in safety, quality, schedule, and cost of project delivery while working effectively with internal and external stakeholders. The successful candidate will embody Coeur Mining's purpose statement, "We Pursue a Higher Standard," and values of protecting our people, places, and planet; developing quality resources, growth, and plans; and delivering impactful results through teamwork. The successful candidate must demonstrate commitment to, and compliance with, all company and industry Health & Safety, Environmental, Social Responsibility, and Code of Conduct policies and is responsible for engaging their work with the Courage to Care, meaning never compromising on safety, looking out for one another, and stopping work if it is not safe. Key Responsibilities Champion Site Safety Policies & Procedures Demonstrate Safety-first mindset and commitment to the Courage to Care positive safety culture. Maintain review compliance with all relevant Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and other site safety policies on at least an annual basis or as revised and ensure performance of work in accordance with SOPs. Conduct Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) for non-routine tasks and ensure that all work conducted by the Construction Department is supported by appropriate risk assessments, permits, and safety documentation. Participate in Critical Risk Management, safety audits, workplace inspections, hazard identification, and leading safety performance activities in the field to identify, stop, and correct unsafe conditions or behaviours. Demonstrate leadership in fostering a positive culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement. Construction Planning Develop Construction Execution Plans (CEPs) throughout the project lifecycle from project initiation and development through to closure, and update as necessary throughout the project as planning develops. Contribute to the development, maintenance, and continuous updating of construction plans, estimates, and schedules, including materials, resources, and execution methods throughout the project. Ensure regular updates accurately reflect current conditions and that all work is accounted for in short-term and long-term planning revising plans as site progress, priorities, conditions, and objectives change. Set daily, weekly, monthly, and annual plans and goals in collaboration with Supervisors, Superintendents, and other stakeholders to achieve business objectives. Monitor progress and variance and enact action plans to maintain project schedules. Support workforce and equipment lineup planning and identifying required skill sets, operator coverage, and potential needs or changes to maintain critical path progress and workforce and equipment optimization. Prepare, chair, and present construction planning meetings, ensuring clear communication of upcoming priorities, resource needs, critical path activities, and hold collaborative workshop planning for upcoming construction scope, risk mitigation, opportunities, and action record keeping. Contribute to Project Engineering & Design Review engineered drawings, specifications, and contract documents and identify constructability concerns, conflicts, or propose alternative solutions to improve performance for consideration by design engineers. Create and respond to Requests for Information (RFIs), and other formal construction documentation throughout project execution such as Site Instructions (SINs), or Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs). Organize and participate in design constructability review workshops with internal and external resources. Reporting Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly reports on construction progress, performance, risks, and opportunities. Support the Construction Administrator with data entry, clarifications, and other recordkeeping requirements. Provide clear, timely communication to leadership regarding project milestones, variances, challenges, risks, and upcoming priorities as construction plans change. Raise variances and risks early and propose action plans for mitigation and schedule recovery. Prepare professional cross-shift notes to ensure detailed forward-thinking handover between rotations, providing clear updates on project progress, changes, field issues, risks, important discussion highlights, upcoming priorities, and actions required by the incoming team. Cost Control Support Project Controls with cost breakdown structures, forecasts, and accurate monitoring of performance. Provide field knowledge input, scheduling, and estimating to assist with budget preparation, forecast accuracy, and cost variance tracking. Ensure alignment between field execution and financial reporting through proactive communication and clear and consistent updates to both short-term and long-term construction planning, scheduling, & prioritization. Field Support Facilitate daily alignment and communication between supervision, survey, coordinators, field crews, consultants, contractors, and other departments as required to execute projects safely and efficiently. Support surveyors with surveying and quality control activities in the field to ensure that work complies with issued-for-construction drawings, technical specifications, and design intent. Coordinate with the Tailings Dam Technician to plan and sequence instrumentation raises and installations. Continuously identify issues related to design, quality, or constructability in the field; evaluate impacts; suggest possible solutions; and prepare or coordinate responses from consultants as needed to resolve matters promptly and align with design intent. Oversee the Owner's Representative for quality control, coordinating with consultants to review results, resolve non-conformances, and manage corrective actions with contractors to meet project specifications. Provide hands-on field support to Construction Supervisors and Lead Hands as required, assisting with daily coordination, resolving field challenges, and construction execution. Qualifications 3 - 5+ years of experience in construction, preferably within mining or heavy civil earthworks industries. 0 - 3 years of experience will also be considered for strong early career candidates. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications; experience with project scheduling software considered an asset. Experience in construction planning, estimating, scheduling, quality, and cost management. Experience in reading, reviewing, and implementing engineered drawings for construction. Civil Engineering or related technical education (P.Eng., E.I.T., Technician, or Technologist) considered an asset. Proven leadership and operational management experience in construction environments. Ability to evaluate and positively influence team performance to foster a dynamic, self-accountable workforce. A demonstrated consistent positive attitude with strong interpersonal and team collaboration skills. Familiarity with mine site safety protocols and heavy equipment awareness. Canadian driver's license and a clean driving record. Working Conditions Split time between office and field (driving and walking). Occasional moderate lifting required (typically less than 50 lbs). Collaborative team environment with regularly scheduled and ad hoc meetings. Exposure to active construction and mining requiring adherence to all site safety standards. Compensation The anticipated salary range for this position will be between $95,000.00 - $105,000.00 Note: this employment opportunity is based on an actual current vacancy, not just for future consideration. We are seeking a Finance Manager who shares our commitment to our mission, vision, and values and who will provide strong financial leadership to support our continued growth and impact. Position Summary Reporting to the Senior Director of Finance, the Finance Manager is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day financial operations of the Bob Rumball Canadian Centre of Excellence, Bob Rumball Camp for the Deaf, and Bob Rumball Foundation for the Deaf. The Finance Manager ensures the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of financial reporting while overseeing operational accounting functions, budgeting processes, audits, and financial compliance. This role provides strategic financial insight to support organizational decision-making and leads the Finance team in achieving operational excellence through effective leadership, process improvement, and sound financial management. Key Responsibilities Leadership and Team Management Lead, mentor, coach, and support the Finance team by fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and professional development. Promote a collaborative, customer-focused approach when working with internal departments and external stakeholders. Supervise and support the Finance team, including the Accounts Receivable Clerk, Accounts Payable Clerk, and Senior Accountant. Prepare accurate and timely monthly financial statements and quarterly ministry and funding reports. Lead monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial close processes. Ensure timely preparation and filing of GST/HST returns and other statutory reporting requirements. Maintain strong internal controls and ensure compliance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), applicable legislation, funding requirements, and organizational policies. Coordinate annual external financial audits. Monitor financial performance, prepare variance analysis and forecasts, and provide recommendations to senior leadership. Provide financial guidance and professional judgment to support organizational planning and decision-making. Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance financial systems, reporting processes, and departmental effectiveness. Experience leading organizational change and implementing process improvements. Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities with strong attention to detail. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build effective relationships across all levels of an organization. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word, and ERP accounting software. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains) and QuickBooks is considered an asset. Ability to prioritize competing deadlines, manage multiple projects, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment. Limited Opportunities to Work Remotely Salary: $31.98/hour Application Deadline: August 20, 2026 by 11:59 pm Program Overview ? Community Care, Mental Health & Addictions The Comprehensive Care Specialist is responsible for working independently and with the Comprehensive Care and Integration Specialist (CCIS) team to facilitate smooth care transitions (i.e. from acute care to community), to provide service coordination, psycho-social assessment, intensive case management, therapeutic and/or supportive counselling, and making referrals to various resources to improve outcomes for older adults, seniors and/or their family/caregivers. The role includes collaborating with health care providers, and other resources in the community to enable individuals who are vulnerable, at risk and marginalized to live safely and independently in the community and reduce unnecessary hospitalizations and emergency room use. What You Will Do Referrals and Outreach: Develop trust and rapport with clients and hospital staff in order to identify individuals who could benefit from social work support and transitional care coordination. Work with hospital staff to identify and engage clients and support hospital staff in making referrals to the CCIS team, as appropriate. When necessary, follow up with referral source(s) to learn more about the client being referred, reason for hospitalization and/or reason for referral, to support in development of Coordinated Care Plan (CCP). Develop relationships with other service providers in order to make seamless, effective referrals and service connections. Work closely with CCU central intake and program managers to identify clients with frequent hospital/ED use who may benefit from CCIS support to reduce unnecessary hospital use. Direct Client Support: Perform psychosocial and/or psychological and geriatric assessments. Provide service/care co-ordination, system navigation, short-term and long-term planning and follow-up support. Provide short-term case management services (up to 90 days) to clients through the development and implementation of a care plan and/or Coordinated Care Plan (CCP) to address their priority and emerging needs. Provide short-term intensive care coordination and work closely with the CCIS team, hospitals, and other referral sources to support clients and facilitate smooth transitions between hospital and community. Provide clinical and/or supportive counseling to clients utilizing a wide range of therapeutic approaches that best meet the clients? needs and circumstances. Provide preliminary assessment of risk in crisis situations, consult and devise an intervention and action plan, and provide crisis intervention. Provide crisis intervention and practical assistance to clients and/or family or caregivers as required in homes and community settings. Link clients with internal resources, program and services within Community Care Unit and WoodGreen as well as with external resources and programs. Work to prevent future avoidable ED visits, 30-day hospital re-admission and Alternative Level of Care (ALC) placements for clients referred to the CCIS team. Facilitate access to service including arranging for phone/in-person interpretation when needed. In consultation with internal and external partners, develop appropriate onsite programming and supports. Facilitate or lead social and/or support groups as required. Provide suggestions, support and resources to other CCI specialists and participate actively as part of the CCIS team, sharing expertise Participate in Team Calls, and manage all referrals accepted, including data collection/tracking Discuss options for expanding referral sources while balancing CCIS capacity, operational issues and offer recommendation to continue to develop Hub model General: Ensure the organization?s policies and procedures are carried out. Ensure excellent communication with other staff who work on-site at the various specified locations, including PSWs, housing workers, Supervisors and other partners in the community. Keep current about the range of services available in other agencies. Provide mentorship, training and/or supervision to student placements and volunteers. Participate in team and unit meetings regularly, and promote the healthy functioning of the team and unit. Participate in ongoing training and education. Participate in supervision sessions and annual performance appraisals with program manager. Maintain appropriate records and documentation in a timely manner and collect statistical data required for the accountability of the program. Represent the unit on internal and/or external staff committees as directed by program manager. Perform other duties as assigned. What You Bring to the Team Masters of Social Work or post-graduate degree in relevant field MSW or Post-Graduate degree in a related area with 2+ years of extensive crisis/complex seniors experience or BSW with 5+ years of extensive crisis/complex/seniors? experience Registration in good standing with the Ontario College of Social workers and Social Service Workers or another relevant regulatory body in Ontario (e.g. CPRO or COTO). Minimum of 3 years related experience in mental health, addictions, and/or social work. Demonstrated experience facilitating psycho-social groups and supporting individuals with significant mental health and/or addictions issues, cognitive impairment (e.g. dementia), and chronic health issues from a harm reduction, trauma informed, and mental health recovery approach is required. What Will Set You Apart Experience in conflict mediation, client engagement and community development is required. Demonstrated ability in supporting individuals who have complex mental health and/or addiction issues, geriatric issues, cognitive impairment, history of trauma, violence/abuse, chronic physical health issues, etc. Proven working knowledge of theories of addiction, evidence-based treatment models and best practice approaches. Knowledge of, experience with, and demonstrated ability in providing therapeutic and supportive counseling. Knowledge and experience providing addictions counseling and support. Proven ability in providing intensive and short-term case management, care coordination and system navigation. Strong assessment skills. Strong de-escalation and crisis intervention skills Strong interpersonal and conflict resolution skills to work collaboratively with all service providers and stakeholders. Excellent organizational and time management skills. Excellent oral and written communication skills and documentation skills. Self-directed and independent, but also proven experience in working effectively as a team member in collaboration with other community professionals. Ability to exercise good judgment and flexibility. Ability to work from a client-centred approach. Comprehensive understanding and knowledge of the mental health, addictions, geriatrics, health sector, and community resources. Demonstrate knowledge of issues affecting marginalized communities, policies, legislation, programs, and other issues related to scope of practice and social determinant of health. Applied computer skills (MS word, Excel, Internet) and ability to use client information systems. Training and experience using InterRAI suite, Pirouette and ConnectingOntario is an asset. Proficiency in second language, written and oral, is a strong asset. Due to WoodGreen?s multi-site locations we reserve the right to relocate the incumbent to another site, in the same position performing the same duties, as may be dictated by program needs. Reasonable notice of such site relocation will be given. Capable of fulfilling the physical and psychological demands of the job as per the attached Position Demands Analysis. Accommodations for disabilities provided upon request.

Working towards or have completed a Master?s Degree in Couple and Family Therapy or Social Work with a preferred minimum of 1-3 years of clinical experience in mental health. Strong ability to integrate critical analysis, problem-solving skills, and creativity with justice-oriented, client-centred care. Ability to adapt and work effectively in a variety of settings, independently, collaboratively, and within diverse communities. Writing, marketing, and creative skills for blog content, social media, and other projects. Note: This is an independent contractor position, and applicants must be legally eligible to work in Canada. We are an equal-opportunity organization and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

You will ensure the proper geological practices of the team are being followed in terms of planning, organizing, managing and controlling programs to define and extract the mineral reserves/resources existing at the mining site and in its vicinity. You will also ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle's values, health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment. Contribute to economic preliminary studies, pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, coordinating the work of your team with the work of other disciplines and producing technical reports. Provide and coordinate technical support in geology to operations. Assess, organize and approve the required departmental trainings. Keep your department at the forefront of new technologies, following the best practices in the mining industry. Respect and promote the standards of the company and the governmental policies and regulations at play. Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Geology or Geological Engineering. Minimum of 8-10 years of experience in a similar role, in underground mining, production and for gold. Hold all qualifications and requirements to act as a Qualified Person as defined in the NI-43-101 standard. Excellent working knowledge of all Microsoft Office Suite applications, especially Outlook, Excel, Word & PowerPoint and Deswik. CC-342672.title: Technical Services Manager
CC-342672.description: Position Overview Reporting to the Assistant General Manager, Technical Services, you will lead the Mine Planning, Geology, and Geotechnical departments. You serve as the vital link between long-term strategy and execution, ensuring that tactical plans are safe, geologically accurate, and seamlessly aligned with the Life of Mine (LOM) vision. You will ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle's values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment. Key Responsibilities Strategic Integration & Collaboration: Act as the primary technical partner to the Strategic LOM and Resource Modeling teams. You will ensure that tactical pit designs and sequences honour the long-term value drivers while providing 'boots-on-the-ground' feedback to refine future resource models and LOM assumptions. Tactical Execution Leadership: Direct the 0-36 months and 5-year planning window, transforming the LOM strategy into high-precision, executable schedules that meet production targets while optimizing equipment utilization. Geotechnical & Structural Integrity: Oversee the geotechnical team to manage slope stability, monitoring, and ground support designs. You are responsible for ensuring that the pit remains a safe and stable environment for personnel and equipment. Ore Body Custodianship: Lead the Mine Geology department in executing world-class grade control and reconciliation. Ensure that the reserve and grade control models are effectively applied at the face to minimize dilution and maximize metal recovery. Operational Design Compliance: Provide technical governance over all active mining areas, ensuring that haul roads, benches, and waste dumps are built to engineered specifications. Technical Risk Management: Proactively identify and mitigate technical risks - whether geotechnical instability or geological variance - before they impact the production critical path. Bench Strength & Mentorship: Develop a high-performing technical culture, mentoring engineers and geoscientists to bridge the gap between theoretical design and operational reality. Qualifications Bachelors or Masters Degree in Mining Engineering Bachelor's Degree in Mining or Geological Engineering; P.Eng or P.Geo registration in Ontario. 15+ years of experience in large-scale open-pit mining, with at least 5 years in a multi-disciplinary leadership role A proven track record of working across cross-functional departmental lines. You must demonstrate the ability to influence and collaborate with Strategic and Resource teams to achieve a unified site objective Expert knowledge of mine planning and/or geology software (Vulcan, Deswik, etc.) and a deep understanding of how short-term execution impacts long-term asset value The ability to communicate complex tactical constraints to strategic planners and translate high-level strategy into clear instructions for the pit floor. Additional Skills Proven and exemplary organizational, leadership and communication skills and a professional and collaborative approach to problem solving High level of integrity and accountability Highly influential with strong facilitation, negotiation and contractor management skills. Your Work Schedule Schedule: 4/3 schedule at our Detour Lake mine site

CC-343274.title: Finance & Administration Coordinator
CC-343274.description: JOB POSTING Finance and Administration Coordinator (Ottawa - hybrid) Canoe Kayak Canada (CKC) is inviting applications for the role of Finance and Administration Coordinator. CKC is the national body for competitive paddling in Canada. We are a volunteer lead and staff driven organization made up of a community of paddling enthusiasts ? athletes, coaches, officials, volunteers, staff and supporters ? from coast to coast About the Role We are looking for a well organized, detail-oriented, and enthusiastic Finance & Administrative Coordinator to join our team. More than anything, we're looking for a team player?someone who enjoys supporting others, takes pride in their work, and is willing to jump in wherever needed to help the organization succeed. The successful candidate will be responsible for the financial records of the organization including accounts payable and accounts receivable, as well as provide administrative support to ensure the effective operations of CKC. The successful candidate will work closely with the Finance Manager and CEO and be responsible for the financial records of the organization including accounts payable and accounts receivable, as well as provide administrative support to ensure the effective operations of CKC. The position will be based out of the CKC office, which is located in OPawa at the RA Centre ? 2451 Riverside Dr. Salary is based on experience and ranges between $48,000 to $52,000/ year along with benefits. This position requires a minimum two days in the office per week. Start Date: As soon as possible Core Responsibilities Bookkeeping & Financial Administration Enter vendor invoices and employee expenses into the accounting system for payment processing. Process and record corporate credit card transactions and supporting documentation. Receive and record electronic funds transfers (EFTs) and e-transfers. Prepare and issue customer invoices. Assist with accounts receivable monitoring and collections. Process payroll and maintain payroll records. Prepare electronic payments to vendors and suppliers. Complete monthly bank, credit card, and account reconciliations. Prepare bank deposits and record transactions accurately. Ensure all accounting entries are supported by appropriate documentation and recorded accurately and on time. Maintain organized financial records and filing systems. Assist with month-end and year-end accounting processes. Support management with financial reporting and other accounting-related projects as required. Administrative Support Provide administrative support to management and staff. Scan, file, and maintain electronic and paper records. Prepare and distribute incoming and outgoing mail. Maintain organized office files and documentation. Assist with inventory tracking and control. Coordinate and support general office operations. Communicate professionally with clients, vendors, and team members. Assist staff with administrative and operational needs. Perform other duties and special projects as assigned. Qualifications & Experience Diploma or certificate in accounting/finance/business administration. Bookkeeping experience is required such as experience processing accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and bank reconciliations and an understanding of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. Experience with non-profit accounting is considered an asset. Office administration and coordination in a fast-paced environment. Experience with both accounting software (ideally QuickBooks Online) and office software (Microsoft Office, specifically outlook, excel and word). Skills You Will Bring to the Role Ability to produce financial statements and budget documents Effective written and oral communication, bilingual an asset Strong organizational and time-management skills with an ability to manage multiple priorities Ability to pay attention to detail and accuracy, strong analytical skills A positive attitude and willingness to help whenever needed and work collaboratively within a team environment. How to Apply Please submit a resume and cover letter electronically to the attention of Kathy Hare, Operations Manager, email: KathyHare@canoekayak.ca Deadline for Applications: Ongoing until a suitable candidate is found. While we thank all applicants for their interest, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

You will ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle's values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment. Key Responsibilities Operate underground bolting equipment to install rock bolts, mesh, and other ground support systems to stabilize tunnels Conduct routine inspections and maintenance on bolting equipment to ensure safe and efficient operations Perform bolting duties according to mine plans and engineering specifications Adhere to all safety procedures and company policies to maintain a safe work environment Collaborate with the underground team to ensure that all bolting activities are completed on schedule and within operational standards Maintain accurate records of bolting activities, equipment usage, and maintenance logs Monitor ground conditions and report any concerns to supervisor or engineers Identify unsafe conditions in underground headings and report to supervision Assess all excavations and install ground support in development or reconditioned areas as per plan and section as the development progresses Install or fix existing mine services such as vent tubing and pipes using various lifting equipment such as scissor trucks, chain blocks, and hand tools Install ground support following approved method of installation Drill holes using hand-held pneumatic drills (jackleg and Stoper) Prepare the face and load the round for the mining cycle. Qualifications Minimum of 4000 hours operating bolting equipment in an underground mining environment Knowledge of ground support systems and their role in ensuring tunnel stability Ability to read and interpret mine plans and bolting specifications Strong attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining high safety standards Good physical condition, with the ability to work in confined underground spaces Excellent teamwork and communication skills Basic UG Hard Rock Common Core Ability to work in a safe and productive manner and to safely direct the activities of less skilled employees Working knowledge and skills in Development Mining Shotcrete/concrete/construction experience would be considered an asset Experience operating scooptrams, scissorlifts, and other underground equipment Ability to lift and physically handle material up to 50lbs Experience in installation of ground support. CC-343877.title: Health & Safety Coordinator
CC-343877.description: Job Summary Reporting to the Director, Health, Safety and Wellness, provides internal occupational health and safety support to Kettle worksites, and liaises with external stakeholders (regulators, third party contractors, etc.). Why This Role? Health and Safety at The Kettle is about people first. This is more than a compliance role. It's an opportunity to partner with passionate teams, build trusted relationships, and contribute to a workplace where people feel safe, supported, and empowered to do their best work. You'll help turn ideas into practical solutions that make a meaningful difference across the organization. If you're collaborative, curious, and energized by working with people to solve challenges, you'll feel at home here. Join us and be part of a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work has a lasting impact. Assist in the development and implementation of health and safety policies, procedures and programs. Conduct regular workplace inspections and audits to identify hazards and ensure compliance with safety regulations. Support incident investigations, including documentation, root cause analysis and corrective actions. Maintain accurate records of safety training, inspections, incidents and compliance reports. Coordinate and deliver safety orientations and training sessions for new and existing employees, third party contractors as needed. Participate in Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) Committee meetings and support committee activities. Monitor and ensure compliance with local and provincial health and safety legislation. Assist third parties (ergonomists, occupational therapists) with job site visits to review job duties as these relate to occupational hazards and/or disease. Promote a culture of safety through awareness campaigns and employee engagement initiatives Assist with emergency preparedness planning and drills. Qualifications: Education & Experience Diploma or Certificate in Health & Safety, Environmental Science, or related field. 0-2 years of experience in a health and safety role (co-op placements considered). Knowledge of relevant health and safety legislation (e.g. WorkSafe BC, OH&S regulations). Strong organizational and communication skills Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Powerpoint). Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Ability to travel between program sites as needed. Strong commitment to equity, inclusion and trauma-informed approaches. Preferred Qualifications Basic First Aid or Mental Health First Aid certification Experience working in social services, non-profit, or community-based organizations Valid BC Driver?s License Violence Prevention certification Food Safe certification Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Knowledge of policies, regulations and legislation governing occupational health and safety in British Columbia. Knowledge of other regulatory framework applicable to managing and operating supported housing and licensed care sites (bylaws, life and fire safety, food safety, tenant related regulations, etc.) An understanding of the psychological, physical and social aspects of working with adults with mental illness and those suffering(ed) from abuse, addiction, homelessness and recovery. Intermediate to advanced computer skills in Microsoft Office to include Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Physical ability to carry out the duties of the position. Additional Information This is a hybrid position, requiring a minimum of three days per week in-office at The Kettle Society?s East Vancouver headquarters and Taylor Manor, with up to two remote days per week if desired. The Kettle Society is committed to equity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. What We Offer A meaningful opportunity to support a mission-driven organization making a real difference in the lives of people living with mental illness. A collaborative environment with a passionate, committed team of professionals. Centrally located office in Vancouver, easily accessible by transit. Compensation The successful candidate will start at a rate between $54,623 and $64,864 per annum depending on qualifications, based on a 37.5-hour work week. This will be individually tailored to reflect your unique experience and qualifications as they relate to the role, along with internal equity. Comprehensive benefits package, including extended health and dental coverage, participation in the Municipal Pension Plan, and generous paid time off (vacation and compensatory leave). The Kettle Society is committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family status, or disability. We welcome qualified applicants with lived experience(s). Please do not contact the employer directly as only short-listed candidates will be contacted by our People & Culture Team. We appreciate your interest in our organization. Applications will be accepted until August 31, 2026. We will begin reviewing applications after August 31, 2026. Please include a cover letter with your resume as part of your application and apply through our website.

The incumbent is responsible for providing emotional support and case management; assisting clients to identify goals that will enhance their family's well-being; and supporting clients to develop strategies and access resources to realize those goals. Maintain rapport with local community resources to ensure effective referral options and contacts. Assist in the facilitation of education programs, workshops, group activities on scheduled topics related to life skills and so forth. Manage the distribution of care supplies to clients. Program Development (20%) Ongoing community engagement to ensure we reach our target audience. Work closely with the Vita Centre team to deliver services based on the needs of clients. Participate in liaison work with various schools, community agencies and the public to educate them on the services Vita Centre provides. Agency Responsibilities (20%) Compile monthly statistics on clients and generate monthly reports. Conduct semi-annual client satisfaction survey. Maintain up-to-date files on clients. Support student placements with learning opportunities. Network in the community and represent Vita Center at meetings and community events. Attend job specific training sessions offered within and outside of organization to enhance job skills and knowledge. Maintain current knowledge of and integrate best practice and current research evidence to support professional practice decisions and actions. Other duties as assigned Qualifications Degree in Social Work or related field. At least one year?s experience in human/social services (can include school placement experience). Client-centered, strength-based approach and ability to respect confidentiality. Sensitivity to issues around vulnerable parent populations. Knowledge of community resources. Excellent listening, communication and presentation skills. Well organized, able to work independently. Adaptable, flexible and resourceful. Proficient in Microsoft Office. Valid driver?s license, access to a reliable vehicle and relevant insurance. Vulnerable Sector Record Check (within the past six months) is required. Basic first aid/CPR certificate is an asset. Working conditions The job requires the incumbent to work both in the office and in the community. The job will require some travel to client residences, community events and off-site client meetings. Physical requirements The incumbent will have to spend long hours sitting and using office equipment and computers. The incumbent may also have to do some lifting of supplies and materials from time to time.

CC-344386.title: Relational Trauma Therapist
CC-344386.description: Who We Are At Toronto Relationship Clinic (TRC), we are experts in sexual harm and trauma recovery . We offer trauma-focused collaborative care for survivors of sexual abuse as well as other types of complex trauma. We also provide an intensive and structured treatment program for men who have sexually offended, whether or not charges have been laid. Our comprehensive framework for addressing sexual harm through a restorative and transformative justice lens prioritizes relationship and connection in a way that is protective and empowering for survivors while providing a framework for offenders to be held accountable. What We're Looking For We are seeking a relationally oriented, trauma-focused psychotherapist to join our clinical team. We are looking for top-notch clinicians who are passionate about mental health, trauma recovery, and transformative justice, and eager to join a growing collective. In this position, you will primarily work with individuals, couples, and families, providing general and trauma-focused psychotherapy. You may also be working with men who have perpetrated sexual harm or have been criminally charged with sexual offences, including offences against minors. This position can also include relational work with partners and families and/or survivors of sexual trauma. Working within an adult education framework, the instructor supports learners at OALCF levels 1?3 and applies strong instructional expertise in literacy, numeracy, and digital skills to facilitate meaningful skill development. Service delivery takes place in community partner locations and outreach settings, requiring responsiveness to rural realities and barriers such as transportation challenges, digital access limitations, housing and income instability, and social isolation. Develop individualized learning plans aligned with OALCF levels, learner goals, and employment, training, or education pathways. Demonstrate digital technology skills, reading, writing, and math proficiencies sufficient to develop curriculum and instruct adult learners within OALCF levels 1, 2, and 3. Facilitate 1:1 and group instruction using in-person, virtual, hybrid, and itinerant delivery models across North Durham. Deliver services in community partner and outreach locations, adapting to rural and geographically dispersed communities. Adapt instructional approaches, scheduling, and service delivery methods to meet the unique needs of rural and geographically dispersed communities. Select and adapt learning materials aligned with learner goals, OALCF principles, and community/labour market context. Contribute to continuous improvement by evaluating learner needs and outcomes, identifying community gaps, and then participate in developing and implementing program improvements. Maintain accurate case notes, learner plans, progress reports, and service user files in accordance with program standards. Ensure timely and accurate data entry and reporting using required systems and tools (e.g., Excel, CaMS). Provide relevant instruction based on the Ontario Adult Literacy Curriculum Framework (OALCF) levels 1?3. Able to work in an environment that requires the ability to collect and gather statistical information, meet deadlines, and achieve targets. Proficient in collection and data entry into spreadsheets (Excel) and online portals (CaMS). Maintain and complete monthly performance-related statistical reports as required. Contribute to program marketing and outreach activities and promote JHS training programs throughout the community. Represent the agency in the community when required. Facilitate and attend workshops, meetings, seminars, and community partner activities as requested. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Education & Certifications: Completed post secondary education in Education, Social Services or related field Experience: Teaching/tutoring experience and demonstrated understanding and application of the principles of adult education. Facilitation, instruction, employment counselling, motivational interviewing, , and client centered individual support and guidance experience. Experience delivering outreach, community-based, itinerant, or hybrid programming is considered an asset. Experience working within rural or geographically dispersed communities is considered an asset. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Demonstrated digital technology skills, reading, writing, and math proficiencies sufficient to develop curriculum and instruct adult learners within OALCF levels 1, 2, and 3. Sound understanding of Skills for Success and the OALCF framework, including goal paths, competencies, tasks, and levels of performance. Strong organizational and time management skills. Solid understanding of group dynamics and ability to motivate others. A strong understanding of adult learners? needs and circumstances. Extensive knowledge of labour market training opportunities and labour market information and resources. Proven experience working with diverse learner populations, including youth, newcomers, internationally trained professionals, OW, EI and ODSP recipients, individuals experiencing long-term unemployment, and persons with disabilities. Strong case management and assessment skills. Able to take initiative and work independently as well as collaboratively as part of a team. Knowledge of services related to adult literacy. Strong computer skills in a Windows environment using Office 365 applications, as well as knowledge of computerized learning software applications. Experienced in using Zoom to host/co-host meetings, including using polls, breakout rooms, and annotation mode. Familiarity with social media and digital communication platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Wordpress). Excellent written, verbal, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently within community-based and partner locations while maintaining strong communication with the broader team. Demonstrated adaptability, flexibility, and problem-solving skills within evolving community-based service environments. Understanding of barriers impacting rural populations, including transportation access, digital literacy, poverty, housing insecurity, and social isolation. Ability to build and maintain collaborative relationships with community partners and host organizations. Service delivery may occur at multiple community partner locations, outreach sites, and virtual platforms. From time to time, you may be required to work from the Oshawa site to provide coverage, support program needs, or participate in team-based activities and service coordination. A valid Ontario driver?s licence, access to reliable transportation, and the ability to travel throughout North Durham and surrounding communities are required. CC-345911.title: Communications Coordinator
CC-345911.description: British Columbia Council for International Cooperation Job Posting Communications Coordinator Location: This is a remote, work-from-home position based in the Lower Mainland that requires you to attend periodic in-person meetings, retreats and events, largely in Vancouver. Hours: 37.5 hours per week Start date: October 13, 2026 Pay: $67,000-71,000 a year Benefits: After 3 months of employment, extended health benefits are available Application deadline: September 7, 2026 at 11:59pm PT About Us At the British Columbia Council for International Cooperation (BCCIC), we believe that the way we work is as important as the work we do. BCCIC is a membership network that brings together civil society organizations and individuals committed to advancing global justice and contributing to a more just, equitable and sustainable world. Rooted in British Columbia and connected through relationships across Canada and around the world, our members and partners reflect a rich diversity of cultures, languages, histories, identities and ways of knowing. We believe this diversity is one of our greatest sources of learning, creativity and collective wisdom. As a membership organization, our role is to create the conditions for people and organizations to learn from one another, strengthen relationships, navigate complexity together and take collective action. Our team works in a culture of trust, responsibility, shared stewardship and continuous learning. We believe that strong systems support people, learning, collaboration and accountability. We encourage initiative, work across roles toward shared goals, and recognize that everyone contributes not only through their own work but also by helping strengthen the organization as a whole. About the Position The Communications Coordinator helps shape how BCCIC communicates with its members, partners and the broader public. At BCCIC, communications are woven throughout the organization rather than existing as a separate function. The Communications Coordinator works alongside colleagues to strengthen how BCCIC communicates in order to foster understanding, participation and dialogue?supporting member engagement, helping translate complex ideas into accessible language, coordinating communications across the organization, and ensuring that BCCIC's public voice reflects its mission, values and strategic priorities. The role is not simply about communicating BCCIC's work. It is about helping people understand one another, make meaning together and strengthen relationships across a diverse network. Success in this role depends as much on listening as on communicating, and as much on curiosity as on expertise. Our communications serve three interconnected purposes: strengthening relationships across our network, engaging the broader public, and contributing to conversations that advance global justice. Specific Duties: Manage BCCIC's communications to maintain a consistent, accessible, and engaging public presence across all communication channels. Create and manage communication assets and campaigns to support BCCIC initiatives, programs, events and promotions. Plan, write, schedule, and publish social media content while monitoring engagement and responding as appropriate. Maintain and update the BCCIC website to ensure information is current, accurate, and accessible. Coordinate the publication of communications across digital platforms to ensure timely and consistent messaging. Support member and public engagement through targeted communications, announcements, and promotional materials. Develop, write, edit, and distribute regular newsletters, member emails, and other communications. Develop communications that increase public understanding of BCCIC's work and encourage public engagement. Identify communication opportunities by gathering stories, program updates, member achievements, and organizational news for publication. Edit written content for clarity, accessibility, consistency, and alignment with BCCIC's brand and communications standards. Assist with administrative matters related to Communications and Engagement Assist with the planning, promotion, and delivery of public engagement activities, events, webinars, and other organizational initiatives. Provide communications support for events, including promotional campaigns, registration materials, and post-event communications. Monitor and manage the organization's general information inbox and voicemail, responding to inquiries or directing them to the appropriate staff member. Monitor for coherent communications and learning Monitor current events, sector developments, and relevant news to identify resources, stories, and opportunities for BCCIC to share with members and the public. Contribute to BCCIC's Planning, Monitoring, Learning and Accountability (PMLA) processes by documenting communications activities, capturing lessons learned, and advancing continuous improvement by integrating outcomes and metrics from communication initiatives into future iterations. Track communications metrics and engagement data to help evaluate the effectiveness of communications activities and inform future planning. Collaborate with staff, members, partners, and external stakeholders to gather content and support organizational communications. Perform other communications, administrative, and project-related duties as assigned to support the goals of the organization. Technical or Professional Experience Our ideal candidate has: Post-secondary degree in communications, public relations, social justice, international development or another related field Experience with intercultural communications and working collaboratively with diverse actors that may have different views, perspectives, priorities, or goals. 3-5 years of experience working in communications, media, or public relations, ideally experience with BC-based communities Demonstrated proficiency in WordPress, MailChimp, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, SEO, Google Suite, social media analytics, and social and emerging digital media platforms and tools Proven ability to establish and maintain positive, strategic working relationships with key stakeholders and decision-makers Excellent time management, decision making, organizational, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills Demonstrated self-starter who exhibits flexibility, creativity, and initiative Comfortable working with minimal supervision in a deadline-oriented environment Superior written, oral, and online communication skills Experience with public engagement through digital communications and social media Shows a keen attention to detail We May Be a Good Fit for Each Other If... You can work independently, ask good questions, make recommendations, keep our communications active while drawing on contributions from the rest of the team. You are systematic, organized, able to multi-task and accept that there are always moving pieces. You are curious about how people engage with information today and the emerging communications strategies, platforms, practices, and technologies. You understand the importance of timely, relevant and fit-for-purpose communications. You have an understanding of, and enthusiasm for, intercultural communication, with experience communicating with diverse communities and audiences. You enjoy making sense of complexity and are committed to learning with others. What You'll Bring We recognize that excellent candidates bring different combinations of education and experience. You may have experience in communications, journalism, public engagement, public affairs, nonprofit communications or a related field. Experience working with member-based organizations, networks, coalitions or collaborative initiatives will be considered a strong asset. You bring both professional expertise and the perspective that comes from your own lived experiences. We value people who have learned by navigating different contexts, communities, cultures, identities or ways of working, and who draw on those experiences with humility and curiosity. You combine maturity with imagination, understand both systems and relationships, and recognize that practice shapes systems just as much as systems shape practice. Ultimately, we're looking for someone who communicates with clarity, listens with curiosity, exercises good judgment, builds strong relationships, and is excited by the opportunity to help a diverse network learn, connect and act together. How the Team Works This is a full-time remote, work-from-home position based in the lower mainland that requires you to attend in person meetings occasionally. There is an expectation that staff be available for periodic in-person meetings, retreats and events, largely in Vancouver. Everyone at BCCIC, from interns to staff to Board of Directors, are accountable to BCCIC?s strategic directions, its vision, mission and purpose, as well as the Istanbul Principles. You can learn more about these here . We are a flexible, accommodating and supportive team that recognizes that we each work differently, have different needs, and that work is one of the many dimensions of our lives. Given that our team is lean, collaborative and dynamic, all staff are expected to be flexible with their roles and fulfill necessary administrative functions and other tasks deemed necessary What can you expect from the team? A welcoming, inclusive team that is open to difficult discussions and feedback. Experience working within a team that is learning to work in a feminist way, and is learning to use anti-oppressive, anti-racist and decolonized approaches in all aspects of our work, with an international lens. A dynamic group that wants to learn and grow with you. This is a full-time position based on 37.5 hours a week. The salary range for this position is $67,000-71,000 a year. Health insurance is available after 3 months. How to Apply We are accepting applications until September 7, 2026 at 11:59pm PT. The position will start October 13, 2026. To apply, please email BCCIC at info@bccic.ca a brief cover letter and your resume; please include the subject line: Communications Coordinator Application. BCCIC is committed to building a team that reflects the richness and diversity of the communities with whom we work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, cultures, languages and lived experiences, and from those whose life or work has required them to navigate different worlds with openness, curiosity and respect.

CC-346317.description: Service Navigation Coordinator ? Toronto (Full-Time) The Organization Spinal Cord Injury Ontario is an expert in the field of spinal cord injury (SCI) community services. Founded in 1945, SCI Ontario?s mission is to ?provide peer experiences, education, advocacy, and ongoing services for those impacted by spinal cord injuries.?. Our Vision: Individuals impacted by spinal cord injuries thriving. Job Summary As part of a dynamic provincial organization, the Service Navigation Coordinator provides coordination of services, active support, resources, and education. The position focuses on client centered goals and solutions to navigate system barriers that prevent persons with spinal cord injuries living the life they choose. This is an existing position and an active vacancy. The Service Navigation Coordinator position requires an innovative and resourceful individual to assist with serving clients in Toronto area. This full-time position is based out of the Toronto provincial office with travel throughout the community. The current work arrangement includes approximately three (3) days per week working on site at the office, with the remaining workdays varying based on client, community, and operational needs. JA British Columbia (JABC) is seeking an experienced Governance & Operations Coordinator to provide high-quality administrative and coordination support across governance, executive support, and internal operations. As part of JABC's Operations team, you will coordinate Board and Committee administration, support the President & CEO, help keep our downtown Vancouver office running smoothly, and assist the VP, Finance and Operations with recruiting, HR administration, and employee engagement activities, IT and equipment coordination. Responsibilities include: Board and Governance Coordination Coordinate the annual schedule and administration of Board and standing Committee meetings, including scheduling, room bookings, catering, virtual meeting arrangements, and other logistics. Coordinate annual reviews of Board and Committee work plans, Board and Committee surveys, the Board skills matrix, and agreed follow-up items. Support the planning, preparation, and documentation of operational and strategic planning sessions, including preparation of materials and meeting minutes. Research, prepare, format, and proofread reports, presentations, correspondence, and other materials as requested. Office Operations Coordinate day-to-day office administration and help maintain an organized, welcoming, well-equipped, and functional workplace. Purchase and monitor office supplies, equipment, and other routine operational items, and liaise with building management and office service providers. Maintain records for office access cards, keys, parking fobs, first-aid supplies, fire-safety requirements, and other workplace administration. Maintain an accurate inventory of JABC computers and other assigned property, coordinate equipment purchases and replacement needs, and ensure appropriate backup equipment is available. Coordinate routine IT setup, equipment, software, and approved user-access requirements with JABC's third-party IT service provider. Maintain assigned administrative records, the general info@jabc.org mailbox, and shared staff resources and information. HR Administration and Employee Support Provide administrative support for recruitment, including posting vacancies, organizing applications and recruitment files, and supporting hiring process logistics. Coordinate onboarding and offboarding activities, including forms, records, equipment, system setup, and employee orientation logistics. Provide administrative support for routine HR processes, maintaining confidentiality and escalating sensitive or complex HR matters to the VP, Finance and Operations. Employee Engagement and Internal Events Chair and coordinate the Employee Engagement Committee, including meetings, work plans, staff recognition activities, internal events, and follow-up on agreed actions. Administer the Employee Engagement Survey and coordinate the collection, collation, and reporting of results as directed. Other Tasks Maintain administrative procedures within the role's area of responsibility and identify and recommend practical improvements to processes, workflows, and staff experience. Provide general administrative support and perform other related duties as assigned by the VP, Finance and Operations. Qualifications Post-secondary degree, diploma, or certificate in business administration, office administration, nonprofit management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 3-5 years of progressively responsible administrative, executive support, office coordination, or similar experience. Demonstrated experience supporting senior leadership and/or Boards or Committees; direct Board or Committee support experience is strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience preparing meeting materials and recording clear, accurate meeting minutes. Strong proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint. Experience handling confidential information and coordinating multiple recurring deadlines and stakeholders with limited supervision. Experience in a nonprofit environment, familiarity with BC society governance. Experience with CRM databases, such as Salesforce, or HR systems, and IT/service vendor management are assets. Knowledge, Skills and Attributes Exceptional organizational skills and strong attention to detail. Strong initiative and ability to anticipate requirements, prioritize work, and follow through without frequent direction or reminders. Sound judgment, discretion, maturity, and diplomacy, particularly when working with Board members, senior leaders, and confidential information. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strong proofreading, editing, and document-formatting capabilities. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate professionally with a wide variety of internal and external stakeholders. Solid technical aptitude and ability to learn new systems, applications, and administrative processes quickly. Practical problem-solving skills and a continuous-improvement mindset. Positive, collaborative, and service-oriented approach, with a commitment to JABC and its values and mission. What You'll Love About Working at JABC A flexible, hybrid work model , with 2-3 days per week in our downtown Vancouver office. Extended benefits after three months, and RRSP contributions after four years of service. Three weeks' vacation to start. Mission-driven culture , a high-performing and collaborative team, and the opportunity to take real ownership of your work. An opportunity to do meaningful work and contribute to programs that make a tangible difference in the lives of young people across British Columbia. Compensation This is a full-time position (37.5 hours/week, Monday to Friday). The salary range for this position is $58,000-$63,000 per year , commensurate with experience and internal equity. An offer of employment is conditional upon successful completion of reference and criminal record checks (including vulnerable sector screening), in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. We welcome and encourage individuals from Indigenous backgrounds, racialized communities, persons with disabilities, and individuals of any sexual orientation or gender identity to apply. Your passion and potential are what matter most. If you require any accommodation during the recruitment and selection process, please contact us at HR@jabc.org , so we can offer you individualized assistance and ensure equity in our process. Applications will be reviewed as received until the position is filled.
