Closing date : Sep 18, 2026 Compensation: $62,000 to $68,000 (depending on experience) About Neighbours United Neighbours United is a community-driven charity that brings people together in rural, small, and suburban areas to support policies that defend the people and places we love. Through strategic campaigns using engagement organizing, deep canvassing, and communications, we are shifting hearts and minds in places often left out of progressive movements. By centering personal stories we broaden public support beyond the usual environmental base. We focus on areas and audiences that are frequently written off. We invest in real conversations that matter to people. We are known for our deep canvassing based approach: listening, leading with personal stories, and creating space for people to wrestle with real tensions. Rather than broadcasting messages, we create conversations that allow people to reflect, connect, and act. About the Role Oil and gas companies sign agreements to clean up the wells they leave behind. When they walk away instead, the cleanup doesn?t disappear. It lands on the public and on the people who live closest to the well, while the companies that made the mess post record profits. Neighbours United is starting a campaign to change that. We?re looking for a Campaign Organizer to build public pressure in one rural community resulting in the decision makers publicly saying that oil and gas needs to clean up its mess. You Will: Create a campaign that guides community members step-by-step from initial awareness to active civic involvement. Starting with petitions and letters to decision makers and progressing to meetings with their decision-makers or leadership roles like event hosting, community outreach, and public speaking Work with our Communications Director on strategic outreach that puts public pressure on selected targets Recruit, train, and coach a core team of committed volunteer leaders - leadership development takes priority over mass activity Develop and drive a regional escalation strategy focused on mapping how everyday people can force big oil and gas companies to ?clean up their mess?, identifying and tracking the opinions of power holders on this issue Prepare volunteers for meetings with political representatives and coordinate targeted letter and email pushes to those decision-makers - integrating political pressure into every stage of the program Maintain existing partnerships, and build new ones, with allied organizations and coalition partners already working on this issue Engage respectfully with Indigenous Nations Provide regular metric-based updates to the Organizing Director, measuring success by political outcomes and durable volunteer relationships, not organizing volume alone Contribute to campaign learning documentation, support grassroots fundraising, and uphold Neighbours United's mission and team-first values Oversee allocation, tracking, and reporting for the Polluters Pay campaign budget, ensuring all expenditures align with organizational guidelines and grant requirements Maintain clean, reliable campaign data in organizing tools (e.g., CRMs/databases) to track volunteer journeys, engagement metrics, and outreach lists You Should Apply If You Are: Mission-aligned and deeply motivated by helping everyday people have a stronger voice in decisions that affect the people and places they love Knowledgeable about local dynamics, with an understanding of Alberta?s political, social, and community landscape Caring and community-minded, knowing how to listen deeply to local perspectives and excited to coach people to step into their own power You?re comfortable being the only staff person in the room. You don?t need a big team to get things done A communicator who interacts with clarity, empathy, and professionalism across all audiences Campaign-minded, ideally with experience volunteering on a campaign, organizing locally, or navigating policy issues (a strong asset, though transferable community leadership counts too!) Experienced in developing volunteers into leaders who take on real responsibility Able to take independent ownership of your work, managing your time effectively and driving projects forward in a remote work setting without needing step-by-step supervision Highly organized and able to manage logistics, oversee a budget, and keep track of data Experienced in building strong collaborations and organizational partnerships Aligned with Neighbours United's values: fairness, transparency, and building community first We know great organizers come from all kinds of backgrounds. If you don't check every box above but you know how to build real relationships and grow people into leaders, we want to hear from you. Compensation and Benefits: Neighbours United is a Living Wage Employer. Alongside purpose-driven work in a supportive environment, we offer: 10 paid sick days, pro-rated 6 weeks of paid time off, including four weeks vacation, and paid time off during our August and January office closures, pro-rated (If needed) technology hardware provided Paid statutory holidays for staff who have worked 15 of the previous 30 days, including Boxing Day and Easter Monday, with additional consideration for days of cultural or religious significance Paid time for Leadership Training, for Organizational Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Training, and other professional development Extended health benefits Annual raises for cost of living and performance How To Apply Send a letter answering the question ?how are you personally impacted by the issue of Alberta's multi-billion dollar well cleanup crisis ?? along with your CV to jessica@neighboursunited.org . CC-347894.title: High School Physics Tutor
CC-347894.description: High School Physics Tutor Vector Learning Co. | Part-Time Employee | Remote + Monthly In-Person Filming | $40/hour Vector Learning Co. is hiring a High School Physics Tutor to join our growing team for the 2026?2027 school year. We provide personalized, one-on-one tutoring for Ontario high school students, helping them genuinely understand physics, strengthen their problem-solving skills, and approach unfamiliar questions with confidence. We are looking for someone with a strong physics background who can do more than calculate the correct answer. The ideal tutor can identify why a student is struggling, explain concepts in multiple ways, and help students develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical skills needed to solve problems independently. Courses Applicants should be confident tutoring the following Ontario high school science and physics courses: Grade 9 Science (SNC1W) Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) Grade 11 Physics (SPH3U) Grade 12 Physics (SPH4U) Applicants should be comfortable teaching topics such as kinematics, dynamics, forces, energy, momentum, waves, electricity, magnetic fields, and gravitational fields. Responsibilities One-on-one tutoring Provide engaging, personalized online tutoring sessions to Ontario high school students. Explain physics concepts clearly, accurately, and intuitively. Support students with homework, assignments, test preparation, and exam preparation. Teach students how to interpret problems, identify relevant information, select appropriate equations, and justify their solutions. Help students understand the reasoning behind physics formulas rather than simply memorizing equations. Identify gaps in student understanding and adapt explanations accordingly. Strengthen students? confidence with the mathematical skills required for physics, including algebra, trigonometry, graphing, and vectors. Help students make connections between physics concepts and real-world applications. Arrive prepared and on time for scheduled sessions. Maintain a supportive, professional, and encouraging learning environment. Educational content creation Educational social media content is an important part of Vector Learning Co.?s growth and student outreach. Tutors in this position will: Prepare and record approximately five short-form educational physics videos per month. Participate in one paid monthly filming session in downtown Toronto, typically on the first Friday of each month unless otherwise agreed upon. Create curriculum-relevant content, including mini-lessons, common mistakes, practice questions, problem-solving strategies, demonstrations, and exam tips. Explain physics concepts clearly, confidently, and naturally on camera. Prepare assigned topics and questions before filming. Collaborate with Vector Learning Co. on content ideas and educational accuracy. Vector Learning Co. manages editing, branding, captions, and publishing. Tutors are not required to post content on their personal social media accounts. Required content creation time is compensated. Qualifications The ideal candidate: Has a strong academic background in physics, engineering, physical sciences, physics education, or a related field. Has excellent knowledge of Ontario high school physics and is confident teaching the courses listed above. Is familiar with the Ontario Grade 9?12 science and physics curriculum. Can explain challenging concepts in simple, intuitive ways. Has strong mathematical skills and can help students apply algebra, trigonometry, graphing, and vectors to physics problems. Is patient, engaging, and encouraging with students. Adapts explanations to individual learning needs. Has excellent verbal communication skills. Is comfortable appearing on camera. Is professional, organized, and reliable. Has a reliable internet connection and an appropriate environment for online tutoring. Can attend monthly in-person filming sessions in downtown Toronto. Previous tutoring or teaching experience is strongly preferred. Availability Tutoring primarily takes place during after-school, evening, and weekend hours. Applicants should be available to work throughout the 2026?2027 academic year, from September through June, and maintain reasonably consistent weekly availability. The anticipated commitment is approximately 4?8 tutoring hours per week to start, with opportunities for additional hours based on student demand and tutor availability. Location Tutoring sessions are conducted remotely. Monthly educational content is filmed in person in downtown Toronto. Compensation $40 per hour for one-on-one tutoring. Required training and monthly educational content creation are compensated separately. Part-time employee position. Opportunities for additional tutoring hours as Vector Learning Co. grows. Application process Selected candidates will complete: Application and resume review. A short virtual interview. A teaching demonstration using Ontario high school physics. A short educational video or camera demonstration. A reference check. To apply, please submit your resume and a brief introduction outlining your tutoring experience, the Ontario science and physics courses you are comfortable teaching, and your general weekly availability. We are looking for someone who is not only excellent at physics but also excels at teaching it. If you love helping students succeed and value flexible, meaningful work, we would love to hear from you.

CC-348047.title: Project Development and coordinator
CC-348047.description: Sina Homes is seeking a post-secondary student to support the planning, estimating, procurement, and coordination of residential construction projects in Calgary. The student will work directly with the project team and gain practical experience across the full construction project lifecycle, from pre-construction through active construction and closeout. Key responsibilities will include reviewing architectural and consultant drawings, assisting with quantity take-offs and cost estimates, obtaining and comparing subcontractor and supplier quotations, maintaining project budgets and cost tracking, assisting with construction schedules, coordinating with trades and consultants, preparing project documentation, tracking procurement and outstanding items, and supporting site progress reviews. The student will also assist with project administration, including maintaining project records, tracking invoices and commitments against budgets, preparing progress updates, documenting changes, and helping identify cost, schedule, and procurement risks. The position provides hands-on exposure to residential construction management, estimating, design coordination, procurement, budgeting, scheduling, and site operations. The student will work closely with experienced construction professionals and will have the opportunity to apply concepts learned in their post-secondary program to active residential projects.

CC-348391.title: Mentoring Coordinator - 1:1 Mentoring Programs
CC-348391.employer: Big Sisters of BC Lower Mainland
CC-348391.description: A proud member of Big Brothers Big Sisters Canada Federation Mentoring Coordinator ? 1:1 Mentoring Programs Job Posting Mission, Vision and Core Values Our Mission is to enable life-changing mentoring relationships to ignite the power and potential of young people. Our Vision is that all young people realized their full potential. Our Core Values are: We Champion Potential Every Connection Counts Showing Up Matters Big Sisters of BC Lower Mainland ( www.bigsisters.bc.ca) is a non-profit society and proud member of Big Brothers Big Sisters of Canada Federation. We are committed to enhancing the confidence, selfesteem and well-being of self-identified girls and youth who identify as non-binary, trans, and Two Spirit. Big Sisters of BC Lower Mainland is a leader in mentoring youth and providing ongoing support through a variety of engaging programs. Our organization is committed to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion and ongoing learning towards creating a more equitable society. We encourage applications from those who identify as Indigenous, a person of colour, 2SLGBTQIA+, a person with a disability, or a member of another community that experiences additional barriers. Join us and make a positive difference in the lives of others in the community. Why it?s great to work with us: Big Sisters is a friendly, inclusive and committed team who offers their employees up to fifteen vacation days and wellbeing days, and up to three personal days, in the first year of employment. We provide a generous employer-paid extended health care and benefits package, including prescription drugs and dental plan. We also offer our employees a professional development allocation and various learning opportunities. Ignite your full potential with Big Sisters! Is this you? You are an energetic, responsible, and positive person with a strong commitment to our mission. You are passionate about mentoring girls, non-binary youth, and transgender youth who are looking for support from an additional caring and trusted adult in their lives. You take pride in building strong client relationships and supporting each match so they can work towards helping the Mentee achieve their goals and boost their self-esteem. You have strong case management skills and understand the importance of ensuring safe and healthy mentoring relationships between volunteer mentors and our Mentees (ages 7-17). About this role: Reporting to the Director of Programs, the Mentoring Coordinator initiates, facilitates, supports, and monitors the mentoring relationship between a youth (the ?Little? or ?Mentee?) in need of academic support and an adult volunteer (the ?Big Sister? or ?Mentor? ). CC-348397.title: Child and Family Social Worker
CC-348397.description: About Sojourn House Sojourn House provides Emergency Shelter and Transitional Housing services to newly arrived refugees coming from all parts of the world. We provide a safe place and an inclusive environment to people who have had the refugee experience. We are dedicated to providing the best possible settlement services and programs that help residents transition and integrate into the community. With decades of experience and being one of the first refugee housing facilities in Toronto, we take pride in being a leading organization in refugee care Why This Role Matters As the Child and Family Social Worker, you will provide settlement programs and services to refugee families and their children within our Emergency Family Shelter and, as needed, as they transition into the community. Working from an integrated anti-racism, access and equity framework, you will provide effective interventions and coordinated case management, while connecting children and families with programs, services and community supports. What you?ll do Plan and deliver trauma-informed individual and group counselling, programs and supports for refugee children and families. Complete intake, assessments and case plans, and provide coordinated case management throughout families? stay and transition into the community. Connect families with schools, childcare, settlement services and other community resources, including supporting applications and referrals. Advocate for children and parents, including school outreach, meetings, accompaniment and follow-up support as needed. Design and facilitate child and family programming, including after-school, life-skills, educational, recreational and parenting programs. Identify service gaps, contribute to program planning and evaluation, and support the development of new program initiatives. Maintain accurate and timely case files, case notes, service statistics, program records and required reports. Build collaborative relationships with community partners, schools, service networks and coalitions, and represent Sojourn House through outreach and community engagement. Mentor and support student placements and volunteers. Identify and communicate program risks and concerns. What You?ll Need A Bachelor?s degree in Social Work and membership in good standing with the Ontario College of Social Workers and Social Service Workers (OCSWSSW). 3+ years of practical experience in child and family service programs. Knowledge of refugee children and families, the refugee determination and settlement process, and the complex issues that may affect individuals and families who have experienced trauma. Knowledge of child development, child and family services legislation, social work practices and ethics. Experience with case management, case coordination, crisis intervention, and individual, group and family counselling. Knowledge of and ability to apply an integrated anti-racism, access and equity framework in your work. Strong analytical, problem-solving, conflict-resolution and issue-management skills. Knowledge of community networks and resources, with the ability to work effectively with trained interpreters. Proficiency with computers and digital communication tools. What to expect A hands-on role combining counselling, case management, advocacy, programming and community outreach. Regular interaction with refugee children and families navigating complex settlement, adjustment and support needs. Work primarily in an office/shelter environment, with some work in schools, community organizations and other non-standard workplaces as required. A role requiring compassion, sound professional judgment, strong boundaries and the ability to respond effectively to challenging situations. Monday to Friday, 7.5 hours per day, based on a set schedule. What We Offer Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including life insurance, AD&D, short- and long-term disability, and employee and family assistance supports. Group RRSP with employer contributions. Paid vacation with increased entitlement based on years of service. Up to 18 paid sick days per year Paid Float Days after one year of continuous service Sojourn House thanks all applicants but will contact only qualified candidates selected for interviews In accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code, Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, a request for accommodation will be accepted throughout the hiring process. Interview candidates are required to provide their accommodation needs at least three business days before the assessment date. Sojourn House is committed to employment equity and encourages applicants from all equity seeking groups.

Provide program expertise, stories, and outcomes to support fundraising proposals, reports, and donor communications led by the Fundraising team, and participate in donor/funder meetings as appropriate. CC-350576.title: Clinical Manager
CC-350576.description: Role Overview As the Clinical Manager, you will be a member of FIREFLY's Leadership Team and play a central role in overseeing clinical services for children and youth. You will support a team of professionals, guide program delivery, and work collaboratively across the organization and community to strengthen services and outcomes. Key Responsibilities Provide leadership and oversight to clinical professionals and support staff. Manage day-to-day service delivery, programs, and clinical operations. Portfolio will have a focus in diagnostic services. Promote service excellence by monitoring performance and implementing strategic improvements and leading a team of dedicated clinicians and staff, promoting professional growth and clinical excellence. Support staff through coaching, supervision, training, and performance review. Foster a collaborative, supportive team culture that encourages innovation and problem-solving. Ensure clinical and service data is accurate, meets Ministry requirements, and supports quality decision-making. Participate in agency-wide service planning and contribute to FIREFLY's strategic priorities. Collaborate with Leadership Team members and community partners to enhance service coordination and access. Represent FIREFLY in community partnerships and system planning initiatives as required. Ensure compliance with agency policies, procedures, and applicable legislation. Effectively manage complex, sensitive clinical and operational situations. Lead and manage the delivery of services across our regional service area. Foster a culture of continuous improvements and client-centered care. Support integrated, cross-program service delivery through collaborative planning and partnership development. Represent FIREFLY in community planning tables and initiatives that enhance access to services for children and youth. Perform other duties as required. Qualifications Master's degree in a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience. 7-10 years of experience in child and youth development services or related areas. 3-5 years of progressive leadership experience. Professional registration with a relevant regulatory body (preferred). Skills & Competencies Strong team leadership, supervision and conflict resolution skills. Proven ability to support data-informed service planning and quality improvement. Demonstrated proficiency in FIREFLY's Management Competency Framework, including Client Focus, Emotional Intelligence, and Results Oriented. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and support evidence-based decision-making. Sound judgment, diplomacy, and ability to manage complex and sensitive situations. Ability to manage competing priorities, deadlines, and a high volume of work. Commitment to fostering a positive, inclusive and collaborative work environment. Understanding of relevant legislation, standards, and best practices in children's developmental health. Understanding of trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and client-centered care. Excellent organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Conditions of Employment Clear Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screen. Ability to manage a reasonable workload with effective prioritization and follow-up. Commitment to professionalism, teamwork, and quality service. Ability to manage conflict, mediate, and support problem-solving. Commitment to promoting and following FIREFLY's health and safety practices. Travel within the FIREFLY service region is required; some evening and weekend work may be required from time to time. Benefits Make a meaningful difference in the lives of children, youth, and families. Be part of a collaborative team that values innovation, wellness, and continuous learning. Enjoy professional development opportunities and a supportive leadership culture. Receive a competitive compensation and benefits package including: HOOPP pension 4 weeks vacation entitlement to start, plus paid holiday closure between Christmas and New Year's Paid sick leave Comprehensive benefit plan covering health, dental, vision, travel, life insurance, and critical illness insurance. CC-350579.title: Subcontracts Coordinator
CC-350579.description: The Subcontracts Coordinator is responsible for sourcing, evaluating, negotiating, awarding, and administering construction trade contracts for multi-family residential projects throughout Western and Central Canada. Working closely with site staff, Project Coordinators, Construction, Design, Quality Control, Estimating, Purchasing, and other project stakeholders, this role ensures qualified trades are engaged with clear scope, cost, schedule, and performance expectations. The successful candidate will combine strong construction knowledge, commercial judgment, negotiation skills, and relationship management to support competitive procurement, contract compliance, cost control, schedule performance, and successful project delivery. Your contributions to the team: Source, recruit, and qualify new and existing subcontractors in current and emerging project regions using industry networks, referrals, online research, direct outreach, supplier relationships, and site visits. Manage the tendering process for assigned trade scopes, including reviewing project plans, Site Instructions and scope requirements; establishing tender lists; issuing complete tender packages; and confirming schedule, manpower, duration, and project requirements with bidders. Review and analyze subcontractor bids against project budgets, historical pricing, scope requirements, inclusions, exclusions, assumptions, unit rates, schedule commitments, and overall project risk. Negotiate competitive pricing, contract terms, payment terms, scope clarifications, manpower commitments, durations, material lead times, and other commercial requirements to maximize SPD's financial and operational performance. Prepare clear bid analyses and contract award recommendations, complete required due diligence, and coordinate the contract award process in accordance with SPD authorization requirements. Define and communicate complete scopes of work, inclusions/exclusions, clarifications, payment schedules, phase codes, schedule expectations, and contract requirements before subcontractors mobilize to site. Coordinate with Project Coordinators and site teams to ensure subcontractor start dates, durations, manpower, sequencing, and milestone commitments align with the project schedule. Administer assigned subcontract agreements throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring contract changes are captured through timely and accurate Change Orders and supporting documentation. Evaluate subcontractor pricing for changes and extras, validate scope entitlement, negotiate cost and schedule impacts, and prepare Change Order approval packages within established timelines. Support subcontractor performance management by reviewing contract requirements, schedules and site records; communicating performance concerns; obtaining corrective commitments or recovery plans; and assisting with formal contractual escalation when required. Work collaboratively with Site Superintendents, Construction Managers, Project Coordinators, Quality Control, Safety, Design, Estimating, Purchasing, Accounts Payable, and other stakeholders to resolve subcontractor issues and maintain project momentum. Maintain accurate subcontractor, tender, bid analysis, award, contract, Change Order, WCB/WSIB, insurance, reference, and related records in SPD systems. Build and maintain professional, productive relationships with subcontractors and industry partners while balancing collaboration with accountability to SPD's safety, quality, cost, schedule, and contractual expectations. Attend required project meetings and provide timely input on tendering, contract awards, subcontractor availability, commercial risks, and trade performance. Support the preparation of Construction Execution Plans by identifying realistic tender and award timelines for assigned trade scopes. Perform other Subcontracts coordination duties as required to support project and departmental objectives. What you need to be successful: Post-secondary education in construction management, business, engineering technology, a skilled trade, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Experience in construction procurement, subcontract administration, estimating, project coordination, or a related construction role; multi-family residential and wood-frame construction experience is an asset. Working knowledge of construction drawings, scopes of work, tendering, bid analysis, subcontract agreements, payment schedules, Change Orders, and project schedules. Demonstrated ability to analyze pricing, identify scope gaps and commercial risks, compare bids to budgets and historical costs, and negotiate effectively with subcontractors. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the confidence to clearly communicate expectations, resolve issues, and hold subcontractors accountable to contractual commitments. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills with a collaborative approach to working across site, project, design, estimating, purchasing, and subcontractor teams. High attention to detail with strong critical thinking, problem-solving, analytical, and organizational skills. Ability to manage multiple trade scopes, competing priorities, deadlines, and project requirements in a fast-paced construction environment. Proactive and decisive, with the ability to follow issues through to resolution and escalate appropriately when performance, cost, quality, or schedule is at risk. Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with construction management, estimating, tendering, or ERP software is an asset. What we offer: Employees enjoy a wide range of benefits and competitive reward. You will be eligible to receive salary starting from $56,800 to $71,000 per annum, this will be determined by your skill set, education and experience. You will also be eligible to participate in the Company?s benefits program covering: Employer paid extended health, vision, and dental coverage (including family) Employee and Family Assistance Program Employee Referral Program Yearly health and wellness benefit RPP eligibility after 1 year Employee recognition program In-house professional development opportunities Why Seymour Pacific? Seymour Pacific Developments is an industry leader in building multi-family homes with unparalleled speed and efficiency. We develop and build over 1000 units a year by leveraging effective teamwork and industry expertise. We offer excellent wages and benefits, as well as a variety of training for employees who are motivated to succeed and want to expand their horizons. Seymour Pacific Developments practices equal opportunity hiring and onboarding processes to ensure equal access and participation for everyone. We understand that we have a responsibility for ensuring a safe, dignified, and welcoming environment and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees irrespective of race, colour, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by law. We believe in integrating people with disabilities into our workforce by removing barriers and meeting accessibility needs.

CC-350625.title: Donor Relations and Operations Coordinator
CC-350625.description: OVERVIEW Seva Canada restores sight and prevents blindness in low- and middle-income countries. Since 1982, Seva Canada donors, together with our partners, have given over 5 million people the power of sight through life-changing surgeries and have provided eye care services to millions more. Vision loss results in a staggering global economic productivity loss of US$ 411 billion annually. However, correcting vision loss can significantly boost economic opportunities, alleviate poverty, and promote gender equity. We work with local partners to create sustainable eye care programs that achieve long-term change, are culturally sensitive and reach those most in need ? women, children and people living in extreme poverty and isolation. Everything we do at Seva Canada, from training to providing supplies to conducting research and funding surgery, glasses and medicine, is for one reason: to provide communities with access to high-quality eye care that will restore sight and prevent blindness, now and in the future. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Operations and Finance, the Donor Relations and Operations Coordinator supports the Seva Canada team by ensuring donors feel welcome when they contact Seva Canada and have a good donor experience, and that every interaction is positive, helpful, and informative. The Donor Relations and Operations Coordinator also assists with activities related to operations and raising funds. Seva Canada is a dog friend office that offers a hybrid work environment and a supportive, close-knit team where curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn are valued. CORE ACCOUNTABILITIES Donor Relations Serves as the first point of contact for donors ? whether they reach out in person, by phone, through social media, via webform, or by email to the general inbox ? and responds promptly and warmly to each inquiry; Is responsible for all activities related to donation processing: accurately enters donations into the database, generates receipts in accordance with established processes; emails/mails receipts to donors in a timely manner; Maintains the database of donors, updating information about donors as requested by the donor, the Seva Canada team, and/or our fundraising agency; Prepares and sends donor mailings such as catalogues, planned giving program surveys and brochures, new donor welcome packages, annual reports, requests for donations and tribute cards; Makes thank you calls to donors at a defined level of giving as assigned by the Donor Relations and Operations Manager or Philanthropy team, following the thank you call script; Reads day-to-day correspondence from donors, responding to donor requests and/or forwarding them as needed to the appropriate person or department for follow up; Manages Seva's volunteer portfolio from end to end, including recruiting, vetting, and onboarding new volunteers, and maintaining the volunteer roster. Coordinates ongoing volunteer activities for both in-office and remote volunteers ? scheduling shifts, preparing the workstation for in-office volunteers, and ensuring each volunteer has clear task instructions along with the resources and information needed to complete them. Fundraising Support Uses databases and donor lists to help identify potential new supporters of Seva Canada and provides this information to the Philanthropy Director to assess and potentially pursue; Supports the management of Seva Canada's legacy and monthly giving, helping to steward relationships and maintain accurate records of legacy and monthly donors and their intentions; Formats tailored funding proposals, individual donor program reports, and presentations for a variety of audiences using written content provided by various departments; Helps facilitate donor touchpoints by preparing donor communications, including acknowledgment letters, updates, and other correspondence that keep donors informed and engaged; Performs prospect research on new and potential supporters of Seva Canada following the direction of the philanthropy team. Operations Support Maintains general office upkeep (cleaning, repairs, equipment) and keeps an adequate inventory of office supplies; Formats and compiles slide decks for internal and external meetings, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and professional presentation; Under the supervision of a senior staff member, supports organizing logistics for Board meetings, AGMs, and off-site staff meetings and events, including venue and catering coordination, volunteer scheduling, and event day set-up/clean-up; Provides administrative support to the Program Director, Operations including compiling and entering data from program partners for use in reports such as the Annual Report and funder/grant reports; Provides general administrative support to the Executive Director, as needed. Team Collaboration Attends biweekly team meetings; Collaborates with the team to prepare and host organization-wide events, ensuring excellent experiences for Seva donors; Provides light assistance or support for various team members, such as scheduling, setting up and sending polls; set up and clean-up of meetings; organizing collateral, general office organization and running off-site errands; Other duties and projects as required. Decision Making Authority Uses good judgement to make day-to-day decisions within established procedures and processes, under the supervision of the Donor Relations and Operations Manager. Supervision Direct reports include: N/A QUALIFICATIONS Minimum of 2 years? experience in a similar role with proven experience in donor relations, fundraising, and/or customer service; Strong time management, planning, and organization skills with ability to multi-task when required; Detail oriented & able to adhere to, and maintain, administrative procedures; Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint Excel, etc); Strong written and oral communication skills; Works well with a team and independently; A professional and outgoing manner with the ability to interact tactfully and diplomatically with a wide variety of people; Ability to take direction, positively respond to constructive feedback, and accurately follow instructions; Flexibility to work evenings and weekends on occasion; Able to travel within Canada and internationally to places where Seva Canada works. Assets Experience in operations/administration, volunteer management, or nonprofit sector; Experience using donor databases such as Virtuous or other CRM products; Experience with digital design tools such as Canva, Affinity or Adobe Creative Suite; Interest in international development and learning how a small-to-medium charity operates.

CC-350626.title: Facilitator, Governing Strike Body
CC-350626.description: Facilitator, Governing Strike Body Position Summary: The Facilitator of the Governing Strike Body, will develop a team of students to undertake the planning, actions, research, and information synthesis, relating to a Student Strike to combat egregious tuition increases. The Facilitator will attend meetings with external partners of Students Against Austerity at both a provincial and national level, to coordinate strike actions with other campuses. This role will additionally attend worker/union rights events, provincial and national union councils, provide updates, author tentative motions, and facilitate the creation/distribution of protest materials and strike safety information to the Governing Strike Body. Anticipated Start Date: September 21, 2026 Reports to: Manager of HR and Admin, OCAD Student Union Board of Directors Board Liaison: Executive Director of Campaigns and Advocacy Supervises: A team of students from OCAD University, to be developed after on-boarding to the role. The team will be composed of individuals with great passion for the Student Strike Movement. Pay Scale & Hours of Work $22 per hour, on contract in accordance with the OCAD University semester turnover. Opportunity to renew contract. This role would undertake 10 to 20 hours of work per week, with the prior understanding that weeks preceding and including strike events will expect more hands-on work than the average day-to-day. Responsibilities: This role is meant to facilitate the student strike by acting as the point person that liaises between the strike governing body and any other parties involved. The Facilitator is not in command of the Strike Body, but helping to facilitate it in an organized and engaging way, ensuring the responsibilities within are equitably tackled by all parties. They will bring information to the strike body to help them make informed decisions. They will also communicate the demands of the Governing Strike Body to external partners. This will help support the strike movement overall by meeting with the assembly, meeting with student groups, coordinating spaces with the university, and coordinating allies outside of the OCAD community. They will synthesize input from many parties to help facilitate the strike. 65% - Community Outreach, Campaign Building Phase 1: Community outreach- the facilitator will perform community outreach through organizing OCAD community events and reaching out to specific interest individuals to begin forming the Governing Strike Body. The main focus of phase 1 is recruiting a diverse group of students who are interested in fighting back against the OSAP changes and curious about pursuing the method of student striking. Possible community events could include townhalls, community potlucks or picnics, movie screenings, informational sessions, tabling at related or adjacent events in solidarity and with Students Against Austerity and more. The facilitator is responsible for coordinating these events, properly budgeting and presenting them to the Board of Directors beforehand. The facilitator is also responsible for coordinating with provincial Students Against Austerity, showing up to their events for outreach, and staying up to date with the group via their Signal chat and bi-weekly calls, reporting back to the Board of Directors with any important information. The facilitator will be asked to create a pamphlet or zine to better explain the Governing Strike Body to students upon recruiting, stating what the group is and how to be involved. Phase 2: Facilitation and coordination- once the Governing Strike Body is formed, the facilitator will facilitate assemblies with the group to get consensus on important items such as budgeting. The facilitator will take note of individual opinions and author motions that are reflective of the group consensus to bring back to the Body to vote on. Once passed, the facilitator will bring these motions to the Board of Directors for final approval. The facilitator will lead the Body in their initiative to promote the student strike through class talks, workshops, banner drops, art builds and more by doing the organizational backend work and reporting back to the Board. The facilitator will be responsible for coordinating, organizing and tabling alongside the Body, speaking to students directly to help inform them of the current situation. Additionally the facilitator will support training such as de-escalation for the student body to prepare for striking activities. 25% - Building Community Knowledge The facilitator will also be responsible for aiding the Executive Director of Campaigns and Advocacy in any student funding related actions and training. The facilitator must write updated reports of ongoing activities and initiatives. The facilitator may need to work to create fundraising opportunities for the Governing Strike Body. 10% - Active Student Support Striking days: for actual striking days, the facilitator will be expected to help lead the picket, support and advocate for students and their safety throughout the duration of the strike. The facilitator must be comfortable in possible high-stress situations. Qualifications Excellent in self-led role management, ability to work independently with some support Experience in community outreach including but not limited to nonprofit work, volunteer work and student advocacy work around political initiatives Experience in picketing, workers rights, unionization, etc. Excellent at synthesizing information and leading the creation of engaging hand-outs including; zines, pamphlets, and educational materials Experience in facilitation with excellent leadership skills, able to facilitate assemblies, note opinions, get consensus and hold a vote (then report back to SU board of directors) Friendly, sociable and able to canvas to involve more students in the movement Passionate and knowledgeable about Ontario Provincial Government Advocacy and preserving student funding (OSAP bursaries vs OSAP loans) Commitment to the student strike tactic Ideally an OCAD student and connected with the student body Prior training in harm reduction, Event Safety and Conflict Descalation, and/or First Aid and CPR considered a strong asset.

CC-350695.title: Exploration Supervisor
CC-350695.description: Position Overview Reporting to the Exploration General Supervisor, you will be part of the Ontario Regional Exploration team. You will be actively involved in planning and running programs, turning data into decisions in real time. You will ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle's values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment. Key Responsibilities Plan and deliver exploration programs (drilling, mapping, sampling, geophysics), adapting to field conditions and results in real time. Lead field teams and contractors, setting clear expectations and maintaining safe, efficient, and well-organized programs. Mentor and develop geologists, and students through coaching, feedback, and hands-on support. Integrate geological, geochemical, and geophysical data to refine models, generate targets, and support project advancement. Contribute to building and advancing the exploration pipeline through sound technical interpretation and decision-making. Prepare internal and technical reports, as well as scope of work and request for proposal documents. Prepare results from ongoing exploration activities for corporate reports and quarterly updates. Maintain strong sampling, analytical, and QA/QC practices to support reliable data and interpretations. Communicate results, plans, and recommendations clearly through reporting and ongoing discussions with the broader team. Promote and support Agnico Eagle's Health, Safety, Environmental, and Cultural standards across all activities. Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Geology or Geological Engineering; Postgraduate education is considered an asset. Registered as a Professional Geologist (P.Geo.). More than 7 years of mineral exploration experience, including field programs and diamond drilling. Experience working with boat-supported mapping programs or barge-drilling is considered an asset. Strong technical foundation with the ability to interpret geological data and support exploration decisions. Experience leading or supporting field teams, with a demonstrated ability to mentor others; Experience contributing to exploration programs, including planning, execution, or coordination of field activities; Solid working knowledge of core logging, GIS, and 3D modelling tools, with the ability to support others in their use; Valid Driver's License. Additional Information Schedule: 16 days on, 12 days off at our Hammond Reef project in Atikokan, ON. Travel allowance and accommodations are provided. In accordance with applicable legislation, the expected compensation includes base salary and potential bonus opportunity. Your individual pay will reflect your skills and experience while remaining competitive within the local market. CC-350697.title: Business Development Representative
CC-350697.description: Role Overview Want to work directly with global brands, run live events, and build real client relationships in your first year out of school? At PheedLoop, we build critical technology for the global events industry. From conferences and trade shows to hybrid and virtual experiences, our software powers high-impact events around the world. As one of Canada?s fastest-growing event technology companies, we design systems that simplify, automate, and monetize events ? including self-check-in hardware, smart badges, and a powerful SaaS platform. We move fast. We listen to customers. We build quickly. And we care deeply about delivering real results. If you're ambitious, love solving problems, and want a role where your work directly impacts clients and revenue, this is for you. This is a 100% in-person role at our Toronto office. Your Day-to-Day You will own real relationships, solve real problems, and drive measurable impact. Provide frontline technical support via email and phone. Lead onboarding sessions and platform walkthroughs for new customers. Conduct post-event debriefs and mid-contract consultations. Develop deep expertise in the PheedLoop platform. Collaborate with Sales and Product teams to improve the customer experience. Support clients during key event moments (including occasional evening or weekend support closer to event dates, with advance planning). Because we power live events, there may be increased activity near major client event dates - but workloads are planned in advance and balanced across the team. What You'll Gain Direct exposure to SaaS operations and client strategy. Real ownership early in your career. Experience working with global brands and large-scale events. Cross-functional collaboration with Sales, Engineering, and Leadership. A fast-paced environment that accelerates growth. Many team members begin in this role and grow into the following types of roles. If you're ambitious and want to unlock your potential quickly, you'll thrive here. What You'll Need to Succeed Recently graduated or are graduating soon! Strong written and verbal communication skills (English). High work ethic and positive, energetic attitude. Ability to work independently while collaborating with a team. Bachelor's degree. Good to have but not required - 1 year of experience in customer success, customer service, or account management. What Would Make You an All-Star Experience in the events industry (conferences, trade shows, etc.). Experience selling or expanding SaaS products. Experience working in a startup or small business environment. Bilingual proficiency (English and French). We're looking for ambitious, hard-working individuals who thrive in environments where they are expected to think critically, move quickly, and take ownership. We believe our new strategic plan, The Way Forward , will once again revolutionize the way we serve and support our community from coast to coast. Working with us means that you'll be part of an ambitious, diverse team that's committed to changing what it is to be blind today. Manage special projects/events as required. Ensure consistency, quality, accuracy and timeliness of all communications consistent with CNIB's brand. Maintain a working knowledge of significant developments and trends in Planned Giving, estates and philanthropy. Collaborate with colleagues from other departments (Finance, Marketing and Communications, Gift Management, Major Gifts) for team projects, data management, accurate processing of gifts tax receipts, and reports. Prepare customized proposals, agreements and gift scenarios involving cash, annuities, and other planned gift vehicle in order to meet the donors personal, estate and financial planning goals. Deals directly with professional advisors (legal, financial, etc) when called upon to assist in the creation of the planned gift or for tax receipting. Who you are: Education and Experience University degree or College diploma in business, marketing and communications, fundraising management Knowledge and Skill Requirements Minimum of 2-3 years of experience in a specific fundraising, preferably Planned Giving or direct mail position. Proficient in MS Office suite software applications including Teams and SharePoint Proficient in using a fundraising database (Sales Force/equivalent) Adhere to applicable privacy laws as well as CAGP, AFP and CNIB standards of discretion and confidentiality. Familiarity with the issues surrounding vision loss is an asset and a desire to be a passionate advocate for CNIB and those we serve. Able to handle and maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information. Superior interpersonal skills Professional attitude, results oriented, strategic, flexible and ability to function with limited supervision and adapts to fast paced environment. Ability to provide strategic solutions to complicated and difficulty problems utilising excellent analytical, problem definition and problem-solving skills. Excellent written and oral communication skills; demonstrated success in proposal and stewardship development Strong strategic critical thinking skills, with the ability to collect, analyze, interpret and evaluate information, and make recommendations. Proven time management, planning, coordinating and organization skills; proactive in initiating multiple projects on an ongoing basis. Excellent project management skills Strategic mindset and creative approaches to deepening relationships and driving results. Familiar with comprehensive Planned Giving functions and regulations, thorough understanding of Planned Giving, Planned Giving vehicles and tax implications. Personal or professional experience relating to blindness and sight loss is considered an asset. Personal or professional experience working with assistive technology and/or accessible environments is considered an asset. Perks We offer industry leading comprehensive and competitive Total Rewards packages and a wide range of perks, including: Flexible and hybrid working arrangements and schedules. Opportunities for professional development and growth, including internal inclusion, diversity equity and accessibility (IDEA) initiatives. Competitive paid time off inclusive of annual vacation entitlement, additional paid holidays, wellness days, and personal days. Group insurance benefits include dental, health and vision care. Employer-sponsored pension plan. Years of service awards and year-round rewards as part of our employee recognition program. Enticing internal employee referral program. Work Environment Willingness to work flexible hours. Occasional travel may be required. Be Part of Our Mission If this sounds like the role for you, please visit our website to submit an application. Be sure to include a resume, cover letter, and mention how you heard about this opportunity. Closing date: September 16, 2026 Please note that while we invite applications from all interested and qualified applicants, we are unable to follow-up with every applicant. Working Together for Change Our diversity is our strength ? we take pride in our inclusive workplace. We are committed to recruiting and selecting candidates through fair, transparent, and accessible practices. We strongly encourage applications from members of groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including but not limited to Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, people who are blind, partially sighted, or Deafblind, and those who identify as women and/or 2SLGBTQ+. CNIB is committed to accommodating applicants with disabilities and will work with applicants requesting accommodations at any stage of the hiring process. Learn more about our mission here .

CC-350851.description: Position Overview We are seeking 3 Project Geologists to support an active diamond drilling and field exploration programs at the Moss Gold Project . The role centres on detailed core logging, sample selection, and ongoing QA-QC, alongside daily verification of geological, geophysical, and geochemical data, drillsite supervision, and close coordination with drilling contractors, keeping the program advancing to high technical and safety standards while supporting the geological development of the property. Qualifications Bachelor's degree (B.Sc.) in Geology, Earth Sciences, or a related field. 3-8 years of exploration / core logging experience, ideally in gold or an Archean greenstone environment. Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices and environmental stewardship. Previous field experience would be considered an asset. Capable of lifting to 50 lbs. Familiarity with Leapfrog, Micromine or QGIS would be considered an asset. Willing and able to work camp-based rotation at site. Gold X2 offers competitive remuneration commensurate with qualifications and experience, together with travel to and from site and meals and accommodation while on camp rotation. CC-352252.title: Union Representative
CC-352252.description: SEIU Healthcare is a union of more than 67,000 members who are frontline healthcare workers in hospitals, long-term care facilities, and homecare agencies in communities throughout Ontario. We advocate with our members by launching progressive member driven programs, adapting best practices, and encouraging new and innovative ideas. We strive to create a society where workers are valued and rewarded for their work. As a result, thriving workers have a greater opportunity to participate and lead in building healthy communities. We provide a strong voice through collective bargaining, labour relations, and political action to ensure frontline workers are heard and respected when decisions about healthcare are being made. We are looking for individuals with a desire to amplify the voice of workers. If you are passionate about labour and social justice, share our values, and want to work toward changing the lives of workers, then a career with SEIU Healthcare is for you! For more information, visit www.seiuhealthcare.ca . POSITION DESCRIPTION : The Union Representative delivers excellent member service and is responsible for all aspects of labor relations and member engagement in the workplaces they represent. These duties include the effective administration of collective agreements, contract negotiations, grievances, and other matters related to the employment relationship between our members and their employers. The position is also responsible for identifying and coaching member leaders to become more active and capable members of the union and to support our member education and mobilization programs in support of our broader organizational strategy to strengthen a wider movement for social justice and political participation across our membership. This position is a full-time role based at our Mural office in Richmond Hill, Ontario . DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Plan, develop and execute initiatives to encourage member driven unit events, actions, and campaigns to resolve unit issues. Coach stewards to lead various meetings and support SEIU Healthcare in early identification and resolution of unit issues. Support organizational political strategies by recruiting member leaders and promoting and participating in political actions and events. Develop and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders (employers, members, internal departments, OLRB, arbitrators etc.). Facilitate and coordinate General Membership Meetings, Steward Meetings, Labour Management Meetings, Site Visits, and Departmental Meetings in assigned units. Lead collective bargaining for assigned units while working with the Research Department in accordance with established standards, procedures, and timelines. Manage the grievance process, working toward early resolution in accordance with individual collective agreements and internal processes. Analyze and interpret complex contracts and legislative language. Resolve issues within units through interpretation and enforcement of contracts and related legislation. Work in collaboration with administrative support to ensure unit files, unit events, negotiation files, records, reports, and grievance collateral are entered in UnionWare. Facilitate attendance management and return to work meetings in assigned units. Ensure timely submission and preparation of detailed files for interest and rights arbitrations. Ensure required committees in assigned units have SEIU representation. Complete and submit monthly unit status reports and monthly expense reports. Ensure legal and other billing accurately reflects events as they occur and are submitted per policy. Manage and record expenses made during regular business using a company credit card/gas card, in accordance with SEIU financial policies. Other duties as assigned. EDUCATION BACKGROUND At SEIU Healthcare, we understand that the best people do not always have the same access and opportunities to education, and while post-secondary education is always preferred, we want to make sure nothing stands in the way of finding the right person. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED Minimum of three (3) years labour relations experience, preferably in a labor union environment. Experience negotiating first and renewal collective agreements and administer those agreements through their life cycle. Experience handling and processing grievances through referral to arbitration Experience in the healthcare sector is an added advantage SKILLS & COMPETENCIES REQUIRED: Proficiency in languages other than English is an asset. IT skills is an asset Working knowledge of relevant legislation (ESA, OHRC, WSIA, OHSA, OLRA). Ability to interpret collective agreement language and apply to specific situations. Ability to negotiate first and renewal collective agreements and administer those agreements through their life cycle. Ability to process grievances through referral to arbitration Proficient with Microsoft Office and Union Ware Strong interpersonal skills, excellent writing, and verbal skills Strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Strong conflict resolution skills and the ability to deal with tense situations. Self-motivated and able to work independently with minimal supervision. Time management skills. Building and maintaining trust relationships with all stakeholders. OTHER REQUIREMENTS This position requires the successful candidate to have a valid driver's license. The successful candidate would have to provide proof that s/he has a valid driver's license upon being hired. PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ WORKING CONDITIONS / ENVIRONMENT Office work may involve prolonged periods of sitting at a workstation and repetitive movements associated with such tasks. Field work may involve extended periods away from home, long hours, and exposure to both physically and mentally demanding environments. Evening and weekend work may be required. Work hours will vary to meet operational needs. Prolonged use of a computer. Frequent use of the telephone. Driving, air travel, cross-border travel, and attendance at off-site meetings. Frequent long-distance travel by motor vehicle. Must be able to lift and transport boxes containing various materials to and from meetings. Exposure to medical, healthcare, and office environments How to Apply Written applications that detail your qualifications and experience should be submitted on our career portal . Salary and other terms and conditions are in accordance with the field staff collective agreement. Please note that the Employer reserves the right to transfer or assign staff anywhere within the SEIU Local 1 Canada jurisdiction. VACANCY DISCLOSURE This posting is to fill an existing vacancy within SEIU Healthcare. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DISCLOSURE Please note that SEIU Healthcare may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this position. WHY SEIU HEALTHCARE? At SEIU Healthcare, you will find a dynamic and inclusive environment where employees are valued and rewarded for their work. Here are a few things that set us apart: Inclusive workplace culture Excellent health, dental and insurance benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Generous vacation and sick leave benefits, inclusive supplemental unemployment benefits Fully sponsored employer pension plan Investment in employee growth ? personal and professional development options Working towards a common goal by making a real difference in the lives of people SEIU Healthcare thanks all applicants for their interest. We are committed to diversity in our workplace and encourage applications from all visible minority groups, women, Aboriginal persons, persons with disabilities among other self-identified diverse groups. We also provide accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (?AODA?). If you require accommodation for a disability during any stage of the recruitment process, please notify Human Resources. Please note that only individuals who are selected for interviews will be contacted.

clients in multiple time zones Strong commitment to inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility (IDEA) Ability to work in French and English (oral and written) would be an asset LOCATION KCI offers a flexible remote / hybrid work model. Our team is deployed across Canada and our head office is located in Toronto. This position will be based in the Greater Toronto Area, primarily working remotely from a private home office and on occasion from our Toronto Head Office (214 King Street West, Suite 402). FOR MORE INFORMATION We believe that people are catalysts and that organizations can only achieve their full potential with the right people on their team. This is true both for our clients and for KCI. The salary range for this position is in the range of $48,000 - $53,000 per annum, plus a comprehensive vacation and benefits package including: 3 weeks? vacation plus a winter break in December; group benefits plan; health & wellness program; donations matching program; and group RRSP. In addition, KCI is proud to have expanded ownership of the firm to all employees through an Employee Ownership Trust (EOT). Over time, this structure will allow employees to become beneficiaries of the future financial success of KCI. All inquiries and applications will be held in strict confidence. Interested candidates should send their resume and letter of interest to Julie Donovan, Manager, Search + Talent Operations at: ProjectCoordinator@kcitalent.com . Please note that we will be reviewing candidates on an ongoing basis, early submission is appreciated. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Artificial intelligence will not be used to screen resumes or assess candidates in this search. KCI is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, equitable, and accessible work environment. KCI will, upon the request of the applicant, provide accommodation during the recruitment process to ensure equal access to applicants with disabilities. If you are selected for an interview and you require accommodation, please inform us. ABOUT KCI The nature of the Canadian charitable sector has changed ? irreversibly. New ideas, new models, new technologies, new generations and new Canadians present opportunities and challenges for Canadian charities. Where do we go from here? At KCI, that?s our favourite question . We are Canada?s leading consultants to the non-profit sector with professionals across the country in fundraising, strategy development, research & analytics, and executive search. Our core purpose is to inspire and enable organizations to raise money, to make the dream of better communities and improved lives a reality. And through our 42 years of experience, we?ve helped thousands of organizations craft their strategies, build their teams, and raise billions of dollars. We serve our clients through a wide variety of services, including Fundraising Counsel & Campaigns; Assessments & Strategy Development; Research & Analytics; Communications & Case Development; and Executive Search & Talent Services. In doing that work, we firmly place our focus on values and people?both ours and our clients?. We are proudly and resolutely guided by our core values: the highest integrity in all our actions; commitment to excellence and innovation in everything we undertake; openness to new ideas; and collaborative and respectful relationships with our colleagues and our clients. We hire to these values and live them every day. These values are also deliberately reflected in our ownership structure at KCI. KCI is employee-owned through an Employee Ownership Trust, with ownership held on behalf of all our employees. For us, employee ownership is more than a structure. It is a natural extension of who we are and how we work: collaborative, accountable, values-driven and built for long-term impact. This also makes KCI unique. We are Canada?s only philanthropy and talent consulting firm whose ownership is held on behalf of all employees through an EOT. And as one of the first companies in Canada to transition to the new EOT model, KCI is proud to be helping define what broad-based employee ownership can look like in this country. At KCI, our people are our most valuable resource. We hire the best and brightest, provide them with ongoing training and support, and allow them to work with a range of clients in different regions and charitable sectors across the country. We strive to foster a collaborative culture of professional and personal growth and to recognize, value, and develop the individual skills and contributions of each of our team members. And because we know the future won?t look like the past, we hold capacity building, knowledge sharing, and insight creation at our core. We have made it our business to know What?s Next . For more information about KCI, please visit: https://kciphilanthropy.com/

CC-352266.title: HR & Office Administrator
CC-352266.description: About Rainbow Railroad Rainbow Railroad is an international nonprofit that helps at-risk LGBTQI+ get to safety. Our mission is to provide life-saving support for LGBTQI+ people experiencing discrimination, violence, and persecution based on their sexual orientation, gender identity, or sex characteristics (SOGIESC). We work at the intersection of LGBTQI+ identities and forced displacement as advocates, thought leaders, movement strategists, community organizers, and direct service providers. Since our founding in 2006, we have supported close to 40,000 at-risk LGBTQI+ people globally, built sustainable partnerships with hundreds of organizations and coalitions, and publicly engaged millions of people about the forced displacement crisis affecting the LGBTQI+ community. Rainbow Railroad is a registered charity in Canada and a 501(c)3 organization in the United States. About the Position Rainbow Railroad is seeking a highly organized, reliable, and detail-oriented HR & Office Administrator to keep our Toronto office running smoothly and to support a positive, engaged, and well-functioning workplace. This role is perfect for someone who takes pride in creating order and supporting others. Whether you?re an emerging HR professional eager to learn and grow, or an experienced administrator who values discretion, confidentiality, and efficiency, you?ll be the friendly face that keeps our office organized, our systems running, and our people connected. Working closely with the Operations and HR teams, you will handle day-to-day office management, coordinate logistics, support HR administration, and contribute to building staff morale and engagement. This is an on-site role at our downtown Toronto office. Key Responsibilities Office Administration Assist in managing day-to-day operations of Rainbow Railroad?s Toronto office, ensuring a welcoming, well-organized, and efficient environment Serve as the first point of contact for staff, visitors, and external inquiries (including monitoring our hire@ inbox), responding promptly and professionally Maintain office supplies, systems, and equipment; liaise with vendors for maintenance, custodial, and catering Coordinate staff gatherings, celebrations, and team-building moments that foster a positive and inclusive workplace culture. Track and process invoices, expenses, and purchase orders in accordance with established financial procedures. Maintain the HR and Administrative procedurals. Helping to refine internal office and HR systems and policies for efficiency and clarity. Provide administrative support to the Director, HR and Admin, the COO, and CEO as needed. Human Resources Administration Serve as the primary contact for general HR-related inquiries, maintaining confidentiality and discretion at all times. Support recruitment processes by scheduling interviews, preparing onboarding materials, and coordinating new hire orientation. Maintain and update HR records, contracts, and staff files with accuracy and attention to detail. Support the administration of benefits, leaves, and performance review cycles. Help organize staff training, engagement initiatives, and recognition activities to strengthen morale and organizational culture. Ensure HR and office policies are followed consistently and communicated clearly across the organization. CC-353409.title: Training and Education Coordinator
CC-353409.description: Organization: Luke?s Place Support & Resource Centre for Women & Children Position: Training and Education Coordinator Type: Full-Time Contract (12 months) ? Current Vacancy Hours: 35 hours/week Classification: Hybrid ? On Site 2 Days/Week, additional on-site as needed Location: 707 Simcoe Street South, Oshawa About Luke?s Place Luke?s Place is an award-winning non-profit centre of excellence in family law support for women who have been subjected to intimate partner violence as they navigate the family law system. We provide legal support services and summary legal services to over one thousand women and their children across Ontario every year. We work with academics to conduct research and collaborate widely to advocate for improved access to justice for women and their children. Our work is grounded in an intersectional feminist, trauma-informed, and anti-oppressive framework. Luke?s Place envisions a family law system that promotes healthy, safe families, living free from abuse, and the threat of abuse. Why Join Our Team? At Luke?s Place, you?ll be part of a collaborative and passionate team, engaging in meaningful work. To support our staff, we provide: A hybrid work environment Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and life insurance 15 vacation days per year to begin 15 paid health days per year Additional paid December wellness break and birthday day off Professional development opportunities Starting Salary range of $51,000 - $55,000 based on qualifications and experience About the Role The Training and Education Coordinator provides strong organizational and program support for Luke's Place training, resource development, and engagement activities. The position plays a key role in coordinating and supporting the development and delivery of virtual and in-person training for professionals who work with women and children subjected to intimate partner violence, as well as supporting the development and dissemination of related resources and programs. The position will also contribute to communications and engagement activities that promote Luke's Place training, resources, and expertise. Reporting to the Manager of Knowledge Mobilization, this position is ideal for someone with 1 ? 3 years of experience in project coordination who enjoys working across a variety of projects and thrives in a collaborative environment. This position requires a hybrid, on-site presence at our Oshawa office. If you are passionate about improving access to justice for women and their children, we look forward to hearing from you! Key Responsibilities Coordinate the planning, development and delivery of trainings, webinars, resources, and knowledge mobilization activities Engage and collaborate with staff, provincial and national partners, and other stakeholders to develop and promote programs, resources and events Coordinate and support the development and facilitation of Communities of Practice and other engagement activities Support the creation of presentations, visuals, templates, and other materials in alignment with Luke?s Place branding Update website and online content related to knowledge mobilization activities Develop promotional strategies to increase awareness and engagement across audiences Monitor basic website, email, and social media analytics Support program and communications reports and statistics, including evaluation, monitoring, and engagement metrics Requirements and Qualifications A diploma or degree in Humanities, Women and Gender Studies, Adult Education, or a related field One to three years of experience in project coordination, event management, community engagement, or a related role Experience creating PowerPoint slides and designing resources and other related digital content Experience coordinating webinars, events, and/or training sessions Proficiency with Microsoft 365, Canva, Zoom, and WordPress. Experience with Moodle is an asset Knowledgeable and confident using learning and content management systems Knowledge of technical accessibility issues and plain-language editing Commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and trauma-informed practice Experience in the violence against women or non-profit sector is considered an asset A satisfactory Criminal Record Check, including Vulnerable Sector Screening About You You?re an Excellent Communicator ? you communicate clearly and confidently with a range of audiences and know how to make information engaging and accessible You?re Detail-Oriented and Organized ? you are comfortable juggling multiple projects and pay close attention to the details needed to keep projects moving forward You?re Creative and Resourceful ? you think independently, find practical solutions, and adapt to challenges when managing projects, technology, and changing priorities Our Guiding Principles Our work is guided by the belief that: Women and their children have the right to safety, and the family law system should promote that safety Addressing violence against women requires an intersectional feminist approach Women?s lived experiences inform and shape our work Ending violence against women is a shared social responsibility Our direct service work informs our education, research, and systemic advocacy Application With its gender-responsive, anti-oppressive framework, Luke?s Place believes that diversity strengthens our ability to deliver services. We welcome and encourage applications from women, especially those belonging to equity-deserving groups. We use the term women to include all self-identified women, including two-spirited, non-binary, cisgender, or transgender women. We encourage you to apply even if you don?t meet every single qualification listed but read this job posting with excitement. We value lived experience, transferable skills, and an openness to learn. Priority will be given to candidates with experience related to Violence Against Women. Luke?s Place does not utilize artificial intelligence (AI) in its candidate screening, assessment or selection process. How to apply Interested candidates are invited to submit a letter of interest along with their resume in confidence to the attention of Samara Mascarenhas, Program Manager at careers@lukesplace.ca by September 16, 2026 .
