CC-342005.title: Analyst, Indigenous Affairs
CC-342005.description: Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC) Analyst, Indigenous Affairs Hiring Range: $70,000 - $80,000 on an annual basis. Placement within this range is based on relevant experience and internal equity. Position Context: This posting is for a current vacancy. Working Arrangement: Hybrid, Attendance at the office required 1 day per week, plus in person meetings and on-site for required events. Position Overview: Reporting to the Director of Policy and Programs, the Analyst, Indigenous Affairs leads the development and delivery of PDAC?s Indigenous Affairs Program, supporting collaboration and constructive relationships between the mineral exploration and development industry and Indigenous Peoples in Canada. Working at the intersection of mineral exploration, Indigenous relations and public policy, the Analyst researches and analyzes emerging issues, contributes to the development of industry policy positions and practical resources, and supports engagement with Indigenous organizations, government and other stakeholders. A significant component of the role involves working closely with PDAC?s Indigenous Affairs Committee. The Analyst coordinates and supports the Committee?s work, facilitates discussion on industry and policy issues, and helps advance projects and initiatives that support responsible mineral exploration and meaningful Indigenous participation in the sector. This position offers an opportunity to contribute to Indigenous affairs and mineral-sector issues at a national level while working with industry leaders, Indigenous organizations, government representatives and other stakeholders. Key Responsibilities: Committee Leadership The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and coordinating meetings of the Indigenous Affairs Committee, including supporting annual work planning, managing project deliverables, preparing materials, and ensuring appropriate follow-up. This includes facilitating effective discussion among committee members, supporting consensus on policy positions and strategies, and providing updates and recommendations on ongoing projects, regulatory matters, and Indigenous engagement initiatives. Research and Analysis The incumbent monitors, researches, and analyzes policy issues related to Indigenous relations, regulatory and policy issues affecting mineral exploration and development in Canada. This includes preparing briefing materials, reports, position papers, and other resources that support informed decision-making and advocacy. A key part is translating complex technical, regulatory, and policy information into clear, accessible materials for PDAC members and stakeholders. Advocacy and Policy Development This position supports the development of evidence-based policy positions by identifying research needs, managing related projects, and drafting submissions, letters, and communications to government and external stakeholders. This work focuses on issues affecting mineral exploration and development and the participation and interests of Indigenous Peoples. The role also contributes to external communications, including website content, press releases, and social media materials that support advocacy initiatives. Member Services This role provides guidance, tools, resources, workshops, and presentations to support PDAC members in Indigenous engagement. This includes helping members understand and respond to common industry issues, while encouraging collaborative problem-solving and the sharing of effective practices. Outreach and Partnerships In this capacity, the successful candidate will build and maintain relationships with national Indigenous organizations, government representatives, industry stakeholders, and other external partners. This includes representing PDAC at meetings, conferences, and workshops, as well as supporting partnerships and collaborative initiatives that strengthen PDAC?s network and advance the association?s goals. Project Management The incumbent will lead the development and delivery of the Indigenous Program at the PDAC Convention, including program planning, speaker coordination, event logistics, and budget oversight. It also leads the Indigenous Ambassador Program, including applicant coordination, mentorship and networking opportunities, and onsite execution. In addition, the role oversees committee-related projects and contributes to other PDAC events and initiatives as required. Organizational Support This position maintains accurate records and documentation for program activities, supports reporting and program evaluation, and provides input into budget planning for assigned program areas. This includes monitoring expenditures related to convention initiatives and supporting organizational communications, including content development for social media and other platforms. Qualifications Required: Bachelor?s degree in a relevant field (e.g., economics, geoscience, political science, or a related field) or an equivalent combination of education and experience. 2?3 years of relevant experience in mineral exploration or mining, Indigenous relations or engagement, natural resource policy, regulatory affairs, policy analysis or advocacy. Experience working within or directly supporting Canada?s mineral exploration and mining sector is strongly preferred. Knowledge of Indigenous engagement practices and relevant legal and regulatory frameworks in Canada, including the Crown?s Duty to Consult and the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP). Knowledge of land-related issues affecting mineral exploration and development, including land use planning, protected areas and conservation strategies. Experience working with First Nations, Inuit or Métis communities, organizations or Indigenous relations initiatives is a strong asset. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Outlook. Strong research and analytical skills, and an ability to synthesize key points from complex information. Excellent written, editorial, and oral communication skills. Demonstrated organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and produce high-quality deliverables. An effective problem solver that has an ability to navigate complex group dynamics with members from diverse backgrounds and viewpoints. Proven capabilities in developing professional networks and relationship-building. The successful candidate will be working in a hybrid work model, with the requirement to attend the PDAC office 1 day per week, as well as in person meetings and on-site for required events. The PDAC office is located at 170 University Avenue, Suite 800, Toronto, Ontario. Applicants are requested to submit a cover letter and resume to hiring@pdac.ca We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. PDAC does not use automated decision-making or artificial intelligence tools to screen or assess candidates for this role. PDAC is committed to fair and inclusive hiring practices and will provide accommodations, upon request, to support participation in all stages of the recruitment process.

CC-344390.description: Position Summary Reporting to the Facility Supervisor and Director of Operations, the successful candidate will assist in the operation, monitoring, maintenance, and optimization of CRWC?s water treatment and distribution systems. Key Responsibilities Assist in the operation and maintenance of a modern Class IV ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis water treatment facility. Operate and maintain a Class II regional water distribution system, including numerous remote pumping and storage facilities. Perform daily water quality testing and process monitoring to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and Canadian drinking water quality guidelines. Monitor and control system operations using SCADA and other computerized control systems. Collect, enter, analyze, and maintain operational and regulatory records. Participate in preventative maintenance activities and troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, and process equipment. Respond to operational issues, alarms, and emergency situations as required. Work independently and collaboratively as part of a professional operations team. Support CRWC?s commitment to safe, reliable, and efficient water service delivery. Qualifications Required Grade 12 diploma or GED equivalent. Valid Manitoba Class 5 Driver?s Licence. Reliable transportation and ability to travel regularly between facilities. Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills. Proficiency with computers and Microsoft Office applications. Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment. Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work at heights and in confined spaces. Preferred Water Treatment and/or Water Distribution certification. Experience in municipal water treatment or distribution operations. Experience operating ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis, or membrane treatment systems. Knowledge of SCADA systems and automated process controls. Experience with chemical handling and process chemical systems. Education in environmental science, water technology, mechanics, plumbing, instrumentation, or a related field. Candidates who are not currently certified but demonstrate a strong aptitude and interest in the water industry are encouraged to apply. The Cartier Regional Water Cooperative is committed to supporting the successful candidate in obtaining and advancing Manitoba Water and Wastewater Operator Certification through training, mentorship, and professional development opportunities. Work Schedule The successful candidate will participate in the current operations schedule, including: Weekend on-call rotation. After-hours alarm response requirements following the probationary period. Occasional emergency call-outs as required. Compensation & Benefits CRWC offers a competitive salary based on qualifications and experience, along with a comprehensive municipal benefits package including: Pension plan Extended health and dental coverage Life and disability insurance Professional development and certification opportunities

CC-347884.description: LMC Healthcare (LMC) is Canada?s largest specialist care provider in diabetes & endocrinology. We?re transforming diabetes care by making it more accessible, comprehensive, and patient-centric than ever before. LMC has 11 multi-disciplinary centers of excellence located in 2 provinces (Ontario and Alberta). Our 50+ Endocrinologists, many of whom are nationally renowned for their areas of expertise, are supported by an interdisciplinary team of highly qualified professionals. Currently, our team is looking for a Diabetes Educator - Registered Dietitian who can work with us on a permanent full-time basis at our Brampton location. Please note that this is a hybrid position based on clinic needs. Responsibilities Educate and advise patients on self-management skills in both individual and group settings focusing primarily on diabetes and secondarily on other health conditions such as general health & metabolic conditions (weight management & obesity). Develop a care plan for patients and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team, as needed. Complete detailed patient encounters within EMR system. Teach administration of insulin effectively, including titration and management, as per medical directives (for applicable patients). Teach self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) effectively for patients living with diabetes, as per medical directives. Perform patient follow ups in person or remotely (email, telephone, video). Obtain relevant health history of patients. Provide consultation as requested to community groups, partners, and team members. Training of additional staff and any new educators, as required. Effectively communicate with patients, families, caregivers, and healthcare professionals. Employ information technology appropriately for patient care (i.e., statistical tracking). Stay current and aware of opportunities to implement new, evidenced-based methods of patient assessment and treatment. Assist with research studies as needed including providing diet counseling for those patients enrolled in research studies. Teach evening virtual workshops, as required Complete a minimum of 2 community outreach events annually. Complete annual outreach calls. Assist with program implementation which includes reviewing patient charts, entering data, & following program guidelines. Responsible for administrative tasks (can be delegated to administrative staff/volunteers/interns as needed). These responsibilities include but are not limited to: rescheduling follow-up appointments, creating workshop folders, ordering supplies & medications, tracking patient visits, & entering data for programs. Participate in Journal Clubs & other group learning opportunities. Participate in disseminating the program vision. Participate and promote non-ministry funded LMC initiatives, including paid and non-paid services. What you?ll bring to the team A proven track record of being resourceful and finding solutions even when there is no clear path. Passionate to motivate and coach patients towards a healthier lifestyle. Adaptable to change and a willingness to take on new program initiatives to meet the growing needs of the program and LMC. Education/Experience A valid RD license in good standing with the College of Dietitians of Ontario Experience teaching/counseling individuals and groups of people. Must obtain or be working towards CDE designation. Must have a valid driver?s license in good standing and access to a personal vehicle. Experience in motivational interviewing and other evidence-based coaching techniques an asset. Health coaching experience is welcomed, or open to training as a health coach. Compensation range: The expected compensation for the position is $61K-$84K/annually. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including; health, dental, vision, pension, and vacation. Please submit your resume and cover letter, referencing the job posting number. This position is open until filled. The MMF requires a satisfactory criminal record check prior to commencement of employment. The MMF will accept existing criminal record checks if dated within 3 months of your start date. Obtaining this document is not a guarantee of employment. Preference will be given to qualified Red River Métis applicants and they are encouraged to self-identify on their cover letter. The MMF encourages internal applicants to apply for career opportunities within our Government. MMF Human Resources Department 300-150 Henry Ave, Winnipeg, Manitoba R3B 0J7 Email to: jobs@mmf.mb.ca Fax to (204) 947-1816

CC-347895.description: Vector Learning Co. | Remote + Monthly In-Person Content Session | Part-Time Vector Learning Co. is looking for an exceptional High School Math Tutor to join our growing team for the 2026?2027 school year. We provide personalized 1-on-1 tutoring for Ontario high school students, with a focus on helping students genuinely understand mathematics, strengthen their problem-solving skills, and feel confident approaching unfamiliar questions. We are looking for someone with a strong mathematics background who can do more than arrive at the correct answer. The ideal tutor can recognize why a student is struggling, explain concepts in multiple ways, and help students develop the skills and confidence to solve problems independently. Courses Applicants should be confident tutoring all of the following Ontario high school math courses: Grade 9 Mathematics (MTH1W) Grade 10 Mathematics (MPM2D, MFM2P) Functions (MCR3U) Advanced Functions (MHF4U) Calculus & Vectors (MCV4U) Mathematics of Data Management (MDM4U) Responsibilities 1-on-1 Tutoring Provide engaging, personalized online tutoring sessions to Ontario high school students Explain mathematical concepts clearly and accurately Help students with homework, assignments, test preparation and exam preparation Teach problem-solving strategies rather than simply providing answers Identify gaps in student understanding and adapt explanations accordingly Help students recognize patterns and make connections between mathematical concepts Arrive prepared and on time for all scheduled sessions Maintain a supportive, professional and encouraging learning environment Educational Content Creation Educational social media content is an important part of Vector Learning?s growth and student outreach. Tutors in this position will: Prepare and record 5 short-form educational math videos per month Participate in a scheduled monthly filming session, typically held on the first Friday of each month, unless otherwise agreed upon Create curriculum-relevant content such as mini-lessons, common mistakes, practice questions, problem-solving strategies and exam tips Be comfortable explaining mathematical concepts clearly and naturally on camera Prepare assigned topics and questions prior to filming Collaborate with Vector Learning on content ideas and educational accuracy Vector Learning will manage editing, branding, captions and publishing. Tutors are not required to post content on their personal social media accounts. Required content creation time is compensated. Qualifications We are looking for someone who: Has a strong academic background in mathematics, engineering, computer science, statistics, mathematics education or a related field Has excellent knowledge of Ontario high school mathematics and is confident teaching all courses listed above Is familiar with the Ontario Grade 9?12 mathematics curriculum Can explain difficult concepts in simple, intuitive ways Is patient, engaging and encouraging with students Can adapt explanations based on an individual student?s learning needs Has excellent verbal communication skills Is comfortable appearing on camera Is professional, organized and reliable Has a reliable internet connection and an appropriate environment for online tutoring Previous tutoring or teaching experience is strongly preferred. Familiarity with the Ontario Grade 9?12 mathematics curriculum is required. Availability Tutoring primarily takes place during after-school, evening and weekend hours . Applicants should be able to commit for the 2026?2027 academic year (September through June) and maintain reasonably consistent weekly availability. This is a part-time position with flexible scheduling based on tutor availability and student demand, with the opportunity to take on additional students as Vector Learning grows. Location Tutoring sessions are conducted remotely. Monthly educational content is filmed in person in the downtown Toronto area . Applicants must be able to attend the scheduled monthly filming session. Compensation $40/hour for 1-on-1 tutoring . Required training and monthly content creation are compensated separately. This is a part-time position, with opportunities for additional tutoring hours based on student demand and tutor availability. Application Process Selected candidates will complete: Application and resume review Short virtual interview Teaching demonstration using Ontario high school mathematics Short educational video/camera demonstration Reference check We?re looking for someone who is not only excellent at mathematics, but also excels at teaching it . If you love helping students and value flexible work, we?d love to hear from you.

The program prioritises individuals with international training in health, education, STEM, and trades, and includes a focus on women. Services include but are not limited to one-on-one employment counselling, group workshops, mentor matches and networking activities to connect job seekers with employers. The Program worker will coordinate with other related programs in the Organization to provide holistic support for newcomers. The program worker will seek out new and strengthen existing employers, mentors and other external stakeholder relationships to achieve program goals. Building and maintaining positive relationships with CultureLink colleagues to provide labour market assistance support to CultureLink clients is essential to program success. In-person work at one or more sites and itinerant service delivery at partner sites will be required. Maintaining positive relationships with partners and CultureLink colleagues is essential to program success. All agency staff are also expected to support each other and to collaborate on agency-wide initiatives. Duties Meet with clients to obtain information on their skills, experience, and education; identify their career goals and barriers to employment; and support them in developing a solution-focused employment action plan Provide continuous one-on-one coaching and employment counselling support throughout the client's job search process by assessing their progress, and providing appropriate support in securing and sustaining meaningful employment. Develop and deliver workshops on topics such as employability skills, job search strategies, résumés/cover letter design, Canadian workplace culture, and other related topics Connect with employers from regulatory bodies, industry experts, and employers to serve as guest speakers and support from clients in regulated professions. Work with clients to assist them in developing tools for job search success such as resumes, cover letters, job portal profiles, job search tracking and interview skills Provide information on employment including accreditation, licensing, business ownership/self-employment tailored to the interests of the client and make appropriate referrals to internal and external sources to minimize barriers and assist with progress in obtaining sustainable employment Host networking events to facilitate opportunities and platforms to connect with other professionals, employers and mentees to build networks and improve clients? knowledge of their professional areas of interest. Recruit and Match industry-specific mentors who can provide tailor-made guidance and coaching support to clients/mentees using matching support platforms such as TRIEC and other related avenues. Provide ongoing support and monitoring of the mentoring process to ensure client and program needs are met. Ongoing outreach and promotion activities Ongoing data capture reporting, maintenance of program statistics; and submission of summaries/reports as required Other duties as assigned Required Work Capacities Physical demands: sitting at a desk for computer work (at least 50% of the workday) and meetings; lifting files and supplies (up to 10 kg); working in an open office Non-physical demands: travel for off-site meetings and service delivery; evening work with advance notice; occasional deadlines; variety of tasks Social/emotional demands: teamwork; relationship/network-building; exposure to emotional/confrontational situations; working closely with the public, with clients and with colleagues Cognitive/mental demands: attention to detail; self-supervision/autonomy; multitasking; organizational ability/time management, adaptability, sound judgement, effective written communication Qualifications Post-secondary diploma or degree in a relevant field, preferably in career development, social work or adult education Minimum three years of community work experience, preferably in the employment sector in coaching, mentoring, counselling and/or delivering workshops Sensitivity and understanding of newcomer issues, specifically barriers to employment Ability to provide high-quality, client-focused services delivered in a positive, professional and compassionate manner Knowledge of the local labour market, community resources Vulnerable Sector Screening within the past six months (or availability to do so) Experience in group facilitation, coaching and presentation skills Proven experience using MS Office tools, data entry and reporting tools, social media platforms such as LinkedIn, and other online job search tools. CC-349431.title: Residential Support Worker (Relief)
CC-349431.description: POSITION INFORMATION Job Title: Residential Support Worker (Relief) Department: Community Residential Facilities (CRF) Reports To: Team Leader, Residential Services, or designate Classification: A (Subject to the Collective Agreement) Programs and Locations: Crossroads Program: 419 Jones Avenue, Toronto, Ontario Donald G. Evans Residence (DGER): 1669 Eglinton Avenue West, Toronto, Ontario Wage: $22.66 per hour, in accordance with the applicable collective agreement. Hourly premiums are also provided in accordance with the collective agreement. Security Clearance Requirement: The successful candidate must be eligible to obtain and maintain an Enhanced Reliability Status security clearance. The screening process requires verification of the candidate?s identity, employment, education, residence and other relevant history for at least the previous five years. Employment is conditional upon successfully obtaining and maintaining the required security clearance. Hours of Work This position operates within a 24-hour Community Residential Facility (CRF) environment. Relief employees are required to maintain flexibility and availability based on operational requirements. Relief staff may be scheduled to work: Day Shifts , Afternoon Shifts Overnight (Awake) Shifts Weekends Statutory Holidays Emergency call-in shifts & Short-notice replacement shifts Employees may be required to work at both Community Residential Facilities and may be assigned to either location based on operational requirements. Collective Agreement This position is governed by the Collective Agreement between the John Howard Society of Toronto and SEIU Healthcare. POSITION SUMMARY The Residential Support Worker provides residential supervision, client support, crisis intervention, case management assistance, and operational oversight within a federally funded Community Residential Facility operated by the John Howard Society of Toronto. The position supports federally sentenced individuals transitioning into the community under Correctional Service Canada supervision, including those on Day Parole, Full Parole, Statutory Release, Long-Term Supervision Orders, or other forms of community supervision. The role promotes public safety and successful reintegration by supporting residents with release-condition compliance, accountability, pro-social behaviour, risk reduction, and access to community resources. Staff must maintain a structured, safe, and professional environment while responding appropriately to complex mental health, substance use, trauma, behavioural, conflict, and emergency situations. Employees must exercise sound judgment, discretion, confidentiality, cultural competency, and professional boundaries while collaborating with CSC, Parole Officers, community agencies, emergency responders, and other stakeholders. They must comply with all organizational policies, contractual obligations, legal requirements, and ethical standards. PROGRAM OVERVIEW Community Residential Facilities The Crossroads Program and Donald G. Evans Residence are federally funded Community Residential Facilities (halfway houses) operating under contract with Correctional Service Canada. Both programs provide structured accommodation, supervision, programming, and reintegration support to federally sentenced individuals released into the community. The programs promote public safety, accountability, law-abiding behaviour, independent living skills, risk reduction, and successful completion of parole or community supervision. Residents must comply with their release conditions, house rules, case management plans, federal legislation, and CSC requirements. Residential Support Workers help maintain the safety, structure, accountability, and daily operation of the residences while providing guidance, support, and intervention consistent with evidence-based correctional practices. 3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES The Residential Support Worker is responsible for maintaining the safe, secure, and effective operation of a Community Residential Facility while providing professional support, supervision, and intervention to federally supervised individuals residing within the program. Duties include, but are not limited to, the following: A. Resident Supervision & Support The Residential Support Worker is responsible for providing continuous supervision and support to residents while maintaining a structured, safe, and accountable residential environment. Employees shall: ? Provide daily supervision of residents in accordance with organizational policies, Correctional Service Canada contractual requirements, and individualized case management plans. ? Maintain awareness of each resident's release conditions, supervision requirements, offence cycle, criminogenic needs, risk factors, behavioural expectations, and case management objectives. ? Monitor compliance with: o Parole Board of Canada conditions o House rules o Curfews o Sign-in/sign-out procedures o Temporary absences o Employment schedules o Programming attendance o Substance restrictions o Visitor procedures ? Verify resident whereabouts and ensure accountability throughout each shift. ? Monitor resident movement within and outside the residence. ? Observe behavioural changes and identify early indicators of deteriorating mental health, substance use, emotional distress, conflict, or escalating risk. ? Provide supportive interventions while maintaining professional boundaries. ? Encourage residents to demonstrate responsibility, accountability, and pro-social decision-making. ? Promote independent living skills through coaching, encouragement, and structured support. ? Maintain fairness, consistency, and objectivity when enforcing house rules and expectations. ? Build professional helping relationships while maintaining clear ethical and professional boundaries at all times. B. Community Reintegration Support Residential Support Workers assist residents with successfully transitioning from federal custody into the community. Employees shall: ? Promote accountability, positive behaviour, and successful community reintegration. ? Help residents establish healthy routines and achieve goals identified in their Correctional Plans. ? Encourage participation in employment, education, treatment, mental health and cultural programming, community services, and volunteer opportunities. ? Support the development of life skills, financial responsibility, time management, communication, problem-solving, and healthy coping strategies. ? Provide information and referrals to appropriate internal and community resources. ? Recognize individual strengths and barriers while promoting long-term stability, independence, and self-sufficiency. C. Case Management Support Residential Support Workers contribute to case management by documenting relevant observations and supporting interdisciplinary communication. Employees shall: ? Review resident files at the beginning of each shift. ? Remain familiar with residents? case management plans, community strategies, special conditions, risk factors, behavioural concerns, medical alerts, mental health needs, and relevant institutional history. ? Observe and accurately document resident progress and behavioural changes. ? Report significant information to Case Managers, Team Leaders, and Parole Officers, as directed. ? Participate in multidisciplinary discussions when requested. ? Encourage attendance at required appointments and correctional programming. ? Assist with appointment and transportation coordination, where applicable. D. House Operations & Residential Monitoring Residential Support Workers maintain the safety, security, cleanliness, and overall operation of the residence throughout each shift. Employees shall: ? Complete scheduled house, curfew, wellness, resident-count, room, building, perimeter, fire-safety, kitchen, common-area, office-security, and equipment checks. ? Monitor cleanliness and ensure residents follow housekeeping expectations. ? Identify safety hazards and promptly report maintenance concerns. ? Secure confidential information and ensure all entrances and exits remain secure. ? Monitor visitors and remain aware of everyone present in the residence. E. Safety, Security & Risk Management Residential Support Workers promote public safety and the safe operation of the residence. Employees shall: ? Maintain situational awareness, identify emerging concerns, and assess changing risk factors throughout each shift. ? Exercise sound judgment when responding to aggression, conflict, substance use, intoxication, mental health deterioration, self-harm concerns, security breaches, and resident absences. ? Conduct authorized room and house searches in accordance with organizational policies and procedures. ? Secure prohibited items and maintain chain-of-custody documentation, where applicable. ? Immediately report safety concerns and follow all applicable lone-worker procedures. ? Protect the safety of residents, visitors, staff, and the public. F. Crisis Intervention & Emergency Response Residential Support Workers must respond calmly, promptly, and professionally to emergencies, including medical incidents, suspected overdoses, fires, behavioural or mental health crises, suicidal ideation, missing residents, violence, security breaches, property damage, criminal activity, natural disasters, and utility failures. Employees shall: ? Conduct immediate risk assessments and use approved verbal de-escalation techniques as the primary intervention. ? Activate emergency procedures and contact emergency services and on-call management as required. ? Coordinate the response until assistance arrives and provide emergency responders with relevant information. ? Maintain resident accountability during evacuations. ? Complete all required documentation before the end of the shift. ? G. Documentation, Reporting & Record Keeping Residential Support Workers must maintain accurate, timely, objective, and professional records that meet organizational, contractual, legal, evidentiary, and Protected B requirements. Documentation may be reviewed or relied upon by CSC, the Parole Board of Canada, law enforcement, legal counsel, auditors, and the courts. Employees shall: ? Complete all required documentation within established timelines and before the end of each shift, unless otherwise directed. ? Accurately record resident interactions, observations, interventions, behavioural changes, and significant events using factual, non-judgmental language. ? Complete required logbook entries, case notes, shift summaries, incident or occurrence reports, database and medication records, emergency and search documentation, maintenance reports, and fire and safety inspection records. ? Follow approved documentation, correction, storage, and Protected B informationhandling procedures. ? Immediately report errors or omissions that could affect resident supervision or public safety. ? Ensure records are complete and capable of withstanding legal, contractual, audit, or investigative review. H. Medication Support Residential Support Workers provide medication support through prompting and observed selfadministration in accordance with organizational policies and applicable legislation. They do not diagnose conditions, prescribe medication, or modify treatment plans. Employees shall: ? Prompt and observe residents taking prescribed medications according to approved schedules. ? Maintain accurate medication records and immediately document and report refusals, missed doses, irregularities, or concerns. ? Secure medications in designated storage areas and protect the confidentiality of medical information. ? Follow applicable infection-prevention and control procedures. ? Respond appropriately to suspected overdoses or adverse medical events, including administering naloxone when trained and authorized. ? Complete all required medication-awareness and overdose-response training. I. Communication & Interagency Collaboration Residential Support Workers must communicate respectfully, promptly, and professionally with residents, colleagues, supervisors, and external partners. Employees shall: ? Promptly report significant resident and operational concerns to management. ? Share relevant observations with Case Managers to support case planning and intervention. ? Liaise professionally with CSC, Parole Officers, institutional staff, healthcare and emergency services, police, and community-based service providers. ? Participate in shift-change communication to maintain continuity of care and operational awareness. ? Follow established escalation procedures and communicate professionally during crises. ? Represent the John Howard Society of Toronto professionally in all interactions. J. Administrative & Operational Responsibilities Residential Support Workers are responsible for supporting the efficient daily operation of the residence while ensuring organizational standards are consistently maintained. Employees shall: ? Complete routine administrative tasks assigned during each shift. ? Maintain accurate filing systems. ? Perform photocopying, scanning, and data entry. ? Monitor office supplies and notify management of shortages. ? Assist with inventory management. ? Maintain organized workspaces. ? Ensure confidential documents are properly secured. ? Support program audits and accreditation activities. ? Assist with implementation of new policies and operational procedures. ? Participate in quality improvement initiatives. ? Report facility maintenance concerns promptly. ? Maintain familiarity with agency forms, databases, policies, and electronic documentation systems. ? Perform additional operational duties assigned by management that are consistent with the position. K. CC-349432.title: Bilingual Case Services Agent
CC-349432.description: Contract Opportunity Bilingual (English/French) Case Services Agent Accountable To: Director of Operations Contract Type: 1-year contract with the possibility of conversion to a permanent employee position. Background screening may be required as a condition of engagement. Schedule: 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET. These are fixed working hours. Work Arrangement: Home office within Canada, with occasional in-person meetings or training as required Compensation: $40,000-$65,000 Anticipated Start Date: September 2026 About CAMVAP CAMVAP is a cross-Canada program that consumers can use to resolve disputes with a manufacturer about defects in their vehicle?s assembly or materials, or how the manufacturer is applying or administering its new vehicle warranty. Disputes can be resolved through binding arbitration. About the Role CAMVAP is seeking a Bilingual Case Services Agent to support inquiry, intake, and case services functions. This is an opportunity to join a small national organization with a consumer, not-for-profit mandate. The immediate priority of this role is to strengthen CAMVAP?s front-end inquiry and intake support in response to increased public awareness and inquiry volume. This is a front-line program operations role. The scope of services may expand as proficiency is demonstrated. CAMVAP will provide training on its program, procedures and case management system. This role is intended for an experienced bilingual service professional who is comfortable managing a high volume of inquiries, detailed documentation and sensitive matters. What You Will Do Respond to phone, email and web inquiries in English and French in a timely, professional, and neutral manner. Explain CAMVAP?s eligibility requirements, process, forms, timelines, and next steps without providing legal advice or advocating for either party (consumer or manufacturer). Assist with intake by helping identify required information. Ensure completeness and accuracy of forms, documents, or communications. Maintain accurate notes, records, status updates, and follow-ups in CAMVAP?s case management system. Use approved templates, scripts, and procedures to support consistent national service delivery. Identify urgent, sensitive, or complaint-related matters and escalate them appropriately. Support routine case services tasks as training is completed, including file readiness, document tracking, status monitoring, and follow-up coordination. Communicate professionally with consumers, manufacturers, CAMVAP staff, and others as required. Help identify recurring questions, delays, or service issues that could improve CAMVAP?s process or public-facing materials. Minimum Requirements Demonstrated experience providing bilingual customer service, intake and administrative support. Ability to work independently following training. Professional written and verbal communication skills in both English and French Three or more years of experience in customer service. Strong organization, follow-up, and attention to detail. Ability to communicate calmly and clearly with people who may be frustrated, confused, or upset. Sound judgment and the ability to recognize when a matter should be escalated. Comfort using email, Microsoft Office, databases, case management systems, and virtual meeting tools. Ability to follow procedures, use templates, and apply standard processes consistently while identifying opportunities for improvement. Commitment to neutrality, confidentiality, professionalism, and respectful service. Experience supporting multiple stakeholders with different interests in a neutral service environment. Why Join CAMVAP CAMVAP offers an opportunity to: Contribute to a small, national, not-for-profit organization at an important stage of growth. Meaningfully support a fair, neutral, and accessible dispute resolution program for Canadian consumers. Develop broader case-services skills through training and hands-on experience in a national dispute resolution program. How to Apply Interested applicants are invited to submit a resume and cover letter to hr@camvap.ca by September 11, 2026. Accessibility and Accommodation CAMVAP is committed to an accessible and inclusive recruitment process. Accommodation is available upon request during the recruitment process and throughout the engagement in accordance with applicable accessibility and human rights requirements. Confidentiality The Bilingual Case Services Agent will have access to personal, confidential and sensitive information. The successful candidate must maintain confidentiality, protect personal information, and comply with CAMVAP?s privacy, confidentiality, information-security and case-handling requirements throughout the engagement. Offre de contrat Agent(e) bilingue aux services de dossiers (français/anglais) Relève de : Directrice des opérations Type de contrat : Contrat d?un an pouvant mener à un poste permanent. Une vérification des antécédents pourrait être exigée comme condition d?embauche. Horaire : 35 heures par semaine, du lundi au vendredi, de 8 h à 16 h (HE). Cet horaire de travail est fixe. Mode de travail : Télétravail à partir d?un bureau à domicile situé au Canada, avec des réunions ou des formations occasionnelles en personne, au besoin. Rémunération : De 40 000 $ à 65 000 $ Entrée en fonction prévue : Septembre 2026 À propos du PAVAC Le Programme d?arbitrage pour les véhicules automobiles du Canada (PAVAC) est un programme pancanadien auquel les consommateurs peuvent recourir pour régler un différend avec un fabricant concernant des défauts d?assemblage ou de matériaux de leur véhicule, ou encore la manière dont le fabricant applique ou administre la garantie sur les véhicules neufs. Les différends peuvent être réglés par arbitrage exécutoire. À propos du poste Le PAVAC est à la recherche d?une personne bilingue pour soutenir les fonctions liées aux demandes de renseignements, à l?admission et aux services de dossiers. Il s?agit d?une occasion de se joindre à un petit organisme national sans but lucratif dont le mandat est au service des consommateurs. La priorité immédiate de ce poste consiste à renforcer les services de première ligne du PAVAC en matière de renseignements et d?admission afin de répondre à la notoriété accrue du programme et à l?augmentation du volume de demandes. Il s?agit d?un poste de première ligne au sein des opérations du programme. L?étendue des responsabilités pourra augmenter à mesure que la personne acquerra les compétences nécessaires. Le PAVAC offrira une formation sur son programme, ses procédures et son système de gestion des dossiers. Ce poste s?adresse à une personne bilingue ayant de l?expérience en service à la clientèle et étant à l?aise avec un volume élevé de demandes, des documents détaillés et des situations délicates. Vos responsabilités Répondre aux demandes reçues par téléphone, par courriel et par le Web, en français et en anglais, avec diligence, professionnalisme et neutralité. Expliquer les critères d?admissibilité, le processus, les formulaires, les délais et les prochaines étapes du PAVAC, sans donner de conseils juridiques ni défendre les intérêts de l?une ou l?autre des parties (consommateur ou fabricant). Soutenir le processus d?admission en aidant à déterminer les renseignements nécessaires. Vérifier que les formulaires, les documents ou les communications sont complets et exacts. Consigner avec exactitude les notes, les dossiers, les mises à jour sur l?état des dossiers et les suivis dans le système de gestion des dossiers du PAVAC. Utiliser les modèles, les scripts et les procédures approuvés afin d?assurer une prestation uniforme des services à l?échelle nationale. Repérer les situations urgentes ou délicates, ainsi que les plaintes, et les acheminer aux personnes responsables. Accomplir des tâches courantes liées aux services de dossiers au fur et à mesure que la formation progresse, notamment vérifier que les dossiers sont prêts à être traités, assurer le suivi des documents, surveiller l?état des dossiers et coordonner les suivis. Communiquer de façon professionnelle avec les consommateurs, les fabricants, le personnel du PAVAC et toute autre personne concernée. Aider à cerner les questions récurrentes, les retards et les problèmes de service afin de contribuer à l?amélioration des processus ou des documents du PAVAC destinés au public. Exigences minimales Expérience démontrée en prestation de services à la clientèle bilingues, en admission et en soutien administratif. Capacité à travailler de façon autonome après la formation. Aptitudes professionnelles à communiquer oralement et par écrit, en français et en anglais. Au moins trois ans d?expérience en service à la clientèle. Grand sens de l?organisation et du suivi, ainsi qu?un souci du détail. Capacité à communiquer avec calme et clarté avec des personnes qui peuvent être frustrées, confuses ou contrariées. Bon jugement et capacité à reconnaître les situations qui doivent être acheminées aux personnes responsables. Aisance avec le courriel, Microsoft Office, les bases de données, les systèmes de gestion de dossiers et les outils de réunion virtuelle. Capacité à suivre des procédures, à utiliser des modèles et à appliquer des processus normalisés de façon uniforme, tout en repérant les possibilités d?amélioration. Engagement envers la neutralité, la confidentialité, le professionnalisme et un service respectueux. Expérience du soutien offert à plusieurs intervenants ayant des intérêts différents, dans un environnement de service neutre. Pourquoi vous joindre au PAVAC Le PAVAC offre l?occasion de : Contribuer à un petit organisme national sans but lucratif à une étape importante de sa croissance. Contribuer concrètement à un programme de règlement des différends équitable, neutre et accessible pour les consommateurs canadiens. Développer des compétences élargies en matière de services de dossiers grâce à la formation et à une expérience pratique au sein d?un programme national de règlement des différends. Comment postuler Les personnes intéressées sont invitées à faire parvenir leur curriculum vitæ et une lettre de présentation à hr@camvap.ca au plus tard le 11 septembre 2026. Accessibilité et mesures d?adaptation Le PAVAC s?engage à offrir un processus de recrutement accessible et inclusif. Des mesures d?adaptation sont offertes sur demande pendant le processus de recrutement et pendant toute la durée du contrat, conformément aux exigences applicables en matière d?accessibilité et de droits de la personne. Confidentialité La personne retenue aura accès à des renseignements personnels, confidentiels et sensibles. Elle devra préserver la confidentialité, protéger les renseignements personnels et respecter les exigences du PAVAC en matière de protection de la vie privée, de confidentialité, de sécurité de l?information et de traitement des dossiers pendant toute la durée du contrat.

CC-350592.description: Entry level | Training provided | Fully remote Good editors are hard to find. Not people who can write, people who can take a decent draft and make it clean, clear, and correct, every single time. At Upkeep Media, we help residential property management companies across North America grow through SEO, content marketing, video, and website optimization. Content is the engine, and the editor is the last set of eyes before anything reaches a client or their customers. Your mission: Make every piece of content we publish cleaner, clearer, and better performing than it arrived. What This Role Is, and Is Not This is not a content mill churning volume over quality. This is not a ghostwriting job. You edit and improve far more than you write from scratch. This is not a dead end. Editors who master the craft here grow into senior content and account roles. This is a precision role. You proofread, edit, format, and optimize blog posts, landing pages, and website copy, and you care whether every link points to the right place. What You Will Own Editing. Proofread and edit blog posts, website content, and landing pages. Improve grammar, clarity, structure, and readability while keeping each client's voice. Quality control. Check accuracy, consistency, formatting, and presentation. You are the reason errors do not ship. Publishing. Format content in WordPress, Grav, and similar platforms and make updates on live websites. SEO basics. Apply on-page fundamentals like titles, headers, meta descriptions, and internal links. We provide the training; you provide the attention to detail. Organization. Keep content files orderly in Google Drive and our project management tools, and communicate clearly with the marketing team. What Success Looks Like Within your first six months you will have: A clean editing record: content shipping on schedule with errors caught before publish Comfortable command of our style guidelines and client voices Real on-page SEO skills applied on live sites, not just theory The trust of the team, because your name on a piece means it is done What You Bring Strong English writing and editing skills High attention to detail and accuracy Organization across multiple projects and deadlines The ability to learn quickly and follow established guidelines Genuine interest in SEO, content marketing, or digital marketing Reliability: independent, punctual, and clear in a remote team Modern editing and analysis tools in your workflow are a plus, as long as you still catch what they miss No agency experience required. We train you in SEO and digital marketing. The Reality Check This role is not for someone who: Skims. The details are the job Wants to write essays instead of improving drafts Treats a checklist as optional Needs constant supervision to hit a deadline What You Will Get Training. Structured onboarding plus real training in SEO and digital marketing. Growth. A supportive team, a growing company, and a genuine opportunity for increased responsibility and compensation. Compensation. C$18 to C$20 per hour to start. Flexible Work. 100 percent remote, 40 hours per week between 9 and 5 EST. Ready to Pick Up the Pen? CC-350860.title: Performance Measurement Analyst
CC-350860.description: Position Overview The Performance Measures Analyst supports the Branch Management Team with operational processes required for the Branch's overall effectiveness and efficiency for ongoing operational performance in accordance with MNO's strategic goals. This position will provide support to branches and regions responsible for the management of the budgets to ensure the contract objectives are met as it relates to performance measurements, quality control and reporting. The Performance Measures Analyst will monitor program financials, program administrative data, and reporting consistent with the funder expectations and MNO standards. This position will work directly with the Branch Director and management team to identify and mitigate performance risk, identify service and spending trends, and create plans to adapt, as necessary, to protect the interest of the MNO and its programs and best utilize its funding. In addition, this position is accountable for the management of key stakeholder files and invoices. What you will be doing Support the definition and oversight of performance measures and/or accountability frameworks to ensure the funding directives are met in accordance with funding agreements and MNO standards. Contribute to project planning, budgeting and forecasting in compliance with funding contracts, and overall Branch operational plans. Analyze key funding activities and interpret the program data and financial spending to identify trends and make recommendations for future services, programs, and systems improvements. Generate comprehensive reports using program qualitative and quantitative data for both internals and external use. Complete program evaluation with the support of the Management and provide recommendations for improvement and/or insights to optimize performance. Participate in the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures. Maintain accurate records, including financial, contracts deliverables, reporting, and adhere to funding deadlines. Provide operational support such as liaising with stakeholders, setting up service agreements, tracking timelines, etc. Maintain project contracts and financials, ensuring complete and proper backup/audit documentation. Analyse, manage and assist in the coordination and delivery complex multifaceted special projects or events within the Branch. Assist with managing/monitoring special project budget(s) including the creation and maintenance of financial spreadsheets. Assist with the creation and implementation of onboarding materials for new hires. Provide support to the Director and Program Managers as needed. Promotes the values of the organization within the workplace and in the community by demonstrating positive and professional relationships with others (employees, citizens, council, volunteers, advocates, etc.) Reports all unsafe conditions, hazards or practices, accidents and incidents in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act and adheres to all Health and Safety requirements within the MNO's policies and procedures and provincial legislation. Performs other job/branch-related duties as required. Qualifications Education: University Degree or certification in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience. A post-secondary degree, certification or courses in business, accounting or statistics. Experience: 3 to 5 years of experience in monitoring, tracking, and reporting on financial performance measures. Knowledge: Extensive knowledge of budget creation, analysis, and forecasting. General knowledge of fund accounting. Knowledge of performance measures, financial modelling, and data analysis methods. Demonstrated analytical and evaluative skills to assess compliance and accountability. Demonstrated analytical, research and problem-solving skills to identify, analyze and recommend solutions to complex or contentious program issues. Strong skills in Microsoft Suite - particularly Excel. Strong communication skills - verbal and written. Strong desire to act in the service of the Métis Citizens, to advance and uphold rights and culture. A high degree of technology literacy and proficiency in MS Office applications and standard office equipment. Advanced communication skills, both written and verbal. Superior organization skills and time/priority management, managing others, including the design and implementation of project work plans. Elevated levels of problem-solving and analytical skills. Demonstrated ability to motivate, lead and work effectively with others in a supervisory capacity. Demonstrated understanding of policies, processes, practices, and documentation used to deliver program services or the Branch mandate. Asset Previous 5-7 years or more experience in a similar/comparable role. What We Can Offer You 4% Vacation pay Pension plan Annual paid two-week holiday closure in December 16 paid public and employer holidays 15 paid health & wellness days Challenging, multi-disciplinary work environment that fosters learning and professional development Substantial educational incentive to promote personal and professional growth An opportunity to make a direct or indirect impact on the lives of the Métis Peoples across the Province Other perks Employee Assistance Plan Telemedicine plan Goodlife corporate membership discount Bell Mobility's exclusive partner program Staple's corporate discount Dell member purchase program Mark's corporate discount

CC-351704.title: Site Porter (Part Time)
CC-351704.description: Evergreen is seeking a part time Site Porter to join our team. We are a national non-profit transforming public spaces in our cities for the health of people and our planet. With over 30 years of championing urban sustainability, we see the potential of our cities to solve some of the biggest issues facing our time and believe that our public spaces are the key to unlocking it. We see beyond the spaces that exist today and imagine them transformed into places where people and nature thrive. The Evergreen Brick Works site, where our head office is located, is built on the sovereign territory and waterways of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat, and Anishinaabe Nations. These nations continue to be the original governments, continuing leaders and decision makers that govern these lands.?The territory is governed by Treaty 13 signed by the Mississaugas of the Credit. Treaties remind everyone of our mutual responsibilities to these Nations and the many First Nations, Métis, and Inuit who call this land home.? Why Evergreen? In staff engagement surveys, Evergreen employees consistently report that their colleagues are one of the best things about working here. What else is in it for you? Access to mental health resources for all staff. Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that support staff who are Indigenous, racialized, or 2SLGBTQ+, as well as ERGs for allyship learning, and to support caregivers of all kinds. Active workplace committees, including Health & Safety, IDEA, and Employee Engagement. Access to informal and formal skills development and resume building opportunities. A beautiful head office location surrounded by nature at Evergreen Brick Works, with a free shuttle bus from Broadview Station. Key Accountabilities A day-in-the-life of this role might include: Ensuring the facility and site are ready for guests, staff & tenants each day. Reviewing and completing daily entries into logs as required. Executing all housekeeping tasks including, but not limited to, dusting, sweeping, mopping, garbage collection, cleaning of washrooms, monitoring and restocking inventory, operation of housekeeping equipment. Daily cleaning and sanitizing of all bathroom facilities, including toilets, sinks, showers, and mirrors along with restocking soaps, toilet tissue and paper towels. Dusting work areas, woodwork, furniture, and other equipment. Emptying garbage, organic and recycling bins and transport to the designated area. Cleaning common area walls, partitions, light switches, doors, and windowsills, etc. Cleaning movable and stationary furnishings and fixtures: dust, spot clean or wash, disinfect, when necessary, polish where required. CC-351706.description: RESIDENTIAL SUPPORT WORKER (RSW) Female (Relying of provisions of Section 24 (1)(a) of the Ontario Human Rights Code) Start Date: Immediately Posted Until: When position is filled Reports to: Director of Shelter Operations ? Oshki Kizis Lodge Under the Accessibility of Ontario and Disability Act (AODA), Minwaashin Lodge is committed to fostering an equitable, accessible, and inclusive workplace. SUMMARY: Minwaashin Lodge - Indigenous Women?s Support Centre is a non-profit charitable agency serving First Nations, Métis, and Inuit women, youth, and children. We are a multi-service agency committed to the healing and wellness of our community, through our programs and services at Minwaashin Lodge and our shelter, Oshki Kizis Lodge. We provide culturally specific programming for children, youth, women, and families. The RSW relief staff report to the Director of Shelter Operations and provides support to the Assistant of the Director. She is responsible for ensuring culturally appropriate, safe space for women and children in the shelter. She is also responsible for ensuring the 24-hours crisis line in maintained in an efficient and helpful manner. This is a physically demanding position requiring the ability to climb three flights of stairs easily and to carry a minimum of 12 kilograms. RESPONSIBILITIES: Answers to the Crisis Line and provides support and crisis intervention to callers. Responsible for additional administrative duties as assigned. Creates and maintains a safe, welcoming environment for women and children. Supports women and children in acquire safe accommodations. Creates and maintains an environment that provides for the emotional and practical support to women and children who have experienced violence. Responds to crises in a professional manner and follows the Policies and Procedure of Minwaashin Lodge and Oshki Kizis Lodge Assists women to find alternate housing when Oshki Kizis is at capacity. Monitors house security system and controls access to the house Supports residents in communal living expectations Assists in programming and services that honour the cultural needs of residents. Maintains daily log and provides comprehensive information for shift change staff. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum of Post Secondary Diploma Experience working in a women?s shelter. Good knowledge of traditional Indigenous healing practices Knowledge of the direct and intergenerational impacts of oppression, colonization and the residential school system. Knowledge of the effects of trauma A commitment to working in an environment that recognizes the diverse needs and gifts of women and children. Ability to actively listen, be empathetic and the ability to empower and support women. Ability to work in a fast paced, time-sensitive, and confidential environment. Must be energetic, creative, resourceful and committed to working as a team member. A commitment to working in an environment that is non-violent, anti-racist, anti- oppressive and values all women. Must be able to climb 3 flights of stairs easily and carry a minimum of 12 kilograms. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: Current Criminal Records Check First Aid/CPR Certification Excellent verbal and written communication skills Excellent computer and spreadsheet skills ADDITIONAL PREFERENCES: First Nations, Inuit, Mètis or non-status applicants will be given preference. CC-351729.description: MANITOBA MÉTIS FEDERATION CHILD CARE ASSISTANT ? INCLUSION SUPPORT PROGRAM September 3, 2026 Posting #26-14-008 The Manitoba Métis Federation (MMF) is the democratically elected National Government of the Red River Métis, also known as the Manitoba Métis. The Red River Métis are a distinct Indigenous Nation and People, and Canada's Negotiating Partners in Confederation and the Founders of the Province of Manitoba. The MMF seeks to fill one full-time Child Care Assistant position within our Michif Children?s Place Childcare Centre located at 525 Main St South in Dauphin, MB . We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, pension, and vacation. The MMF encourages internal applicants to apply for career opportunities within our Government. 114323.description: Plusieurs postes occasionnels Postes syndiqués Le conseiller ou la conseillère en gestion du sevrage résidentiel est responsable de fournir des services non médicaux de gestion du sevrage à l'alcool et aux drogues aux clients du Centre de gestion du sevrage d'Ottawa (CGSO). Les services sont offerts à des personnes qui sont soit sous l'influence d'une substance ou ayant des symptômes de sevrage ou à des personnes qui passent à travers une période de crise les mettant à haut risque de rechute. Les soins cliniques offerts aux clients pendant leur séjour comprennent le dépistage initial, une évaluation, du suivi, des soins physiques ainsi que l'élaboration et la documentation d'un plan de soins et d'un plan de congé en collaboration avec le client. Le conseiller anime aussi des séances de counseling individuel ou de groupe et offre un soutien aux clients et aux membres de leur famille. Les services sont offerts en conformité avec les objectifs et les politiques du CGSO ainsi que les standards de gestion du sevrage de l'Ontario et du ministère de la Santé et des Soins de longue durée. Les candidats intéressés doivent être disponibles pour travailler des quarts de travail de jour, de soir et de nuit incluant les fins de semaines.

besoins physiques, mentaux et émotionnels des clients, en lien avec le sevrage à l'alcool et aux drogues Bonne connaissance des services de santé mentale, de toxicomanie, de soutien communautaire et des partenaires du secteur local de la région de Champlain Excellentes habiletés de communication orale et écrite, de niveau supérieur en français et en anglais Communication efficace axée sur le client Flexibilité et approche basée sur les besoins des clients Formation en intervention non-violente en situation de crise (INVSC), formation appliquée en techniques d'intervention face au suicide (ASIST/FATIS), formation RCR, entrevue motivationnelle, gestion des troubles concomitants, sont des atouts Preuve de vaccination complète contre la COVID-19 et l'hépatites B (obligatoire) CE QUE NOUS POUVONS VOUS OFFRIR : Salaire entre 28,60 $/h et 31,93 $/h Fonds de pension HOOP Pourcentage de salaire en lieu de bénéfices et vacances payées Opportunités de formation continue Programme d'aide aux employé(e)s et à la famille (PAESF) Milieu de travail francophone Faire partie d'une équipe multidisciplinaire et dynamique composée de professionnels d'expérience en toxicomanie et en santé mentale au sein d'une organisation en pleine croissance

115207.title: Junior HSE Advisor
115207.description: JUNIOR HSE ADVISOR At Platecon Projects Limited, safety is not only a core value, it is embedded in every action, program, plan, meeting and interaction we undertake. Our employees face challenging working environments every day and our commitment is to ensure everyone returns home safely, without incident. Platecon's health and safety program continues to evolve and improve every year, leading the way in the industry. We are now seeking an experienced, dedicated and passionate Junior HSE Advisor to join our innovative and dynamic team and continue to build on the success of our safety program. The Junior HSE Advisor will develop, implement, and maintain safety programs and procedures. You will work in cooperation with management, field employees and the Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committees/OHS Worker Representative to ensure our corporate, project and regulatory HSE commitments are met. Joining the team will not only provide challenging and rewarding work experiences, but also the opportunity to develop your career and contribute to a culture that values integrity, people, quality, community, and safety. Responsibilities: ? The role involves actively promoting awareness of the Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) program while fostering a proactive and positive safety culture across all levels of the organization. A key responsibility includes facilitating workplace safety and environmental inspections, such as Job Safety Analysis (JSA), Job Hazard Analysis (JHA), Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Toolbox Talks, and Safe Work Observations across all projects. This includes tracking corrective actions and maintaining thorough documentation. ?? The candidate will be responsible for coordinating safety meetings for both office and field staff, supporting management and supervisors in ensuring that all tasks are completed in compliance with corporate and project-specific HSE requirements. Conducting new hire safety orientations and performing regular inspections of personal protective equipment (PPE), lifting equipment, and other safety-related tools will be an integral part of the job. ? Ensuring that follow-up actions from inspections, audits, and investigations are documented and completed is essential. The role also includes participating in loss prevention initiatives and routinely observing on-site tasks to ensure adherence to all HSE standards. The candidate will assist with internal and external audits, including regulatory and COR® audits, and help identify HSE training needs, scheduling appropriate safety training for all staff. ?Additional duties include supporting the collection, tracking, and analysis of HSE performance indicators, as well as preparing and presenting detailed reports. The Junior HSE Advisor will participate in incident investigations, providing thorough analysis and documentation of findings. Completing HSE task logs and effectively communicating lessons learned from both internal and external investigations to staff are also important aspects of the role. Professional Experience and Qualifications: The successful candidate must have an HSE specific post-secondary degree/diploma or an equivalent level of education. Preference will be given to those with certified safety accreditations such as NCSO or CRSP, or progress towards. A strong knowledge of the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and its Regulations, the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) Act and regulations, as well as safety regulations relevant to Ontario construction, is essential. The candidate must be able to identify critical safety risks associated with tank construction, including hazards related to rigging, working at heights, hot work, and confined space entry. Proficiency in Microsoft Office software is required, and the ideal candidate will demonstrate excellent organizational skills and the ability to work well under pressure, managing multiple tasks and meeting deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, are necessary, along with well-developed presentation and public speaking abilities. Platecon Projects Limited, a RothLochston company, specializes in the design, construction, and repair of platework structures such as oil storage tanks, process vessels and stacks. Our services include engineering design, production of drawings, material procurement and field installation. Our dedicated team is committed to delivering high quality solutions for our clients while ensuring a safe and productive work environment for our people. For more information, please visit https://platecon.com/. ; If you are ready to join a collaborative and detail-oriented team, we want to hear from you. If you have any questions, please reach out to Alison Trimm at atrimm@rothlochston.com . Platecon Projects Limited is an equal opportunity employer seeking qualified candidates who will contribute to the diversification of our views and ideas.

Whether you're a recent graduate looking to launch your career or an experienced animal care professional seeking your next opportunity, we'll provide the training, support, and career development you need to succeed. Record study observations and data, including body weight, food consumption, and clinical signs. Handle animals safely and compassionately. Maintain clean and compliant animal housing environments. Contribute to critical pre-clinical research that advances human and animal health.
